covenants.name: Durenmar
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
The Black Fir near the Great Library is the King of the Black Mountain's slow revenge: planted at the Aegis's edge over a century ago after his direct attacks failed, it was taken inside the Aegis when the magi found its cones gave vis, and so breached their own defence. It creeps about six inches a year toward the Tower of Bonisagus; what happens when it reaches the tower or the vine is unknown but likely severe. The magi think it immemorial.
Murion sends her raven familiar Kolkrabus to spy on Dankmar and others she counts enemies, against the Code.
Vis donations are quietly accepted in place of a contribution to the library and prop up the dwindling vis income; this is never admitted.
Occultes knows the restricted texts and has copied or moved the most interesting into his own sanctum, passing them to allies whose research they suit.
Petrus Virilis means to invent a longevity ritual that would probably leave him infertile; Murion would be furious.
The Fane of the Founders is an artifact into which the Cult of Mercury bound much of the Black Forest's original magical essence (treated as Magic Might 60); if Durenmar fell and the rite lapsed, the King of the Black Mountain hopes to seize that spirit.
covenants.summary:
Domus magna of House Bonisagus and the oldest covenant in the Order, Durenmar fills a hidden, steep-sided valley some fifteen miles inside the northern Black Forest, about fifteen miles south of Hirsau monastery, with Baden to the north-west. Here Bonisagus settled at a ruined Roman temple around 754, here the Order was founded and its first Tribunal held in 767, and here the Rhine Tribunal and the Grand Tribunal still meet, on the Tribunal Field by the Forum of Hermes. The Tower of Bonisagus holds the Great Library, the largest Hermetic collection anywhere, and most Bonisagus magi visit at least once in their lives.

The covenant thinks of itself as the political and traditional heart of the Order and is still greatly respected through its House, but its power is quietly ebbing both in the Rhine and beyond it. Its magi look inward, absorbed in research while the fabric of the place crumbles: an Autumn covenant forever on the edge of Winter, a place of quiet study rather than intrigue, while Fengheld has grown into the Tribunal's largest and arguably strongest covenant. The decline is traced to the Schism War, the failure of House Bonisagus's diplomacy and the exile of the Hercynian lineage whose Waldherz chapter had kept peace with the forest fay; since then Durenmar has been ignorant of the faerie woods about it, and no peace was ever made.

Murion's faction, which now leads, holds that Hermetic theory is to be kept pure of inferior hedge magic and is intolerant of hedge wizards and outsiders; the library's texts on such things are locked away for House elders alone. Critics say this deepens the stagnation and that Murion directs research instead of guiding it; an outward-looking minority gathered round Occultes wants exotic techniques brought in. A Magic aura of 7 lies over the clearing, defended by an Aegis of the Hearth of very high magnitude, devised after the faerie raid of 1085. The clearing is split by a stream and has no walls; the magi's sancta stand on the south bank, forbidden to all but a few trusted servants, and magic items heat, light and clean the towers and carry up the meals. A hidden guard post down the valley conceals the three-mile track in, and unexplored caves run under the north cliffs.

The covenant is led by the Prima of House Bonisagus, who holds the sigil of Bonisagus and is thereby Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal. Its offices are the Colens Arcanorum (the librarian), the Tenens Occultorum, and two honorary posts the Primus fills by invitation: the Protector, traditionally a Flambeau master or archmage who sees to the covenant's defence, and the Artificer, traditionally a Verditius who crafts items for its glory. A Guernicus is always in residence, a Gifted Mercere oversees the Mercer House in the basement of the Tower of Trianoma, and at least one guest magus from every gild is kept in residence. Retired former members may still vote by proxy sigil at covenant meetings. There are no chapter houses at present. Three towers dominate the clearing: the Tower of Bonisagus, enchanted against all decay of its books and wound about by a huge ancient magical vine said to be Merinita's gift; the Tower of Notatus, conjured by the first Primus, which houses most of the Bonisagus magi, Murion's sanctum on its top two floors and two excellent shared labs in its basement; and the shorter, crooked Tower of Trianoma, its top two floors lost to a forgotten accident, home to the Trianoma lineage and the non-Bonisagus members. Lesser buildings include the mill and guard tower where the turb greets visitors and rings a bell for a magus, the standing stone of Notatus where guests are welcomed and given their Aegis token, Verditius' Forge half-buried under a grassy bank, the Protector's Watchtower on the cliffs amid blasted ground, the overgrown ruin called Seneca's Folly, and a hunters' lodge at the top of the clearing.

Up to six peregrinatores lodge here at a time, from a long waiting list; magi accept almost any terms for access to the library, and a guest is usually asked to give two seasons of gild training to a Rhine apprentice, while the Bonisagus members share out the extra season of training owed to every Rhine apprentice. The covenfolk are quiet and peculiar, keep to themselves and have little to do with the magi; born in the aura, all carry Warping and live unusually long, and remnants of an old nature cult linger in their beliefs, with no church. A small band of expert huntsmen forays into the woods for vis and game. Redcaps run south to the Greater Alps and to Harco by the Rorschach chapter on Lake Constance, the Copper Rooster inn at Basel and the friendly covenant Sinews of Knowledge, or directly by the Mercere Portal to Harco.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: Intellego from the golden-green sap of the great vine on the Tower of Bonisagus (amount not given)
Vis: Perdo from the pine cones of the Black Fir, gathered yearly (amount not given)
Vis: Vim from Petrus Virilis's seed
Vis: several kinds cultivated among the exotic plants of Ricardus Caespuus's glass Herbam laboratory
Vis: the hot springs of upper Baden (Magic 2), which Durenmar owns Hermetically
Vis: the huntsmen's forays into the nearby woods
Income: lab rental, 5 or more pawns a season for a shared basement lab in the Tower of Notatus, 2 pawns for a guest lab across the river
Income: dwindling; barred from faerie sites since 1151, and several magical sites were lost to Zaehringen settlement in the early 12th century
Mundane: Durenmar ignores mundane politics; Hirsau monastery, fifteen miles north, spreads rumours of a hidden city of sorcerers
Mundane: speculation that Durenmar patronised, or withered, the Zaehringens of Baden is thought unlikely
Tension: Dankmar is the old enemy; in 1081 Durenmar accused it of league with the fay and lost, in 1151 Dankmar had Durenmar fined a rook of vis to every covenant and barred from faerie sites for fourteen years
Tension: the 1085 raid of the King of the Black Mountain killed or carried off several Bonisagus magi and many covenfolk; none came back
Tension: Murion's purists against Occultes's inclusive faction, which a sizeable minority of the House would rather see as Primus
Tension: Fengheld and its allies oppose Philippus Niger at every turn; the Ash Gild's war on the Norse wizards has Murion's quiet favour
Tension: no research breakthrough in decades, promising magi leaving, elders lost to age and Final Twilight
Tension: Petrus Virilis's programme of Gifted children, and the young magae writing to him
Tension: the Fane of the Founders, where twelve magi renew the Founders' vows every seventh year during the Tribunal; most Durenmar magi know of it, none has found it
Hook: the library is unhelpful about exotic and non-Hermetic lore; obscure lab notes and old books hint at forgotten artifacts; magi from distant Tribunals pass through

covenants.name: Dankmar
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
The book suspects but never states Dankmar's hand in the destruction of St Georgen, whose monks were found hanging dead in strange dark vines.
covenants.summary:
A small Winter covenant in the dampest, darkest part of the Black Forest, about forty miles south-west of Durenmar and a few miles south of the Black Forest Road, founded in 1052 by Aschlaranda, cast out of Durenmar and House Bonisagus, with her apprentice Schadrit, and named in mockery of the Order's birthplace to oppose Durenmar in all things. The firs grow so thick that it is dusk at noon; only fungi live on the poisoned carpet of needles and only ravens call.

A round palisade of split logs encloses wooden huts and four two-storey stone towers, the sancta of its four magae, which run down into linked caves reached only through the towers. Fir and yew lean over the walls and every wooden thing glows day and night with phosphorescent bracket fungi. The Faerie aura is 5, and Orphedra's version of the Shrouded Glen (level 40, Penetration 20, with her darkness sigil) hides the place for at least a mile, turning travellers away in nameless dread; those whose Magic Resistance holds feel nothing. Ancient Schadrit broods at the centre and her descendants do her bidding.

Dankmar keeps a careful working relationship, never an alliance, with the most malign dark fae of the deep forest, the formless beings of darkness and fear that resent mankind, and this has let it outlast Durenmar's hostility and the emperor's clearing of the forests. Its covenfolk are wholly bewitched by Jiphella: fanatically loyal, worshipping the magae as gods and ready to die at a word, but slack-witted, unable to think for themselves and needing to be told to eat each day. There are no consortes.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: not given
Income: not given
Mundane: hostile to the emperor's deforestation; mundanes who feel the Shrouded Glen never return
Tension: Durenmar accused Dankmar at the Tribunal of 1081 of secret league with the fay, and proved nothing; in 1151 Dankmar prosecuted Durenmar for plundering faerie sites and won, with the rare joint backing of the Hawthorn and Elder Gilds
Tension: the destruction of St Georgen monastery in 1208 is widely blamed on Dankmar; at the Tribunal of 1214 Jiphella, its sole delegate, denied it, and with no mundane witness and the Guardians of the Forests ruling to shelter under, a close vote refused an investigation
Tension: Murion's raven Kolkrabus spies on the covenant
Faerie: Orphedra has a pact with the local bockmen to patrol the woods around the covenant
Hook: a cautionary example of what magical domination of mundanes comes to

covenants.name: Triamore
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
The Quaesitores have long wished to censure the covenant for its mundane dealings. The cause of the recent deaths is not stated.
covenants.summary:
A castle and manorial estate on the Meuse at the edge of the Ardennes in Lower Lorraine, on the western fringe of the Rhine Tribunal, with Liege and Verdun the nearest towns; Verdun and Triamore are where the Redcaps of the Rhine and Normandy usually meet. A comfortable covenant of reasonable magi with a Magic aura of 2 and a famous library, to which guests are expected to add a book.

Triamore has long been tangled in the politics of its neighbourhood, for which the local Quaesitores have repeatedly sought to censure it; only the shrewd dealing of its princeps, Daria la Gris, has held them off. Recent deaths and Twilights have left it magically and politically weak and pushed to the margins, so Daria recruits by welcoming peregrinatores and visiting magi, though the tales of trouble keep numbers low.

As co-leader of the Apple Gild she backs the proposed Lotharingian Tribunal, which would free the covenant's mundane dealings and turn it from a border minnow into the hub of a new Tribunal; to that end she cultivates friendships with several Normandy covenants. Both its Tremere sigils are held by Stentorius of Fengheld, the Tremere exarch of the Rhine.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: not given
Income: a manorial estate (details not given)
Mundane: deep in local politics, details not given; Redcaps pass through on the road between the Rhine and Normandy
Tension: the Lotharingian motion, which would make Triamore the centre of a new Tribunal
Tension: Quaesitorial scrutiny of its mundane entanglements, fended off so far by Daria
Tension: vacancies after recent deaths and Twilights, an open door for new magi or a sign of something sinister
Hook: the library draws visitors, who are expected to contribute a book
Allies: several Normandy covenants, cultivated by Daria

covenants.name: Waddenzee
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
Imanitos Mendax of Oculus Septentrionalis feeds Eric advance word of that covenant's ship movements for a share of the plunder, and the Waddenzee magi are party to it; the messages may travel by Astasians, tiny messenger demons taken for airy spirits.
The power of the Pirates' Graveyards may be Infernal rather than Magic; Lucas has barely considered it.
covenants.summary:
A Spring covenant of pirate magi on a deserted stretch of the Frisian island of Terschelling, on the Wadden Sea, preying on the shipping of the North Sea, skirting the Code of Hermes and breaking mundane law every day. It was founded in 1165 as Terschelling by Axior of Flambeau, a dissident of Oculus Septentrionalis, who died in a magical accident within twenty years. Hygwald Veritas and Eric Ribecus arrived in 1200 and by 1207 announced that they were the only magi left, renamed the covenant Waddenzee, a claim to the whole sea, and changed its charter and symbol, to uproar at Tribunal; a Quaesitorial inquiry found no wrongdoing and a vote to treat it as a new covenant needing the Tribunal's leave failed thanks to the Oak and Ash Gilds.

About twenty years ago Hygwald and Eric killed a pirate chief and took his three ships and crews; the covenant now sails five magically enhanced ships, the flagship Nebelkönigin among them, taken from Oculus Septentrionalis while she carried a great cargo of vis and magical books with no magus aboard. It stays within the letter of the Code by leaving no witnesses. Only the failure of the coastal nobles to act together has saved it, and an understanding with Fengheld restrains Oculus Septentrionalis from moving against it.

A Magic aura of 3 covers the covenant building and a few hundred paces round it: a long, low Danish-style long-house sunk partly into the ground for the covenfolk, with four separate buildings for the magi joined to the middle of each wall by sunken covered walkways, each holding a magus, his lab, one or two consortes and some warriors, and a harbour. The magi foster the island's reputation for haunting, in truth the din of thousands of seabirds in spring and summer, and have driven off other settlers. The turb of nearly two hundred pirates and hangers-on from all over Europe is probably the Rhine's largest; about half are at sea at any time in two ships and most of the rest are drunk, but they obey the magi and their deputies.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: rich, but mostly other people's, taken as plunder
Vis: Lucas von Beck harvests vis at the Pirates' Graveyards in Drenthe, where the Frisian pirates bury their dead
Income: piracy on the North Sea with five enchanted ships
Mundane: outlaws to the local nobility, who cannot unite against them
Tension: enemies of Oculus Septentrionalis, which waits for one misstep
Tension: the Quaesitores have warned the covenant repeatedly that it walks a fine line, will get no Tribunal support if the mundane authorities move, and that each pirate magus would likely face charges of High Crimes
Tension: Eric Ribecus's younger cousin Estrid Danesson of Oculus Septentrionalis is his bitter enemy
Allies: a mutual understanding with Fengheld; the Oak and Ash Gilds backed it in the 1207 vote
Hook: a generation hence the Hanseatic League will build bigger ships, sail in convoy and hire soldiers against pirates; with Oculus Septentrionalis at its head an assault on Waddenzee is plausible, but the League is more than twenty years off
Hook: the stolen Hermetic books may have been placed in the pirates' hands and tainted; Lucas may be using infernal lore in his necromancy without knowing it, and only Hachim may have the wisdom to resist

covenants.name: Oculus Septentrionalis
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
The covenant holds three Verditius magestones, given secretly in 1144, each giving a Magic aura of 3 over a large room; they are shared so each magus has a Magic-aura lab for up to two seasons a year. Only Durenmar's senior magi also know. Imanitos might swap them for infernally tainted copies to breed greed in the labs.
Imanitos Mendax betrays the covenant to Waddenzee, selling its ship movements for a share of the loot; discovery would mean expulsion and undying enmity. He may also be a diabolist of a hidden dark Jerbiton lineage serving the demon Radegast, corrupting Lübeck's notables through the Goldenes Kalb and posing as Radegast's prophet to the Mecklenburg family, with low-Might demons for messengers, thieves, spies and seducers.
A secret deal with Fengheld: a rook of vis a year in exchange for a huge yearly shipment of luxuries and over a hundred pounds of silver.
covenants.summary:
The Eye of the North, a Summer covenant mostly of House Jerbiton spread through the city of Lübeck in Holstein, on the Baltic, in townhouses, warehouses, a shipyard and a fleet. The Tribunal created it by charter in 1144, at the Ash Gild's urging, to learn about the Norse wizards, ruling that a covenant needed no site at its founding, only magi bound by a charter. Its first magi did nothing for two decades, were fined three pawns each in 1158 and ordered to find a site, and three of them settled in Lübeck around 1160 while Axior left to found Terschelling.

It abandoned the Ash mission for peaceful contact and trade with the magical folk of the north, two of whom have married its magi, and became a principal proponent of the Apple Gild. Hermetically weak and aloof from Tribunal politics, it is immensely rich and woven into the city as merchants, scholars and craftsmen; the burghers do not know them for wizards, and its wealth may exceed that of all the other Rhine covenants together. Lübeck has an ordinary Divine aura and the covenant no Magic aura of its own. The Quaesitores wrote into its charter that it may admit only magi with the Gentle Gift.

Its magi seldom raise the Parma daily or cast where they can be seen, though most have some discreet magic; they meet rarely, so their politics are gossipy and conspiratorial. Discreet visitors are welcome and indiscreet ones asked to leave. There is room for one or two more magi, Jerbiton, Apple Gild or Redcaps with the Gentle Gift and a mundane trade, and two seldom-used peregrinator labs above the Novgorod Inn. There is no turb, only a handful of mercenaries guarding the businesses, whose staff blur with the covenant's many servants and two scribes. Lübeck is the usual stop for Redcaps bound for Novgorod, a few weeks away by sea, and the covenant keeps a contact at the trading counter Lübeck's merchants have run there since 1205. Theoderich of Jerbiton recently left to help found Heorot in Denmark and remains friendly.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: chronically short; a few sources, all far from Lübeck around the Baltic, gathered by Estrid Danesson
Vis: Boris of Novgorod buys Novgorod vis cheaply
Income: trade, shipbuilding and the businesses of its magi; perhaps the richest covenant in the Rhine
Mundane: integrated among Lübeck's burghers as merchants, scholars and craftsmen; a contact at the Novgorod counter; Henri de Tours is likely to be at the heart of the coming Hanse
Tension: Waddenzee has taken several of its ships and cargoes, the Nebelkönigin among them; the covenant wants the pirates ended by Tribunal ruling or a secretly provoked mundane army, but has no proof and fears Quaesitorial scrutiny of its own mundane dealings
Tension: the Quaesitores forbade the trading venture the Nebelkönigin carried, so the ship cannot legally be recovered
Tension: Crintera suspects it of aiding the Danish invasion of Rügen; Urgen killed its leader Prudentum in Wizard's War in 1179, and since Falke's moderate leadership the two covenants ignore each other
Tension: Philippus Niger presses it to investigate the Norse wizards harder and to open a Mercere Portal to Durenmar
Hook: Henri de Tours may negotiate the treaty of Lübeck and Hamburg of 1241 or become Älderman; the League may be the covenant's own idea, and growing wealth brings Quaesitorial risk and the temptation to bribe at Tribunal
Hook: Marcus Navicularius is designing the Baltic cog, round, flat-bottomed, with a centre rudder and one square sail, carrying hundreds of tons of Novgorod timber, which the Hanse will adopt by mid-century

covenants.name: Fengheld
covenants.notes:
What the players do not know.

Secrets
Fengheld's real policy is to keep every other covenant so tangled in politics that nobody notices its own growing power; it has worked so far, and its vote bloc is the Tribunal's largest.
Eule has passed into Final Twilight, and her celebrated wisdom is her filius Günther Lupus's fraud.
The Bears' Cave in the northern Harz is the private vis source of a hidden lineage of bear-heartbeast Bjornaer descending from the Founder: Urgen of Crintera and his filia Odorpes of the Lusatia chapter.
covenants.summary:
The largest covenant of the Rhine in land, people and magi, twenty-three of them with about a dozen at the main site, and the most diverse, with no House or gild dominant: an Autumn covenant in a sprawling hilltop fortress in a lonely spot among the hills of the eastern Harz, on the borders of Saxony and Thuringia, with a Magic aura of 5 on the hilltop and half a dozen chapter houses across northern mainland Europe. It presents itself as the Tribunal's neutral peacemaker and often arbitrates between covenants; both the Apple and the Linden Gilds were founded by its members.

Founded in 1039 by Flambeau and Tremere veterans home from the Schism War in Stonehenge and Normandy, approved readily as a quiet retreat for ageing war heroes away from mundanes, it became instead the base from which its political Tremere, with the Transylvanian Tribunal, served Emperor Henry III's conquests of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary and seized many vis sites. When the main site filled, the Tribunal blocked its daughter covenants of young Tremere, so it founded chapter houses instead, citing Greater Alps practice and trusting its martial strength to hold several sites. Every chapter magus accepts Fengheld's charter, a ruling on Fengheld binds the chapters and the reverse, and most chapters have a local charter too. Ties with Transylvania have lately loosened and it is no longer seen as a Tremere covenant.

Its hierarchy is rigid: the Archmage Stentorius; eight masters, five at the main site (Eule, Horst, Peter von Würzburg, Dorana, Indulius) and three in chapters (Clemens, Hassan El-Megrayhi, Wilhelm Weiss); then fourteen journeymen, the six at the main site ranking a little above the eight in chapters. Of the eleven chapter magi six are detailed in five chapters and five are left to the storyguide, as is the site of the biggest chapter, run by Clemens filius Stentorius, which could sit near the player covenant; or the player magi could themselves be a chapter under Fengheld's seniors.

An immense curtain wall rings a summit of some twenty buildings: a tower for every resident magus, an elaborate guest house, a huge meeting hall and housing for covenfolk and grogs, with outlying hamlets. Vineyards and orchards cover the south slope, grain and roots the valley floor, sheep and goats the rest, feeding well over two hundred people: about fifty soldiers, fifteen companions and nearly ten dozen smiths, glassblowers, parchment-makers, scribes, huntsmen, herders and serfs, each hierarchy ending in a magus. Eight guest labs at the main site and at least one at most chapters make it a famed host of peregrinatores, with up to six Redcaps present at a time. It is rich in minor enchanted items and raw vis.

Fengheld holds one of the Rhine's two Mercer Houses and its senior Redcap, and is the busier of the two for its central position and its generosity: Redcaps serving the north, Boris of Novgorod among them, meet those serving the south here at agreed times, and Redcaps from other Tribunals who will not cross the Black Forest come here instead of Durenmar. This near-monopoly of the Order's news serves Fengheld well.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: about two dozen sites, some hundreds of miles away, many seized in the eastern conquests of the 11th century; none is named
Vis: a rook a year goes to Oculus Septentrionalis (secretly) for luxuries and silver
Income: a vast farming estate, Peter von Würzburg's wines, and the trade of the Rheingasse and Cherbourg chapters
Mundane: the local nobility has somehow never noticed the scale of the estate, and nobody has openly accused Fengheld of magic to keep it so; Peter's wines are prized by the nobles of southern Saxony and Thuringia
Mundane: the Rheingasse chapter in Cologne manages supplies and contacts; Fengheld House in Cherbourg trades with England and France
Votes: more than forty Tribunal votes, nearly a quarter of the whole, though seldom cast as a bloc; Stentorius holds about three-fifths of the Rhine's Tremere sigils
Tension: the more paranoid magi of the Tribunal suspect a hidden agenda behind the neutrality
Tension: Fengheld and its allies oppose Philippus Niger of Durenmar at every turn; Dorana urges Stentorius to contest Murion's leadership of the Oak Gild and Occultes to contest her Primacy, while the familiars Oswald and Kolkrabus feud over the gild
Tension: a planned chapter at Durenmar, Rudolph of Bonisagus's idea, is backed cautiously and doubted by some seniors
Tension: the Lusatia chapter, ten miles from the agreed Novgorod border, caused the latest boundary dispute with that Tribunal; Odorpes has been accused at Tribunal more than once of neglecting her duties
Allies: a mutual understanding with Waddenzee; Hassan El-Megrayhi is parens of Hachim of Waddenzee, and Imanitos Mendax of Oculus Septentrionalis won his Master rank here
Hook: the library is vast but weighted to low-level books, so Fengheld-trained magi are generalists; specialists are invited as guests to improve it
Hook: Balastor means to return others to a feral state whether they consent or not

covenants.name: Heorot
covenants.notes:
Secrets
Oculus Septentrionalis has very likely struck some private bargain with Heorot as the price of its sponsorship.
covenants.summary:
A newly founded covenant on the Danish island of Zealand, raised on the site of the hall of Hrothgar, the Danish king of legend whom Beowulf rid of Grendel. It is not yet a member of the Rhine Tribunal and hopes to be admitted at the Tribunal of 1221.

Zealand is by tradition Novgorod territory, but no covenant of the Order has ever lasted long enough in the Norse lands to attend a Tribunal, the Order of Odin being thought too great a danger, so whose ground it is remains a grey area. All Heorot's magi come from the Rhine, and their declared purpose is the one Oculus Septentrionalis was founded for and never pursued: to learn about the Order of Odin. Unlike that covenant, they have the skills for it.

Oculus Septentrionalis sponsors the application; Crintera, close by on Rügen, opposes it. Meanwhile the kin of Grendel, trolls of the island's bogs, harass the covenant.
covenants.what_matters:
Membership: not yet a member of the Rhine Tribunal; applies at the Tribunal of 1221, and the Novgorod Tribunal, whose territory Zealand nominally is, has not been told
Border dispute: many Rhine magi enjoy the thought of taking ground from Novgorod, and the Tribunal would like to push its claim east
Opposition: Crintera, close by on Rügen, fears a rival for the region's vis sources and objects to the admission
Support: Oculus Septentrionalis sponsors the covenant; Waddenzee does not object, since Heorot will bring it more victims and serves the Ash Gild's chief interest
Purpose: to learn about the Order of Odin, the aim Oculus Septentrionalis once held, and this time with the skills to pursue it
Trolls: the kin of Grendel still haunt Zealand's bogs and attack the covenant; Signum Irruptus's study of them has already cost fourteen grogs and his own left arm
Vis: no sources recorded
Mundane relations: not recorded; Zealand is Danish, under King Valdemar II

covenants.name: Crintera
covenants.notes:
Secrets
Urgen is widely suspected of driving mundanes from the wild with covert animal attacks, and is stepping them up now that the Primacy no longer restrains him.
Stubnitz only looks untouched: the forest hides many settlements of covenfolk, concealed by magic.
The fetishes of the Animal Powers on the fourth level (a wooden squirrel on a stump, a stone otter among cattails, a rush-woven snake in a hollow boulder, a clay wolf with shell teeth, stone birds in willow saplings hung with feathered thongs, and one for every other beast, only a few visible from any spot) are truly ancient and said to hold primordial nature spirits. Touching one's own brings a deep sense of connection; anyone who resisted the regio's changes, or nears another's fetish, feels compelled to leave it alone. Covenfolk leave offerings at the fetish of their heartbeast.
Bjornaer the Founder was a Pomeranian shapeshifter-witch; the werewolves of Pomerania count her a traitor who sold their secrets to the Roman priests.
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Bjornaer, deep in the Stubnitz Forest on the Jasmund peninsula of Rügen, inside a Magic regio of four levels whose auras run 1, 3, 5 and 8. Its only members are the six Elders of the Bjornaer council, who govern the House from here. It was founded by the followers of Bjornaer in the Order's first days and has stood ever since.

Once a quiet and powerful force in the Tribunal, Crintera has been in turmoil since the Danish conquest of Rügen in 1168 and has spent the fifty years since in Winter, as new churches and a Cistercian monastery push the Dominion towards it and a Christian island yields fewer recruits for the turb. The council is divided between Harmonists, who would live alongside mundanes who leave the wild alone, and Wilderists, who would defend the wilderness against all men.

Religion of every kind is forbidden inside the regio in honour of the Animal Powers, who held the forest before the Bjornaer came; it is among the covenant's oldest laws. Every twelve years the whole House meets here for the Gathering of Twelve Years, which the islanders call the Devil's Year.

Crossing each boundary of the regio works a Corpus effect that draws the crosser's heartbeast forward, a personality trait at the first and small bodily changes at the others, so that someone who has crossed all four looks a quarter or a third animal. The Parma usually resists this, but resisting is thought rude; Bjornaer can shrug the changes off with their Heartbeast. Visitors reach it by the Watching Path, the one route through Stubnitz, marked at its start by two mossy, crumbling stones in a glade near the forest's edge and known to Redcaps and Bjornaer; covenfolk and animal allies watch everyone who walks it.

The covenant of Rethra in Pomerania, once a sister community of Slavic magus-priests, fell silent and was declared abolished by the Tribunal of 1207, leaving Crintera the Order's only presence in the Marches.
covenants.what_matters:
Factions: Harmonists against Wilderists on the council, with Urgen's Wilderists gaining ground as the occupation drags on; the next Gathering, in 1227, is expected to be explosive
Heorot: Crintera opposes its admission in 1221, fearing competition for vis near Rügen
Oculus Septentrionalis: a feud since 1179, when Urgen accused them of helping the Danish invasion and slew their leader in Wizard War; lately the guest Caprea blinded the familiar of their peace envoy Carolus by accident, and relations are worse than ever
The Danes: King Valdemar II's occupation, the churches of Bergen and Altenkirchen, a Cistercian monastery, monks farming Mönchgut and a church planned at Sagard, five miles away; the turb shrinks as recruits grow scarce
Vis: Creo vis every year from Zora, priestess of Hertha, in return for protection of her priesthood and a promise that no victim is taken from Crintera's covenfolk; other sources not recorded, though the invasion is said to have damaged them while leaving them largely intact
The Baltic thaw: each early spring Falke casts Appease the Queen of Winter at Arkona, where Svantovit's lingering presence gives the ritual a bonus, to break the sea ice and reopen shipping
Faerie trod: the volkhvy of the Forest Brothers alone can open the gate in the Ziegensteine barrow, and often let Bjornaer use it; it leads one way to Pripet Major in the Novgorod Tribunal
Pagan allies: friendly with the volkhvy of the Forest Brothers and the priestesses of Hertha; the Svantovit priests of Arkona helped Falke learn her ritual
Mundane relations: hostile or wary towards the Danish crown and the island's churches; islanders shun Stubnitz and tell of animal attacks, shadow-monsters and witches, which suits the covenant
The Gathering of Twelve Years: all Bjornaer come every twelve years (last 1203, next 1227), fifty to a hundred magi, for lineage rites, remembrance of the dead, most Mystery initiations under the Swan Elder, Ardea's re-enactments of old legends, visions of the Animal Powers and House politics; nothing is confirmed or denied to outsiders
The council: Wolf (the Primus), Bear (Senior Elder, always a bear heartbeast, casting vote), Horse (keeps track of all Bjornaer), Stag (protector), Eagle (watches the Order), Swan (leads rituals, long held by a line of heron-heartbeast seers); a bear Primus merges Wolf and Bear and a Seat of the Fox fills the sixth place
Succession: a dead or Twilit Elder waits for the next Gathering, when the rest choose by an ancient divination (once a Great Beast pointed out the heir); the whole House elects the Primus from the council's candidates
Guests: visiting Bjornaer may raise a temporary sanctum on the third regio level and stay for years

covenants.name: Irencillia
covenants.notes:
Secrets
Irencillia was not Merinita's home; the true first domus magna, her temple of Diana, is lost and its name forgotten.
A caricature's Might grows over time to a cap set by its magus's standing at Irencillia, in politics or in faerie understanding rather than raw power; a magus who takes on his caricature's manner grows hard to tell from it, and the two become Arcane Connections to each other.
The Prophet Iacob of the God of Truth is Iacob filius Handri, carrying out the Primus's secret plan to found a religion in the name of the fae; the Quaesitors would be appalled.
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Merinita, hidden in faerie woodland where the northern Bohemian Forest meets the plain, among beech and oak full of fallow deer, boar, lynx and bears. Quendalon, the second Primus, built it after his return from Arcadia, when he turned the House towards the fae, so it dates from the late eighth or ninth century. The land about it is kept wild by the covenant's meddling.

An Autumn covenant, now larger than ever as human encroachment on faerie lands drives Merinita magi home to it; three further magi beyond those named live here, left to the storyguide. It holds aloof from the politics of region and Tribunal alike, prizing its seclusion.

Its Faerie aura is patchy: at least 1 everywhere within the boundary, up to 6 where the sancta stand, with odd high spots such as a covered walk to the kitchens at 4 along its length. Many of the stronger patches, most sancta among them, lie in fragmented regiones whose entrances bear symbols (a badger's head, a crescent moon) that outsiders cannot read. The theory is that all this is the wreckage of the vast magical war between Quendalon and Myanar.

The covenant shows itself to each visitor as expectation shapes it: a castle of living wood with courtiers, a hamlet of foresters in green and brown, a wooded hill with a trilithon over a labyrinth, a gully of caves peopled by twisted folk; those who do not know it is there see open woodland and wander through unaware, avoided by its people. Every view shares an enclosing boundary (palisade, drystone wall or thorn hedge), a single gateway, and over it an inscription said to be Merinita's last words before she vanished in 785, to the effect that the spirits of old endure unchanged in the depths of rivers and the endless twilight of forests.

The glamour is lived, not merely seen: materials, covenfolk's looks and even a plucked leaf differ from one observer to another, and anything carried out of the aura turns to dust and dry twigs at sunrise or sunset. No usable map can be drawn; only the sancta (each magus's firm notion of his own, as castle, town house, garden or barrow) and to a lesser degree the shared library, council chamber and dining hall reach a consensus. No magus's Magic Resistance has ever stopped the effect, and nobody knows whether it is a spell, a faerie power or something else. Every magus who stays more than a season gains a caricature, a faerie double.
covenants.what_matters:
House politics: Handri outmanoeuvred Vinaria and took the Primacy from her; she went into what is called Faerie Twilight and came back after seven years apparently unchanged
The God of Truth: a dualist faith reverencing the wild and its faerie angels has sprung up in the villages near the forest over the last ten years, wherever the Prophet Iacob and his white crow are seen
Handri's diplomacy: long private embassies into faerie lands, and rumours that he has met survivors of House Diedne
Caricatures: every resident magus gains a faerie double (a Faerie Friend for the stay); a double can serve as an Arcane Connection, may be kidnapped to strike at its magus, or be sent to Tribunal in a busy magus's place
The lost domus magna: Merinita was the last Roman priestess of Diana, drawn into the Order only by Trianoma's persuasion as her cult died under Charlemagne's Christianisation; Irencillia was never her home, and the House has forgotten where her temple stood or what it was called
Maddenhofen Woods: the covenant closely guards the nearby woods where Tytalus vanished in 807 and a powerful faerie grants a Heart's Desire for a task never yet completed, yet seems to take no vis from them
Two societies: human and fae live side by side; the Primus's caricature is always the monarch of the Faerie Court, at present Queen Rosmert, though whether one shapeshifting ruler or a new one with each Primus is unknown
Gild: the Elder Gild, which Iacob leads
Vis: no sources recorded
Mundane relations: deliberately none; wanderers are shunned, and the only indirect tie is the God of Truth in the nearby villages

covenants.name: Roznov
covenants.notes:
Secrets
Every summer solstice the whole covenant and village celebrate Radegast at the summit temple with orgiastic drinking and debauchery, and a few celebrants, usually slaves, are quietly seized and sacrificed inside the temple, seen only by Igor's most loyal servants. It is never spoken of, though most covenfolk guess why people vanish each summer. The victims' blood yields Corpus vis and feeds the harvest of dozens of pawns. Some supernatural agency seems to keep the sacrifices secret.
The Tremere of the Fort know nothing of the festival's true nature and, unusually for their House, neither discourage nor disapprove of the paganism; or, at the storyguide's choice, they know and hold their tongues for a hidden reason.
Roznov Castle, a small twin-towered castle inside a curtain wall two-thirds of the way up Mount Radhost and visible only from its own valley, and Roznov Fort, the fort and village at the foot that command the single pass, are joined by tunnels through the mountain.
Ladislaus uses Magic Sensitivity at the Prague market to pick out Gifted children among the slaves, who go to Coeris, the Tremere domus magna in Transylvania; the rest are traded or put to work at Roznov.
covenants.summary:
An Autumn covenant in a valley at the edge of the Carpathians on Mount Radhost, in the far east of Moravia on the Hungarian border, founded in 1067 by three Ex Miscellanea magi and admitted to the Rhine Tribunal in 1074. A Magic aura of 4 covers the whole valley, rising to 6 at the crude stone temple on the summit.

It joins two strong and utterly different traditions. One half is the pagan priesthood of the old Slavic god Radegast, Ex Miscellanea magi in Roznov Castle; the other an arch-conservative stronghold of House Tremere in Roznov Fort. The two act independently, their political aims often coinciding, yet one half commonly hears of the other's schemes only from third parties. Nine magi live here in all: Igor Rastvan and two former apprentices at the Castle, Severicus with his two filii and a Tytalus at the Fort.

Its allegiance looks split between the Rhine, whose Tribunals it attends, and the Tremere-run Transylvanian Tribunal, with which it is thought to keep regular contact, so most Rhine magi distrust it; even so it has grown into a significant political force in the Tribunal. Radegast's worship once centred on his Oracle at Rethra in Pomerania, a covenant of Slavic magus-priests that the Tribunal declared abolished in 1207, but Mount Radhost was always his sacred place.
covenants.what_matters:
Founding suspicion: Roznov could have joined Novgorod or Transylvania but took Durenmar's and Crintera's richer offer; two Transylvanian Tremere joined almost at once in 1074, and some Rhine magi think the whole affair a Tremere ploy for a foothold, with the Ex Miscellanea as dupes
Vis: dozens of pawns gathered every summer solstice at the Radegast festival in the summit temple, and Corpus vis from blood
The festival: if Severicus and his filii learned what really happens at the solstice they would be horrified, with charges of diabolism, a pre-emptive March or Wizard War to follow in both Tribunals; unless the Tremere already know, and keep silent for a very good hidden reason
Kingdom of the Slavs: three young companions each believe themselves the rightful heir of a Slavic kingdom and dream of uniting their people against German dominance; the magi encourage all three to spur them on, and Igor has no favourite so long as the kingdom is Radegast's
The slave trade: Ladislaus, a companion of the covenant, buys at the Prague slave market, where the Knights of the Sword sell their Pomeranian captives
Sigils: Severicus holds his own, one of only two Rhine Tremere to do so (the other is Stentorius of Fengheld), and controls about two-fifths of the other Tremere sigils, his two filii's and Hygwald Veritas's of Waddenzee among them
Gilds: every magus belongs to the Ash or the Oak Gild
Mundane relations: the village below the Fort, whose folk guard the only trail up, and the Prague slave market; otherwise not recorded
Covenfolk: about a score of servants and soldiers at the Castle and four times as many at the Fort, rotated continually; many are devotees of Radegast and many bought slaves, who work feverishly hoping a summons uphill means merit rather than expendability; some earn freedom and a place in the turb by a blood oath
Transylvania: the Tremere of the Transylvanian Tribunal across the Hungarian border make their influence felt here

tribunals.name: The Rhine Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The First Tribunal covers every Imperial land north of the Alps: from the Jutland border in the north to the Danube in the south, and from the mouth of the Schelde, the Ardennes and the Argonne in the west to the Oder in the east, where its border with the Novgorod Tribunal is disputed and shifts. About 130 magi, close to a ninth of the Order, make it the largest and oldest of the thirteen Tribunals; it hosts the Grand Tribunal, and the domus magnae of Bonisagus (Durenmar), Bjornaer (Crintera) and Merinita (Irencillia) all stand in its forests. Its magi descend from Roman and Germanic traditions with Slavic and Scandinavian additions, and about a sixth of them are peregrinatores, wandering magi who guest at covenants under the Tribunal's old laws of hospitality.

The Tribunal meets every seven years at Durenmar, opening on Walpurgis Night, the eve of the first of May, and sitting for over a week; the gilds and some Houses meet in the three days before. Its Praeco is not its oldest magus but the Prima of House Bonisagus, who votes the sigil of Bonisagus by proxy, a custom since Notatus; some, led by Fengheld, now want the Order's usual rule instead. Magi hold the ranks of journeyman, master and archmage: only masters take apprentices and hold a retired magus's sigil by proxy, archmagi hold two, and in a dispute that certamen would otherwise settle the higher rank has the right. Every apprentice trained here spends a season at Durenmar under a Bonisagus, and most join one of the six political gilds, which transcend House and covenant and monopolise the Tribunal's long-term quarrels, so that little changes at its meetings.

The Rhine is no longer a leading force in the Order but is respected for its age and cannot be ignored for its size. Its old tension with Novgorod continues except among the Bjornaer; the Greater Alps are friendly trading neighbours who think their Roman covenants superior; Transylvania's Tremere press on Moravia. The next meeting is in 1221, the 1360th year of the Aegis.

Secrets
The Apple Gild, with Oculus Septentrionalis, Triamore, about half of Fengheld's magi and two covenants of Normandy, means to propose a new Lotharingian Tribunal over the Low Countries and the north-west at the Grand Tribunal of 1228; Waddenzee, though no friend of the Apple Gild, would join to escape the Rhine. The Ash Gild's older members quietly plan war on the Norse wizards beyond the Baltic, which Murion does not oppose. Eule of Fengheld, the likeliest Praeco by age, is in fact in Final Twilight, which her covenant conceals.
tribunals.history:
Roman Germania. Rome's frontier ran along the Rhine and the Danube, and under Domitian the gap between the rivers was closed by the limes, a fortified line from near Remagen to Abusina above Regensburg. West of the Rhine the provinces of Upper and Lower Germania had cities like Cologne, Bonn, Trier and Mainz, with forum, baths and temples, where the priests of Mercury were everywhere. Beyond the river lay Germania Magna, forest, moor and fen, whose tribes of hunters, herders and small farmers worshipped Woden, Thunor, Tius and Fria. Rome never held it: in 9 AD Hermann of the Cherusci destroyed three legions under Varus in the Teutoburger Forest. Tacitus, about 98 AD, found the Germans brave, honest and hospitable but greedy, rough and fond of drink. By the third century the limes was abandoned under pressure from Franks, Alemanni and Goths, though Trier flourished as a western imperial capital under Constantine early in the fourth.

The Great Migration and the Merovingians. The wandering of the peoples was a slow drift rather than a flood: Goths into Gaul and Iberia, Vandals into Italy, Burgundians to the land that bears their name and to Worms in 413, Alemanni over the Rhine, Saxons, Angles and Jutes to Britain. The one violent eruption was Attila's Huns, checked at Chalons in 451 by Merovech and the Roman general Aetius. By about 600 the movements had ended, Slavs filling the empty lands of the Vistula and Oder and Saxons, Swabians, Frisians and Bavarians settled between the old Roman lines and the Slavs. The Franks rose under the Merovingians, named for the half-magical chieftain Merovech, whose grandson Clovis was baptised, united the Franks and ruled from Paris. The dynasty, credited with miraculous gifts, decayed after Clovis's grandsons Sigebert and Chilperic split the kingdom, and by 687 the mayors of the palace ruled in all but name. In 751 Pepin the Short sent the last Merovingian to a monastery and took the crown with the Church's blessing.

The Franks and Charlemagne. Charlemagne, king of the Franks from 768, carried Frankish rule, bishops and learning eastward from Aachen in three decisive campaigns that reached the Elbe and the Danube, gave the pagan Saxons the choice of baptism or death and planted bishoprics from Hamburg and Bremen to Paderborn, Hildesheim and Halberstadt. He fostered schools, made the count palatine his chief justice and in 789 outlawed sorcery and paganism while tolerating benevolent magic. On Christmas Day 800 the Pope crowned him emperor in Rome, and at his death in 814 the Frankish Empire held everything south and west of the Elbe, Bavaria included. His son Louis the Pious fought his own sons, and Frankish custom divided the inheritance: the Treaty of Verdun in 843 gave the west to Charles the Bald, the east to Louis the German and the imperial title with a narrow middle strip to Lothar. The later Carolingians faced Norse raids and the deposition of Charles the Fat in 887, and the last of them to be emperor, Arnulf of Carinthia, died in 899 amid rumours of murder.

The Ottonians. The heirs of Louis the German were nominal kings over Saxons, Swabians, Bavarians, Burgundians and Franconians while Moslems raided Italy, Northmen the coasts and Magyar horsemen plundered as far as France. The Magyar threat rallied the tribes behind Henry the Fowler, duke of Saxony, crowned in 919, who crushed the Magyars at Riade on the Unstrut in 933; his son Otto, crowned at Aachen in 936, ended the menace for good at the Lechfeld in 955. Otto's imperial coronation in Rome in 962 bound the German kings, henceforth emperors, to Italian politics for good. Under the four Saxon emperors the empire became the leading power west of the Adriatic, Slavs and Danes were converted and bishoprics founded in the Eastern Marches and Denmark, while some pagan Slavs withdrew to Rügen. Each Ottonian left exactly one heir, which spared the empire the Frankish habit of partition. Bishops became the emperor's instruments of government, invested by him with spiritual and secular office alike, a practice soon to be contested.

The Salians and the Investiture Contest. Conrad II began the Salian line in 1024, reaffirmed single inheritance of the crown, won in Italy and added the Burgundian crown in 1033; in 1037 the unfree knights called ministeriales entered the German feudal order. Henry III secured the loyalty of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary. Then in 1075 a papal bull forbade laymen to invest prelates, opening five decades of struggle over who led the Church: Gregory VII excommunicated Henry IV and forced his penance at Canossa in 1077, though Henry was crowned emperor in Rome in 1084 all the same. Papal authority advanced with the First Crusade, during which crusaders massacred the Jews of Worms, Speyer, Cologne, Trier and Mainz in 1096 while Henry tried in vain to punish them. The quarrel ended at Worms in 1122: the Church would elect its own bishops and abbots, while the emperor might attend elections and invest German prelates with their secular honours, keeping their feudal dues and much real influence. Henry V, the last Salian, died in 1125.

The Hohenstaufen and Frederick Barbarossa. Lothar II's narrow election in 1125 and the Swabians' choice of Conrad III as anti-king in 1127 began the long feud of Welf and Hohenstaufen; Conrad became king in 1137 and his nephew Frederick Barbarossa followed in 1152. Barbarossa spent a third of his reign in Italy, where the towns resisted royal dues: the Milanese beat him at Legnano in 1176, the Helvetians held out and plague struck his army before Rome. In Germany his contest with Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony and leader of the Welfs, ended in 1180 with the duchy broken up, Henry exiled, Bavaria given to Otto of Wittelsbach and the Saxon lands to Hohenstaufen men. From about 1140 the push to the east cleared forests and planted settlers, a concern of frontier princes more than kings, who still looked to the Rhineland and Italy for the profits of lordship. Frederick carried the relics of the Three Magi from Milan to Cologne in 1164 and drowned in 1190 crossing the Seleph on crusade. His son Henry VI conquered Sicily in 1194 and died after six years; rival kings Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick were elected in 1198, Philip was murdered at Bamberg in 1208, and the Welf Otto IV, crowned in Rome in 1209, was excommunicated and deposed.

The empire in 1220. Frederick II, of a German father and a Sicilian mother, was made king of Germany in 1212 and crowned at Aachen in 1214, helped Philip of France crush Otto IV at Bouvines that year, and was crowned emperor in Rome in 1220 after vowing a crusade he has made no move to begin. He prefers Sicily and a court of brilliant minds, writes poetry and a treatise on falconry, is called the wonder of the world, and has taken the wizard Michael Scot into his service, to the Church's unease. Germany is a loose elective kingdom with no capital: the king is crowned at Aachen and keeps his treasury at Nuremberg, and the princely nobility of dukes, archbishops, prince-bishops, landgraves, margraves and counts attend the Diet and choose him. Fiefs pass only in the male line and are divided among sons, so the provinces have splintered into countless small lordships, with new estates carved from eastern colonisation, forest clearance and drained marsh. Most cities belong to counts, dukes or bishops, but fourteen Free Imperial Cities answer only to the emperor. The Zähringen dukes died out in 1218, the Teutonic Knights and the Sword Brothers crusade in the Baltic, and Valdemar II of Denmark holds Holstein. More than half the land is still forest, and magic has withdrawn from the swelling cities into the woods.
tribunals.meeting_place: Durenmar, in the Black Forest: the Forum of Hermes and the Tribunal Field

cases.title: Heorot asks to join the Tribunal
cases.charge: Heorot, founded on Zealand in 1215 with Oculus Septentrionalis' backing, applies for membership at the Tribunal of 1221; Zealand is nominally Novgorod's, which does not know of it.

cases.title: The Lusatia chapter and the Novgorod border
cases.charge: Fengheld's Lusatia chapter house stands ten miles from the agreed border, the latest of the Rhine's boundary disputes with Novgorod; the Tribunal is asked to assert its claim east to the Oder and to take the matter to the Grand Tribunal of 1228.

cases.title: Choosing the Praeco by age
cases.charge: That the Rhine should choose its Praeco as the rest of the Order does, by age, and not always the Prima of Bonisagus; Eule of Fengheld would then be the likeliest, with Caecilius of Durenmar and Schadrit of Dankmar the other candidates.

cases.title: Crintera and the Danes
cases.charge: Fifty years after Valdemar's invasion of Rügen, Crintera again asks the Tribunal to act against the Danish occupation and the Dominion it brings; the Tribunal split on gild lines in 1186 and Caecilius ruled against in 1194, and Bjornaer who attacked settlers have been prosecuted since.

cases.title: Triamore's dealings with mundanes
cases.charge: Triamore's long entanglement in the politics of the Meuse, for which the Quaesitores have sought censure for years; Daria la Gris has so far talked the covenant out of it.

cases.title: Fengheld's house at Durenmar
cases.charge: Fengheld is building a three-storey stone house on the Tribunal Field as a permanent chapter at Durenmar, with a laboratory and its own Mercere Portal, after Durenmar refused it a Portal in the Forum; Durenmar calls it an encroachment.

cases.title: Waddenzee's piracy
cases.charge: Waddenzee's magi prey on North Sea shipping; the Quaesitores have warned them repeatedly that they walk a fine line and will get no help if the mundane powers move against them, and that each would face High Crimes charges.

cases.title: Odorpes of Fengheld's neglect
cases.charge: Fengheld has more than once accused its own Odorpes, of the Lusatia chapter, of neglecting her duties to the covenant.

cases.title: The Rhine Gorge after the ban
cases.charge: The twenty-year ban on magic in the Rhine Gorge runs out in 1220; whoever would found a covenant there needs a sponsor from every covenant. Durenmar wants a neutral, traditional foundation; Fengheld would rather it were one of its chapters.

rulings.title: A season at Durenmar
rulings.says: From the Tribunal's founding: every apprentice trained in the Rhine spends at least one season at Durenmar, taught by a magus of House Bonisagus.

rulings.title: The laws of hospitality (961 AA)
rulings.says: A magus may ask hospitality of any lawful Rhine covenant, which must publish its conditions; a guest who accepts them is guaranteed at least three and at most seven years, pays at least three pawns of vis a year, and the conditions are the same for every guest in residence and change only when there are none.

rulings.title: Proxy sigils (1017 AA)
rulings.says: Firm rules on the voting of retired magi, ending twenty years of dispute: a master is entrusted with one retired magus's sigil, an archmage with a second, cast in the retired magus's name and, by custom, by his likely wishes.

rulings.title: Ranks
rulings.says: Only a master may take an apprentice (a journeyman's filius is treated as a new hedge recruit); three masters of other covenants, Houses and gilds confer the rank; in any dispute certamen would otherwise settle, the higher rank has the right. House Tremere contests this, as it was made to curb them.

rulings.title: Founding a covenant (1024 AA)
rulings.says: A new covenant needs a sponsoring magus from every existing covenant of the Tribunal. Arae Flaviae and Schwarzburg abolished the same year. Chapter houses need no such leave, which is how Fengheld grows.

rulings.title: Guardians of the Forests (1192 AA)
rulings.says: Magi may actively defend the wilderness against those who would destroy it. In 1194 Caecilius ruled that the Danish occupation of Rügen is no such destruction, as no wilderness was invaded.

rulings.title: A day's march (1248 AA)
rulings.says: A magical site within a day's march of a covenant belongs to it; Valdus of Tytalus, who harvested Treverorum's, was fined a pawn as the covenant had lost nothing, and told to ask in future.

rulings.title: A covenant without a site
rulings.says: At the Ash Gild's urging the Tribunal founded Oculus Septentrionalis to learn of the Norse wizards, ruling that a covenant needs no site at founding, only magi bound by a charter. In 1158 its magi were fined three pawns each for keeping neither.

rulings.title: Dankmar against Durenmar
rulings.says: Durenmar, found to have molested the fay and plundered faerie sites, paid a rook of vis to every other covenant and was barred from faerie sites for fourteen years unless it made peace with them.

rulings.title: No magic in the Rhine Gorge (1339 AA)
rulings.says: After Rheinstein was destroyed by the archbishop of Trier's army, largely through its own doing, no magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years: a ban that ends in 1220.

rulings.title: Waddenzee is Terschelling
rulings.says: The two survivors of Terschelling renamed it Waddenzee with a new charter and symbol; a vote to call it a new covenant needing leave failed, by the Oak and Ash Gilds. The same year Rethra, silent for decades, was declared abolished.

diary.title: Mercurian temple at Durenmar's site
diary.details: Priests of the Roman Cult of Mercury raise a temple deep in the Black Forest, on the ground Durenmar later takes, hoping to turn the primeval power of the Hercynian Forest to their own use. In the Roman years they bind the forest's spirit by its own oaths into what is now the Fane of the Founders; a wild splinter of it escapes south and in time becomes the King of the Black Mountain.

diary.title: Black Forest Road finished
diary.details: The Eighth Legion under Cornelius Clemens completes the road from Offenburg to Rottweil with the help of Mercurian priests, who set warding milestones along it. The Roman limes of the same age cuts the Black Forest, and its spirit, off from the rest of the Hercynian Forest.

diary.title: Donar Oak felled
diary.details: St Boniface cuts down the Donar Oak at Geismar in Thuringia and builds an oratory of St Peter from its wood. Pagan magic, relics and belief wane from that day, and the one great spirit of the Hercynian Forest is shattered into the many lesser forests of Germany.

diary.title: Trianoma apprenticed to Bonisagus
diary.details: Trianoma finds Bonisagus in his cave in the Alps, becomes his apprentice and learns the Parma Magica.

diary.title: The Founders gathered
diary.details: From 731 to 767 Trianoma seeks out the wizards who will be the Founders and brings them to Bonisagus, who refines his theory with each. Merinita comes in from the wild and persuades the shapeshifter Bjornaer to join, for which Bjornaer's old fellows, the sorceress Gyongy among them, condemn her.

diary.title: Bonisagus settles at Durenmar
diary.details: Bonisagus leaves his Alpine cave for the ruined Roman temple in the Black Forest, hoping to reconcile his Hermetic theory with the forest's primeval magic; between 754 and 767 the place is built up with room for many magi.

diary.title: Order of Hermes founded at Durenmar
diary.details: The Founders compose and swear the Oath at the Fane of the Founders and hold the first Tribunal gathering. Bonisagus's followers and some of the Founders settle at Durenmar and build the covenant.

diary.title: Covenants on Durenmar's model
diary.details: Between 767 and 773 Flambeau and his apprentices leave to found Val-Negra in the Pyrenees, and other magi found covenants of their own after Durenmar's pattern.

diary.title: Bjornaer's first council on Rügen
diary.details: Bjornaer and her followers meet in council on Rügen; her House has gathered there every twelve years since.

diary.title: Second Grand Tribunal
diary.details: A Tribunal is ruled to need at least twelve magi from four covenants. Crintera, the domus magna of House Bjornaer, and Fenistal, the domus magna of House Merinita, are founded.

diary.title: First Rhine Tribunal (919 AA)
diary.details: The Rhine Tribunal meets for the first time, at Durenmar. Arae Flaviae in Swabia and Rethra in the Eastern Marches are founded.

diary.title: Jerbiton before Charlemagne
diary.details: Jerbiton, who has taken on the apprentices of the imperial mage-smith Carolinus, meets Charlemagne. The emperor outlaws sorcery and paganism but allows the kind of benevolent magic Jerbiton practises.

diary.title: Merinita leaves the Order
diary.details: The Founder Merinita is seen for the last time, going to seek the spirit of the wilderness; the Bohemian chapter dates her going to 785 and says her last words are carved over Irencillia's gate. Fenistal becomes the first covenant to enter Winter, and the new Primus Quendalon founds Irencillia.

diary.title: Third Grand Tribunal
diary.details: After the gathering Quendalon goes into the faerie woods of Bohemia, leaving Myanar to lead House Merinita.

diary.title: Quendalon returns; Irencillia the domus magna
diary.details: In 801 and 802 Quendalon comes back from the faerie woods and Myanar denies he is the true Quendalon. The struggle kills Myanar and loses Fenistal; Irencillia becomes the domus magna of House Merinita, the House turns to faerie magic, and the Elder Gild splits away from the Hawthorn Gild.

diary.title: Tytalus lost in the Maddenhofen Woods
diary.details: The Founder Tytalus enters the Maddenhofen Woods in Bohemia, saying he will face the Queen of all the Fae, and is never seen again.

diary.title: Bjornaer's last words
diary.details: At the Gathering of Twelve Years at Crintera, Bjornaer speaks for the last time to her House and goes into the forest as a bear.

diary.title: Fifth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Grand Tribunals are to meet every thirty-three years from now on, and the regional Tribunals every seven years from 836.

diary.title: Hercynius's lineage
diary.details: From about 850 to 948 Hercynius of Bonisagus founds a lineage within his House and draws other magi to his teaching on the forest's magic.

diary.title: Tribunal of 996 AA: the Twilight spirits
diary.details: The spirits of three magi lost to Twilight famously return to the gathering.

diary.title: Sixth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The borders of the Tribunals are fixed along the lines of the Frankish partition and named: Rhine, Normandy, Provencal, Britannian, Roman, Theban, Eastern and Greater Alps.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1017 AA: proxy sigils
diary.details: Firm rules on the votes of retired magi end twenty years of dispute over whether and how their sigils may be cast.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1024 AA: founding rules
diary.details: Arae Flaviae and Schwarzburg are abolished, and strict rules for the founding of new covenants are agreed.

diary.title: Rudiaria founded (1031 AA)
diary.details: The Tribunal sponsors Rudiaria, a Flambeau-leaning covenant on the right bank of the Rhine opposite Bingen, and grants it every magical site along the river between Mainz and Cologne.

diary.title: Sirmium destroyed by the Magyars
diary.details: Magyar raiders destroy the covenant of Sirmium in Meissen, and with it the region's known vis sources. Wiederich of Flambeau, the only survivor, joins Henry the Fowler's army for revenge and serves at Riade in 933 and on the Lech in 955; after the Magyars' defeat House Bjornaer adopts three Magyar shapechangers, whose horse-hearted line survives, and Wiederich's descendants have hounded them as blood enemies ever since.

diary.title: Oakdell founded (1073 AA)
diary.details: Diedne magi found Oakdell in the Westerwald, a dozen miles east of the Rhine, with the Tribunal's sponsorship and on condition that it keeps out of Rudiaria's territory.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1080 AA: the Rowan Gild
diary.details: The Tribunal's followers of Diedne, until now of the Hawthorn Gild, found the Rowan Gild.

diary.title: Diabolism charge against Eginolf (1101 AA)
diary.details: Charges of diabolism against Eginolf of Flambeau of Rudiaria are not proven, but the reports of malefic doings near the covenant are noted with disapproval; Rudiaria is ordered to investigate, report within seven years and stop troubling the mundanes.

diary.title: Rudiaria destroyed (1108 AA)
diary.details: House Mercere reports Rudiaria burnt out in what looks like a catastrophic magical accident, every magus slain or missing; diabolism is suspected. The fall comes with a crippling famine and unrest in the region.

diary.title: Rudiaria's site sanctified (1115 AA)
diary.details: Nothing can be salvaged at Rudiaria; an archbishop of Mainz has sanctified the ground. Oakdell's claim to Rudiaria's sites is refused.

diary.title: Waldherz founded
diary.details: Followers of Hercynius leave Durenmar to found Waldherz, first as a chapter house and later as a disputed covenant in its own right.

diary.title: Grand Silesia founded
diary.details: Crintera and Rethra sponsor Grand Silesia, the Order's easternmost covenant yet; its Bjornaer and the Bonisagi of Waldherz join the Rowan Gild.

diary.title: Tenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The Rhine's own gathering of this year is the first of three (997, 1004 and 1011) at which distrust within the Order stops the renewal of the Founders' vows at the Fane.

diary.title: Oakdell's charges dismissed (1136 AA)
diary.details: Oakdell's accusations of espionage and meddling against magi of Durenmar are thrown out as spurious and unproven.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1143 AA: the Rowan Gild Marched
diary.details: The whole Rowan Gild is Marched, beginning the Schism War in the Rhine. Severus Maximus of Flambeau declares Wizard's War on Caithlinn of Oakdell and Cirion of Tremere on Pietro of Oakdell; Tremere and Flambeau magi set about destroying Oakdell and Waldherz.

diary.title: New Slavonic Tribunal declared
diary.details: The Slavic covenants, Rethra and Grand Silesia among them, break with their sponsors and declare a New Slavonic Tribunal. Grand Silesia is destroyed the same year.

diary.title: Oakdell razed (1155 AA)
diary.details: Oakdell is razed and all its Diedne magi slain in the Schism War.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1157 AA: the Schism War ends
diary.details: The Schism War is declared over; the Linden Gild grows up over the following decades. The renewal of the Founders' vows at the Fane resumes, an Ex Miscellanea magus taking the place Diedne's representative once held.

diary.title: Eleventh Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Over the Rhine's protests, the New Slavonic Tribunal is given authority over new covenants in Slavic lands.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1178 AA: Fengheld founded
diary.details: Veteran Tremere and Flambeau magi back from the Schism War in Britannia (fought in Stonehenge and Normandy) found Fengheld in the Harz with the Tribunal's ready approval, as a quiet retreat for ageing war heroes away from the mundanes.

diary.title: Fengheld's Tremere in Henry III's wars
diary.details: Through the reign of Henry III (1039 to 1056) Fengheld's political Tremere, working with the Transylvanian Tribunal, take part in the emperor's conquests of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary and seize many vis sites.

diary.title: Aschlaranda returns to Durenmar
diary.details: Aschlaranda, once of Waldherz, reappears at Durenmar.

diary.title: Dankmar founded
diary.details: Aschlaranda, exiled from Durenmar and from House Bonisagus, settles with her apprentice Schadrit at Dankmar in the Black Forest (the timeline puts their occupation of the site in 1053).

diary.title: Crintera allied with Pripet Maior
diary.details: Bjornaer magi once of Grand Silesia settle at Pripet Maior in the New Slavonic Tribunal, and Crintera and Pripet Maior form an alliance across the Tribunal border.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1192 AA: Guardians of the Forest
diary.details: The Guardians of the Forest ruling is made, allowing magi to defend wild places. Dankmar goes unrecognised as a covenant, Durenmar's influence seeing to it.

diary.title: Twelfth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: To curb the Rhine, the Grand Tribunal rejects its claim to the Polish lands left empty by Grand Silesia's fall and grants all Slavic lands to the New Slavonic Tribunal.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1206 AA: Roznov and Dankmar
diary.details: Roznov is founded in Moravia by three Ex Miscellanea magi, and Dankmar is at last recognised as a covenant of the Rhine.

diary.title: Roznov admitted
diary.details: Roznov is admitted to the Rhine Tribunal; two Tremere from Transylvania join it almost at once.

diary.title: Durenmar's charge against Dankmar
diary.details: Durenmar accuses Dankmar before the Tribunal of being secretly in league with the forest fay. Nothing is proven.

diary.title: King of the Black Mountain raids Durenmar
diary.details: The great faerie lord of the Black Forest attacks Durenmar; several Bonisagus magi and many covenfolk are killed or carried off, and the captives are never returned. In the years after, Durenmar's magi devise the most powerful Aegis of the Hearth yet known.

diary.title: First Treverorum proposal fails (1227 AA)
diary.details: Xantippes and Julia of Jerbiton and Selena Tibicena of Bonisagus propose a covenant in Trier to recover Roman secrets; with no sponsor from Irencillia, Crintera or Dankmar it is not recognised.

diary.title: Treverorum approved (1234 AA)
diary.details: The same three, now joined by Arliandus of Tremere, propose again and Treverorum is approved.

diary.title: Durenmar's lean half-century
diary.details: From about 1100 to 1150 Durenmar loses several magical sites to Zähringen settlement, runs short of vis and raids the forest's faerie sites greedily to make it up. The Black Fir begins to grow at the edge of its Aegis about this time.

diary.title: Valdus fined a pawn (1248 AA)
diary.details: Treverorum charges Valdus of Tytalus with twice harvesting vis from its site outside Trier's walls; he admits it but calls the site neglected and not theirs. The Tribunal rules that a site within a day's march of a covenant belongs to it, yet as Treverorum lost nothing Valdus pays one pawn and must ask leave in future.

diary.title: Rheinstein founded (1262 AA)
diary.details: Schwall of Bjornaer and Fulmonious of Tytalus found Rheinstein on Pfalz Island in the Rhine Gorge with the Tribunal's sponsorship, promising every other covenant a tithe of three pawns of vis a Tribunal for five Tribunals.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1283 AA: Oculus Septentrionalis founded
diary.details:
At the Ash Gild's urging the Tribunal resolves to learn more of the Norse wizards, the supposed Order of Odin, and orders a covenant founded for the purpose; three magi under Axior volunteer and Oculus Septentrionalis is born. The Tribunal rules that a covenant need have no site at its founding, only magi bound by a charter.

Secrets
Three Verditius magestones were secretly given to the new covenant.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1290 AA: Durenmar fined
diary.details: Dankmar accuses Durenmar of molesting faeries and plundering the Black Forest's faerie sites for vis. With Crintera, Irencillia and Fengheld, and the Hawthorn and Elder Gilds, behind the charge, Durenmar is fined a rook of vis to every other covenant and barred from faerie-site vis for fourteen years unless it makes peace with the fay; no such peace has ever been made.

diary.title: Triamore founded
diary.details: The newly risen Apple Gild founds Triamore at the court of Conrad III; Oculus Septentrionalis takes up the Gild as well.

diary.title: Redcap Ioanna murdered in Trier (1290 AA)
diary.details: The Redcap Ioanna is murdered in Trier; Treverorum denies all knowledge and a Quaesitorial investigation is ordered.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1297 AA: Oculus Septentrionalis fined
diary.details: The magi of Oculus Septentrionalis are found to have broken their charter: no site, no investigation, and still living in their old sancta. Each is fined three pawns of vis and ordered out of the old sancta within a year, with a permanent site to be found before the next Tribunal; two Jerbiton join them.

diary.title: Xantippes convicted of meddling (1297 AA)
diary.details: Xantippes of Jerbiton is found guilty of major mundane meddling, having worked Mentem magic of his own devising on the people of Trier for gain, to the harm of the Order's standing and perhaps a cause of Ioanna's death. He is fined ten pawns, his fortune is shared equally among the Tribunal's covenants and he owes three seasons' scribing to the Great Library.

diary.title: Agnes claims to have seen Merinita
diary.details: Agnes of Irencillia tells the Tribunal she has seen the Founder Merinita in Bohemia; few believe her.

diary.title: Hildegard of Bingen a Larta of Jerbiton
diary.details: Hildegard of Bingen is said to have been taken into House Jerbiton about this year as an unGifted maga under its protection and tutelage; she never attends a Tribunal and meets few magi, and the tale is unconfirmed.

diary.title: Oculus Septentrionalis settles in Lübeck
diary.details: About 1160 three magi of Oculus Septentrionalis settle in Henry the Lion's new city of Lübeck; Axior leaves them.

diary.title: Fifteenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The Rhine again loses the Polish boundary dispute to Novgorod, as the New Slavonic Tribunal is now called.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1304 AA: the Lübeck charter
diary.details: Oculus Septentrionalis announces its new seat at Lübeck, and the Quaesitores force additions to its charter, among them that it admit only Gentle-Gifted magi.

diary.title: Treverorum fined fifty pawns (1304 AA)
diary.details: A Quaesitorial inquiry into the unrest in Trier finds Treverorum guilty of interfering with mundanes and the Church to the possible harm of its sodales; it is fined fifty pawns, payable by the next Tribunal, and ordered to repair its relations with the town.

diary.title: Terschelling founded
diary.details: Axior of Flambeau founds Terschelling on the Frisian island of that name. He dies in a magical accident within twenty years.

diary.title: Urgen Primus of Bjornaer
diary.details: Urgen takes the Primacy of House Bjornaer, which he holds through the Danish conquest of Rügen until 1203.

diary.title: Gathering of Twelve Years
diary.details: Jon Arnsson takes the Seat of the Stag on Crintera's council, a year before the Danes land on Rügen.

diary.title: Crintera enters Winter
diary.details: Valdemar I of Denmark conquers Rügen and Bishop Absolon breaks the temple of Arkona the next year. Over the Wilderists' objections Crintera chooses to wait the Danes out; the covenant falls into crisis and the Winter it has lived in for fifty years begins.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1311 AA: Treverorum abolished
diary.details: Scholastus of Jerbiton declares himself Treverorum's last survivor and the covenant is abolished; he calls Trier unsafe for magi because of its churchmen, gives no details and leaves for the Greater Alps. The fine is partly unpaid, so he is held liable and a Redcap request follows him. No one from Crintera attends.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1318 AA: Wizard's War on Prudentum
diary.details: Primus Urgen of Bjornaer charges Oculus Septentrionalis with aiding the Danish invasion of Rügen but offers no proof. Failing, he declares Wizard's War on its leader Prudentum of Jerbiton and kills him.

diary.title: Luctatio's crimes laid before the Tribunal
diary.details: Eule of Fengheld lays before the gathering her evidence that magi of Luctatio in the Roman Tribunal helped Milan beat Barbarossa at Legnano and that a necromancer of Vardian's Tomb made the plague that stopped his army before Rome.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1325 AA: Rügen and the Guardians ruling
diary.details: The Hawthorn Gild invokes the Guardians of the Forest ruling to strike back at the Danes on Rügen, with the Ash and, unexpectedly, the Elder Gilds in support. The Tribunal splits along factional lines and reaches no decision beyond a promised inquiry, so Crintera is refused leave to expel the Danes; several Bjornaer are prosecuted afterwards for attacking Danish settlers.

diary.title: Avarret Primus of Bonisagus
diary.details: Avarret becomes Primus of House Bonisagus and turns the House back to the conservative refinement of existing theory.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1333 AA: no wilderness invaded
diary.details: Held a year late because of the Grand Tribunal. Falke of Fengheld pleads passionately for Crintera to be allowed to resist the Danes, but Quaesitor Caecilius rules that no wilderness has been invaded or destroyed, Crintera's forest standing intact; the Guardians ruling is much narrowed and Crintera falls into factional infighting.

diary.title: Sixteenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Five magi of the Roman Tribunal are Marched over the Luctatio affair.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1339 AA: Rheinstein falls
diary.details: Horst of Mercere reports Rheinstein attacked and destroyed by an army of angry mundanes led by the archbishop of Trier, its magi's fate unknown; their own conduct drew the attention that undid them. The Tribunal bans all magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years.

diary.title: Terschelling turns to piracy
