diary.details: Eric Ribecus and Hygwald Veritas join Terschelling and about this year kill a pirate chief and seize his three ships and their crews; the covenant takes to piracy, and Imanitos Mendax spends some years there as a guest soon after.

diary.title: Gathering of Twelve Years: Falke Prima
diary.details: Urgen resigns the Primacy of House Bjornaer but keeps the Seat of the Bear; Falke of Fengheld is elected Prima and takes the Seat of the Wolf.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1346 AA: Waddenzee
diary.details: Eric Ribecus and Hygwald Veritas announce they are the only magi left at Terschelling, rename it Waddenzee and change its charter and symbol. A Quaesitorial inquiry finds no wrongdoing, and a motion to treat it as a new covenant needing the Tribunal's leave narrowly fails, the Oak and Ash Gilds voting it down.

diary.title: Rethra abolished (1346 AA)
diary.details: The Tribunal declares the Slavic covenant of Rethra abolished, nothing having been heard from its magi for decades; the Knights of the Sword had lately desecrated and plundered its site.

diary.title: St Georgen destroyed
diary.details: The monastery of St Georgen in the Black Forest is destroyed and its monks found dead among dark vines; Dankmar is suspected.

diary.title: God of Truth preached in Bohemia
diary.details: Over the last decade the religion of the God of Truth, preached by the prophet Iacob, spreads near the Bohemian Forest.

diary.title: Murion named Prima of Bonisagus
diary.details: Before his Final Twilight Primus Avarret names Murion his successor, passing over the better-qualified but 'too dangerous' Occultes and keeping the conservative line in charge of the House.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1214: St Georgen
diary.details: The latest Rhine gathering raises the destruction of St Georgen; Jiphella, Dankmar's only delegate, denies any part in it, and a close vote declines to investigate.

diary.title: Heorot founded on Zealand
diary.details: Three Rhine magi found Heorot on the Danish island of Zealand, on the site of Hrothgar's hall, in what is formally Novgorod's territory; Theoderich of Jerbiton leaves Oculus Septentrionalis to join them. It means to ask the Tribunal of 1221 for membership.

diary.title: The Gorge ban lapses
diary.details: The twenty-year ban on magic in the Rhine Gorge runs out. Durenmar's leadership, with no covenant founded for decades and Fengheld's chapters multiplying, sponsors newly Gauntleted magi to survey the Gorge's lost sites and found a new Middle Rhine covenant.

diary.title: Fengheld's Lusatia chapter and the border
diary.details: Fengheld, having been refused leave to sponsor daughter covenants of young Tremere, has lately founded a chapter house in Lusatia, ten miles from the agreed Novgorod border, provoking the latest boundary dispute between the two Tribunals; it has also loosened its Transylvanian ties, and Rudolph of Bonisagus proposes a Fengheld chapter at Durenmar itself.

diary.title: Fengheld's new masters and journeymen
diary.details: Imanitos Mendax attains Master rank at Fengheld, Beechleaf joins its main site, Felecia, Dorana's apprentice, passes her Gauntlet and Garrinchus is newly Gauntleted at the Rheingasse chapter.

diary.title: The Nebelkönigin stolen
diary.details: Waddenzee's pirates have lately taken the ship Nebelkönigin, with vis and books aboard, from Oculus Septentrionalis; as the Quaesitores had forbidden the trading venture she carried, the covenant cannot lawfully pursue her.

diary.title: Caprea blinds a peace envoy's familiar
diary.details: At Crintera the guest maga Caprea blinds the familiar of Carolus of Oculus Septentrionalis, sent as a peace envoy, and the two covenants' feud worsens.

gilds.name: Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The oldest and largest gild, a quarter of the Tribunal: tradition, respect for elders and the Founders, the Rhine's old glory. Led by Murion of Durenmar; Bonisagus, Guernicus and Tremere favour it.

gilds.name: Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The smallest: protects the wild places and beasts from mundanes and shuns contact with them. Led by Urgen of Crintera; mostly Wilderist Bjornaer.

gilds.name: Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Dominion over the land, a forthright Order, and (unspoken) war on the Order of Odin. Led by Philippus Niger of Durenmar; Flambeau, Tremere and Tytalus.

gilds.name: Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Split from the Hawthorn: the fae and friendship with them above all. Led by Iacob of Irencillia; nearly all of Irencillia and Dankmar, with a few Harmonist Bjornaer.

gilds.name: Linden Gild (Lindengilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Founded after the Schism War by former Fengheld magi: co-operation, peace and an end to apathy; nearly a fifth of the Tribunal, the go-between. Led by Occultes of Durenmar; Mercere, Jerbiton, Verditius, Tremere and Trianoma's Bonisagus.

gilds.name: Apple Gild (Apfelgilde)
gilds.dues: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The newest and weakest: friendship with mundanes, acceptance, humility before God. Led by Henri de Tours of Oculus Septentrionalis, Wilhelm Weiss of Fengheld and Daria la Gris of Triamore.

neighbours.name: The Rhine Valley and Lorraine
neighbours.summary:
The river country from Basel, where the Rhine turns north and ships begin to sail it, down past Strassburg, Speyer, Worms and Mainz to Cologne and the marshy delta about Utrecht and Deventer, together with the lands west of it: the Vosges, Upper Lorraine round Metz, Toul and Verdun, and Lower Lorraine with Aachen, Liege and the Ardennes on the Tribunal's western fringe.

This is the oldest settled part of Germany, built on Roman colonies and legionary camps, and the Church is strongest here: the cathedral of Mainz has a Divine aura of 7 as a Holy See, those of Speyer, Worms, Trier, Aachen and Cologne 6, and most cities 3. Trade along the river makes its archbishops rich and its cities large; the Jewish communities of Mainz, Speyer and Worms are the greatest in Germany.

The Middle Rhine between Mainz and Koblenz, the Mosel and the Lahn belong to the Rhine Gorge and its curse, which the saga chapter describes.

The Rhine was Rome's frontier, and its west bank is the oldest settled land in Germany: Trier, Mainz, Worms, Speyer, Strassburg and Cologne all began as Roman towns, and Trier was an imperial capital under Constantine. The Burgundians held Worms from 413 until the Huns destroyed them, the matter of the Nibelungenlied, and the Merovingian Franks ruled Austrasia from Metz before Charlemagne made Aachen his seat and Boniface made Mainz the Church's centre for all Germany. The Treaty of Verdun in 843 left the river's western lands as Lotharingia, long disputed between the kingdoms, and the Salian emperors made Speyer their favourite seat and resting place. The First and Second Crusades brought massacres of the Jews of Worms, Speyer, Mainz, Cologne and Trier, and in 1122 the Concordat of Worms ended the Investiture Contest. Today the three archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier rule the valley with the prince-bishops and the Count Palatine, Cologne is the greatest city of the empire, and robber-baron castles live off the tolls of the Gorge.

neighbours.name: The Black Forest
neighbours.summary:
The largest forest of western Europe fills the south-west of the Tribunal: over a hundred miles north to south and up to forty across, all hills under an unbroken canopy, with the Rhine plain to the west and the Neckar and the Swabian uplands to the east. Oak and beech grow on the lower slopes and fringes; in the centre and on the heights the fir stands so thick that no sunlight reaches the floor. There are no clearings, little level ground, a few villages at the edges and about a dozen monasteries drawn by the seclusion.

A Faerie aura of 3 lies over the whole forest, broken only by the Divine islands of its monasteries and a few Magic sites: Durenmar, the Fane of the Founders and the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls. Bears, boars and deer share it with stranger beasts; bockmen, goblins and giant bats hunt by night, villagers who go too deep vanish, and the few folk living inside are said to be half fay. Only the old Roman road crosses it; anywhere else is weeks on foot.

The forest was once the south-western part of the Hercynian Forest, cut off when the Romans built the limes, and its spirit split with it. The Cult of Mercury bound the greater part by its own oath-magic into what is now the Fane of the Founders, and the peaceful remnant withdrew to the Glade; a rebellious splinter fled south, dwindled, and regrew on mortal fear as the dark faerie King of the Black Mountain (Faerie, Might 90), who now rules every dark court of the forest. Since Durenmar's condemnation in 1151 the forest has been a hazard to magi, and no peace with the fay was ever made. The Swabian lands east of the forest, the Jura and the sources of the Danube, belong to this region too.

The Black Forest was the south-western part of the great Hercynian Forest until the Roman limes and the Black Forest Road of the first century cut it off; the Romans held its edges and never its heart. It became part of the duchy of Swabia, and from the eleventh century the Zähringen dukes cleared and settled its fringes, founding Freiburg in 1120, while Hirsau (1059) and its daughter houses such as St Georgen (1084) planted monasteries in its seclusion. The Hohenstaufen rose from their castle on the Kaiserberge nearby, and Barbarossa made Ulm a Free Imperial City in 1164. With the death of the last Zähringen duke in 1218 much of the forest's lordship passed to the Hohenstaufen; its interior remains unbroken wilderness, and the monasteries within it suffer attacks no one can explain.

neighbours.name: The Lowlands
neighbours.summary:
The northern third of Germany, flat and much alike from end to end: from the North Sea eastward the Frisian islands and the Wadden Sea, then swamp and moor, then some two hundred miles of farmland with prosperous cities and few forests, reaching Saxony, Westphalia, Holstein and the Baltic coast about Lübeck.

Its cities are ruled by trade rather than by princes. The southern ones were founded by Charlemagne after he conquered the Saxons or grew from missionary bishoprics; the northern ports are newer, rich, and reaching for Free Imperial status, though Holstein and Pomerania lie for the moment under King Valdemar II of Denmark.

Magi here feel themselves on a Hermetic frontier: most know of some Scandinavian wizard beyond the border, Lübeck is the Redcaps' usual stop toward Novgorod, and the Divine auras run a little weaker toward the Baltic than in the Rhineland.

Hermann's destruction of Varus's legions in the Teutoburger Forest kept Rome out of the north, and the Saxons and Frisians held it as pagans until Charlemagne conquered the Saxons in the late eighth century and planted missionary bishoprics at Bremen, Münster, Paderborn, Hildesheim and the rest. Vikings founded Haithabu and burned Hamburg in 845, and the Poles burned it again in 1030; the coast stayed a frontier. In the twelfth century Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony, made Lübeck a city (1157) and built up Brunswick, until Barbarossa broke his duchy in 1180 and divided its lands. The northern towns have since grown rich on trade: Hamburg became a Free Imperial City in 1189 and Lübeck's merchants have traded at Novgorod since 1205, but Valdemar II of Denmark took Holstein in 1201 and occupied Hamburg in 1216, and holds the coast with Frederick II's acknowledgement.

neighbours.name: Central Germany
neighbours.summary:
The heart of Germany and of the Empire: from the Harz on the edge of Saxony down through Thuringia and Franconia to the Danube, and the smaller part of Bavaria north of the river that was never Roman and belongs to the Rhine Tribunal (the Danube cities, Regensburg chief among them, are claimed by the Greater Alps).

Rolling hills, rocky isolated wildernesses and countless magic and faerie forests of every size, only moderately peopled. Its cities are younger than the Roman ones of the Rhine but weigh heavily in trade and imperial politics, and its courts and cathedrals have grown a distinctly German culture: the Wartburg's minnesänger, Nuremberg's imperial castle, the great abbeys of Fulda and Hersfeld.

Fengheld, the Tribunal's largest covenant, sits in the eastern Harz, and the Harz, the Kyffhäuser and the Thuringian Forest hold some of the strongest spirits of the old Hercynian Forest.

The heart of Germany, from the Harz to the Danube, was pagan country until Boniface felled the Donar Oak and planted the Church at Erfurt, Würzburg and Hersfeld in the eighth century, and Charlemagne founded Frankfurt, which became the capital of the eastern Franks under Louis the German in 843. Henry the Fowler and the Ottonians ruled from Saxony, Henry II made Bamberg a bishopric in 1007 and set out to build a second Rome there, and the silver of the Harz enriched Goslar. The Wartburg, founded in 1067, became under Landgrave Hermann I of Thuringia (1190 to 1217) the centre of German song, where Walther von der Vogelweide won the singers' contest of 1204. The Hohenstaufen enlarged and fortified Frankfurt, where imperial elections are now held, and the Wittelsbachs have ruled Bavaria since 1180; Frederick II's court has visited Erfurt four times since 1214 and held its last German Diet for many years at Frankfurt in 1220.

neighbours.name: The Eastern Marches
neighbours.summary:
The lands between the Elbe and the Oder: lakes and forest, thinly settled, with the reputation of a home of werewolves, witches and giants and the decaying temples of the Slavic gods. Christianity came in the tenth century from the frontier bishoprics of Magdeburg and Merseburg; since then war and peace with the Slavs have alternated, German settlers have poured in, and German speech now prevails.

Meissen in the south-west is wholly German, Lusatia in the south-east mostly Sorbian, and Rügen and Pomerania in the north a mixture under Danish overlords. Land is so plentiful that the local rulers seldom quarrel with one another. Nearly every pagan or magical site of the southern Marches has been destroyed; more survive in Pomerania.

Apart from Crintera the Order has little presence here, but the Rhine Tribunal claims the Marches firmly, disputes its eastern border with the Novgorod Tribunal, and would gladly push further into Polish lands. The Baltic freezes for months every winter and must be thawed each spring by a ritual cast at Arkona.

The Marches between the Elbe and the Oder were Slavic lands, and Christianity came only in the tenth century from the frontier bishoprics of Magdeburg, Merseburg, Brandenburg (948) and Meissen (963), after Henry the Fowler fortified Meissen in 929; the Slavic counter-attack later that century briefly undid the work. Since then war and peace with the Slavs have alternated with intermarriage and heavy German colonisation: the Wettins have ruled Meissen since 1089, Albert the Bear founded the March of Brandenburg in 1150, and the Saxon crusade of 1147 fell on the Wends of Pomerania. Valdemar I of Denmark conquered Rügen in 1168 and broke the temple of Arkona, Barbarossa made Bogislaw duke of Pomerania in 1181, and the Knights of the Sword, founded in 1202, crusade along the Baltic. Meissen is now wholly German, Lusatia mostly Sorb, and Rügen and Pomerania a mixed people under Danish overlords, with land so plentiful that the lords rarely quarrel.

neighbours.name: Bohemia and Moravia
neighbours.summary:
The Tribunal's south-east: the subject kingdom of Bohemia and its March of Moravia, broad half-wooded plains along the upper Elbe and its tributaries, ringed and divided by long wooded mountain chains. There are no great cities, only modest towns thinly spread, and in 1220 the only notable ones lie about and north of Prague.

The Premyslid dynasty, descended from the legendary Czech, has ruled since the eighth century; Christianity came in the ninth with St Methodius and took generations to root. Barbarossa raised the duchy to a kingdom a generation ago, and King Otakar reigns now as a semi-independent tributary of the Empire. Farming, hunting, mining, glass, brewing and horse-breeding are its trades.

Moravia is the Empire's easternmost reach, bordering Hungary and the Transylvanian Tribunal, whose influence, especially House Tremere's, the magi here feel often. Irencillia, the domus magna of Merinita, hides in the Bohemian Forest, and Roznov holds the Carpathian border.

Bohemia has been ruled since the eighth century by the Premyslids, the line the Gifted princess Libuse founded when her vision at Vysehrad chose the ploughman Premysl as her husband. Christianity came in the ninth century with St Methodius and took generations to root; Duke Wenceslaus was murdered by his pagan brother early in the tenth, and the bishopric of Prague was created under Mainz in 973. Moravia passed to Poland in 999 and to Bohemia in 1019, and the kingdom has since been a semi-independent tributary of the empire, suffering Hungarian attacks early in the twelfth century, while Strahov (1140) and Sedlec (1142) brought the new monastic orders. Barbarossa raised the duchy to a subject kingdom a generation ago; King Otakar rules from Prague, and silver newly found at Sedlec promises to change a land of modest towns.

neighbours.name: The Hercynian Forest
neighbours.summary:
The primeval oak forest the Romans found beyond the Alps, nine days wide and of a length nobody knew, covering all of Germania. It had a single vast spirit of the Magic realm (Magic, Might not given), a reflection of the Ideal Forest that some magi call Eden. The rituals of the Cult of Mercury, who guided the legions in building the limes and its magically linked roads, and later St Boniface's felling of the Donar Oak in the eighth century, shattered that spirit into the genii loci of today's forests.

Each fragment met one of four fates: survival as a Magic forest (the Teutoburger Forest, the Drudenbaum, the Romowe oak), dissolution into a mundane wood (the Hertogenwald), replacement by a being of another realm, usually Faerie (the Black Forest, the Ash of Nortorf, the Donar Oak), or alliance with a faerie (the Four Seasonal Courts). The forests have hardly shrunk since Charlemagne's day and resist clearance as if by will. Each still holds a direct link to the Magic realm, the primal power that drew the Cult of Mercury and Bonisagus himself, and the paths through the forest that House Bjornaer and some Merinita can show lead to it.

neighbours.name: The Four Seasonal Courts
neighbours.summary:
Four linked faerie forests, Holly, Alder, Oak and Willow, that the storyguide places where the saga needs them, ideally in a ring at the cardinal points about the player covenant; the names are conveniences, not true names. They are four fragments of one spirit, perhaps once as strong as the Black Forest's, each too weak to live alone and each allied with or possessing a faerie lord. The aura of each is Faerie, rising to 3 across the whole wood at its court's solstice or equinox and shrinking month by month to nearly nothing at the opposite season; patches of Magic aura linger in the Oak Forest, and every ruler has the Regio power (levels not given).

King Holly (Faerie, Might 40, pool 20 to 50; north, winter; Tyrannical +3, Cold-hearted +2) rules a court of ice and frost faeries from a holly grove by an iron will and a detailed law; the spirit forcibly possessed a rebellious winter faerie. The Alder Prince (Faerie, Might 40; west, spring; Compassionate +3, Secretive +2) is red-hued, shy and benign, keeps a shrouded court in a serene vale and rules many holzfrauen. King Oak (Faerie, Might 40; south, summer; Regal +3, Generous +2) holds court under a great oak as a generous host whose honour is touchy and who takes words literally, so a slip binds a guest in an enforced contract. The Willow Maiden (Faerie, Might 40; east, autumn; Manipulative +3, Uncaring +2) seems generous but every gift has a hidden price; she has slipped the spirit's pact and all but owns her wood, and is obsessed with the Alder Prince.

The courts are bound in a yearly drama of stolen power in which the coming season's court raids the reigning one: in December Holly at full strength slays Oak, who is reborn in his forest; in March Alder heals the Willow Maiden's malice with love and she flees home; in June Oak captures Holly and imprisons him in the heart of the Holly Forest; in September the Willow Maiden weds and drowns the Alder Prince in her river. Each ruler keeps Might 40 for resistance and Penetration all year while its pool swings by five a month. Summer against Winter is open war; Spring against Autumn is subtle politics and should pay better, and vis is the obvious wage for taking a side.

neighbours.name: The castle of Triamore
neighbours.summary: A castle and manorial estate on the river Meuse at the edge of the Ardennes, in Lower Lorraine on the western fringe of the Tribunal, with Liege and Verdun the nearest towns of note. The Magic aura is 2. Redcaps bound between the Rhine and Normandy Tribunals make it, with Verdun, their usual meeting point.

neighbours.name: The Rhinefalls
neighbours.summary:
The greatest falls of Europe, five hundred feet wide and eighty high, on the Upper Rhine below Constance near the south-eastern edge of the Black Forest. In their midst stands a rock island taller than the falls with a copse on top; it can be reached only by boat from downstream (Profession: Boating against 9) and climbed only on slippery rock (Athletics against 12), and the summit is a deafening place of raw elemental power. The island's Magic aura is 2, rising to 4 at the summit, and a regio of several levels climbs from it.

Under the rock lies the Spirit of the Rhine (Magic, Might not given), a river elemental pinned there long ago when the Nibelungs, dwarves and giants tamed the wild river; it is said to guard the Rhinegold in revenge. Those who climb the rock and hurl valuables into the maelstrom find the smashed fragments washed up downstream later, each worth a pawn of Aquam vis; it is never found by accident.

Secrets
Schwall's final Quest is to free the Rhine elemental and merge his mind with it, a kind of immortality before Final Twilight takes him; the floods that would wreck shipping, towns and cities along the whole river are to him a welcome bonus. The early signs are disturbances on the river. The Tribunal would March anyone involved, but he expects to be beyond its reach.

details.tethers: The Spirit of the Rhine pinned beneath the rock

levels.name: The lower levels of the rock
levels.enter: Climbing alone cannot enter the regio; powerful magic is needed
levels.notes:
Several levels rise with the climb; their auras are not given.

Secrets
Schwall of Bjornaer, an elderly Wilderist of the Hawthorn Gild formerly of Rheinstein, keeps a hidden sanctum here. His heartbeast is believed a fish, he can also become a mass of water, and his many Twilight Scars leave him always wet. He has completed several Quests for the Rhine spirit.

levels.name: The elemental summit
levels.enter: Powerful magic; no climb reaches it
levels.notes: A turbulent realm of raw elemental water (aura not given). The Rhinegold and the other treasures hurled into the falls over the centuries may lie here.

neighbours.name: Mount Saint Odile
neighbours.summary: The Hohenburg, a convent two and a half thousand feet up in the northern Vosges on the Alsace side, founded by St Odile, who was born blind and given sight at her baptism by her uncle St Erhard; a rock opened to hide her from her father Duke Adalric, who afterwards gave her the castle. Small chapels, Odile's crypt and an ancient Merovingian cemetery stand on the summit. Below the convent the spring she struck with her cane cures the sick, above all diseases of the eye, and has a Divine aura of 4 (the convent's own is not given). She died in 720 and pilgrims have come ever since.

neighbours.name: Thann Chapel
neighbours.summary:
A chapel of 1161 in the southern Vosges about a dozen miles west of Mulhouse, built over the staff of the servant of Bishop Theobald of Gubbio, who had hidden his dead master's ring and thumb inside it; the staff rooted itself in the fir forest under three lights and could not be moved. The lord of the nearby Engelburg raised the chapel, a village grew about it, and the Engelburg peasants ceremonially burn three fir trees before it each summer. Its Divine aura is 3 and it draws pilgrims.

Secrets
The Vosges once had a secretive fir spirit like the Black Forest's. Villages, monasteries and felling wore it down, and the planting of the holy staff extinguished it, which is why no continuous Vosges forest remains. If the staff were removed it might be the one artefact able to counter the spirit of the Black Forest.

details.tethers: The rooted staff of Bishop Theobald's servant beneath the altar

neighbours.name: The Sanctuary of Hercules
neighbours.summary: A hidden cave on the isolated western slopes of the Vosges where three spring-fed pools lie in a Magic aura of 3. The Gauls kept it as a shrine to Ogmios, god of strength, eloquence and poetry; the Romans recast him as Hercules and built a Greek-columned shrine. Grateful petitioners left altar stones in a ring about the pools, and they stand there still for whoever finds the place.

neighbours.name: Andresina
neighbours.summary: An abandoned Roman city in Upper Lorraine, two dozen miles south-west of Toul, built round a great temple of Apollo and its sacred pool, fed by miles of piping; the emperors Caracalla and Constantine both visited. The temple ruins, a half-oval amphitheatre, a crumbling basilica with a mosaic floor, underground chambers and an old rampart remain, with a small village beside it. The Magic aura is 2 and would likely rise if the temple were restored; the book suggests it as a covenant site.

neighbours.name: The Vosges Mountains
neighbours.summary:
The range on the west bank of the Upper Rhine facing the Black Forest, as high as it and fir-clad on the upper slopes, but not wholly forested: villages lie among the hills. The southern peaks are rounded granite, the northern hills red sandstone. Many springs, some of them hot, feed the tributaries of the Mosel, and the storks that arrive each spring are thought lucky. The mountains have no general aura; Mount Saint Odile, Thann Chapel and the Sanctuary of Hercules are its sites.

Secrets
The fir spirit of the Vosges is extinct, put out by the holy staff at Thann.

neighbours.name: Burg Trifels
neighbours.summary: An eleventh-century Hohenstaufen fortress on the crag of the Sonnenberg at the edge of the Palatinate Forest, twenty miles west of Speyer, and Barbarossa's favourite castle; it has never been taken. Henry VI held Richard the Lionheart prisoner here in 1193 for a ransom of 150,000 marks. It has a large dungeon and one of the Empire's greatest treasuries. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Schwanenburg
neighbours.summary: The Swan Castle on its steep hill over Cleves on the Lower Rhine, named for Lohengrin, the Knight of the Swan, who came in a barge drawn by a swan to defeat Telramund for the widowed Duchess Elsa of Brabant, married her on condition she never ask his name, and left when she did, as Wolfram von Eschenbach tells in Parzival. The lords of Cleves bear a swan in their arms. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Hertogenwald
neighbours.summary: A forest south of Aachen in Lower Lorraine, and the book's example of a Hercynian fragment that dissolved: farmland and the strong Divine aura of Aachen drained its spirit away, and it is now a mundane wood with no aura at all.

neighbours.name: Heiliger Sand
neighbours.summary: The vast and ancient Jewish cemetery just outside the west walls of Worms, elaborate in its stones, overgrown and deserted except at the newest plots, since the dead are left in peace. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Rheingasse
neighbours.summary: Fengheld's chapter house in the centre of Cologne, a city house in the Rheingasse near the market, where two Gentle-Gifted magi of the Apple Gild very ably arrange the covenant's supplies and its dealings with the mundane world. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The valley of Durenmar
neighbours.summary:
A steep-sided hidden valley some fifteen miles inside the northern Black Forest, about fifteen miles south of Hirsau monastery, with Baden to the north-west. A guard post lower down is enchanted to hide the three-mile track up to it, and the covenant's towers stand below the surrounding treeline. The clearing on the valley floor, split by a stream and unfortified, has a Magic aura of 7 and is protected by the strongest Aegis of the Hearth in the Order; the Cult of Mercury's temple stood here before Bonisagus came in 754. Caves of unknown extent run under the north cliffs, with wild rumours of enslaved gnomes mining gems.

Covenfolk born in the aura all carry Warping, and their longevity is unexplained. A lone fir near the Great Library, the Black Fir, is tolerated for the Perdo vis of its cones; the great vine on the Tower of Bonisagus yields Intellego vis in its sap.

Secrets
The Black Fir was planted over a century ago by the King of the Black Mountain at the edge of the Aegis after his direct attacks failed; when the magi found it gave vis they moved the Aegis boundary to take it in, breaching their own defence. It creeps about six inches a year toward the Tower of Bonisagus, and nobody alive remembers it being young. What happens when it reaches the tower or the vine is unknown but likely severe.

neighbours.name: The hollow of Dankmar
neighbours.summary: The dampest and darkest part of the Black Forest, about forty miles south-west of Durenmar and a few miles south of the Black Forest Road, where the fir stands so thick that noon is dusk, only fungi grow on the poisoned carpet of needles and only ravens call. The Faerie aura is 5. A circular palisade of split logs encloses wooden huts and four stone towers whose cellars join caves beneath, fir and yew lean over the walls, and every wooden thing glows with phosphorescent bracket fungi day and night. For at least a mile about it a version of The Shrouded Glen (level 40, Penetration 20) turns travellers away in nameless dread, and bockmen (Faerie, Might 20) patrol the surroundings by pact with Orphedra.

neighbours.name: The Black Forest Road
neighbours.summary: The only road across the forest, from Offenburg up the Kinzig valley to Rottweil, built in the first century under Vespasian by the Eighth Legion under Cornelius Clemens to shorten the way from Strassburg to Augsburg. Mercurian priests raised magical milestones along it that still ward off the forest's supernatural denizens, so wise travellers camp beside them. The paving is weathered and overgrown but it remains the one way to bring a cart through; the central stretch of nearly thirty miles between Gengenbach monastery and the village of Waldmoessingen on its ruined Roman fort has no human dwelling and takes two days, so one night in the forest cannot be avoided. Bockmen (Faerie, Might 20) lurk along it, and Dankmar lies a few miles to the south. Its own aura is not given; the forest's Faerie 3 lies over it.

details.tethers: The Mercurian milestones that ward off the forest's faeries

neighbours.name: The Feldberg and the Hoellental
neighbours.summary:
The highest peak of the southern Black Forest, reached only through the Hoellental, and the seat of the King of the Black Mountain, King Fir (Faerie, Might 90; Malicious +5, Secretive +3, Vengeful +3), pictured as a huge black-cloaked man with a terrible face. He commands the weather, grants flaws such as depression, fear, lameness and loss of direction, possesses, shrouds and holds a regio of several levels with Faerie auras from 3 to 8; victory and virtue he grants very rarely. He is the dread and undisputed ruler of every dark faerie court in the forest, and his influence covers all of it. Monasteries inside the forest suffer his attacks: vanishing monks, blight, landslides and earthquakes.

Secrets
His dominion cannot reach the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls or the Fane of the Founders; lacking the original spirit's nature, they are unknowable to him. He craves revenge on those who bound the old spirit and wants to be whole again, so he seeks Durenmar's destruction: were it to fall, the rite of the Fane would lapse and the bound spirit would be his to dominate and absorb. The raid of 1085 was his, and its captives never returned; the Black Fir at Durenmar is his centuries-long plan.

details.tethers: The great dark fir on the summit, King Fir

levels.name: The Hoellental
levels.notes: Hell Valley, a haunted winding valley climbing from the centre of the forest, the only way to the mountain; the lowest of the regio's several levels, whose auras run from 3 to 8.

levels.name: The Black Mountain
levels.notes: The bare summit with its one great dark fir, King Fir: no mortal who sees it ever leaves the forest. Beneath lies a vast dungeon where hundreds of enslaved humans who strayed too deep toil without end.

neighbours.name: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls
neighbours.summary: At the exact centre of the Black Forest, in a place nobody has found or admitted finding, a stream falls through a precipitous valley over seven waterfalls, and the one way up is a narrow path beside the water through hazel and beech. The regio has seven levels, one for each fall, and the Spirit of the Glade (Magic, Might 80; Enigmatic +4, Wise +3), the peaceful female remnant of the forest's original genius locus, lets a climber past each fall only after a Quest; she guides, swears oaths, shrouds and grants clear thought. Each ascent brings a deeper understanding of the Forest and the top a complete one, at the price of escalating Sacrifices such as parts of one's Hermetic magic. The Hercynian lineage of Bonisagus held it the place the Mercurian priests and Bonisagus sought; some prophesy godlike power for a destined finder, others guess the spirit has faded and been replaced by a powerful maga in Final Twilight, perhaps the Founder Merinita. The bell of St Georgen was carried here, and the forest took its revenge on the monastery. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The Spirit of the Glade, the peaceful remnant of the forest's spirit

levels.name: The first waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The second waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The third waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The fourth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The fifth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The sixth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given). The top level gives a complete and harmonious understanding.

neighbours.name: The Fane of the Founders
neighbours.summary:
A quiet glade not far from Durenmar, its whereabouts hidden by powerful magic, with a twelve-sided stone slab at its centre and a Magic aura of 6. Here the Oath of the Founders was composed and sworn, and every seven years during the Rhine Tribunal twelve magi, one of each House, come secretly to renew the Founders' vows in a rite believed to preserve the Order; they leave with vis as their reward, and the place encourages clear and calm thought. Only the Primi and their chosen know it exists, though most Durenmar magi know of it, and all who have sought it have failed. It is older than the Order: many truces were made here, among them one between Germanic chiefs and a Roman general that fixed the Empire's northern limit. The rite was skipped only at the Tribunals of 997, 1004 and 1011 and resumed in 1018 with an Ex Miscellanea magus in Diedne's place. Rumour says the attendees met Hermes himself, or a powerful faerie posing as him who extracted a terrible service from the Founders.

Secrets
The Fane is an artefact into which the Cult of Mercury bound much of the Black Forest's original magical essence by a great ritual. It behaves as a spirit of Magic Might 60 with limited forest powers: it produces vis, shrouds, swears oaths and grants clear thought for a time. The rite must be renewed regularly or the spirit escapes the stone, which the King of the Black Mountain hopes for so that he may seize it.

details.tethers: The twelve-sided stone slab and the spirit bound in it

neighbours.name: Mummel Lake
neighbours.summary: An enchanted and isolated lake deep under the mountains near Seebach. A Nixe (Faerie, Might not given), a water-nymph, lives in it and now and then visits the nearby settlements to bewitch a young man with her beauty; she must return every night, and the jealous elemental spirits of the lake (realm and Might not given) kill any mortal who follows her home. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Source of the Danube
neighbours.summary: In the eastern Black Forest an enchanted spring runs from a crack in the rock into a small pool, deceptively deep, which is the source of the Danube. The Faerie aura is 3 about the pool and 5 within the water. Unlike the Rhine's, the river's spirit is a faerie: Danu (Faerie, Might not given), once a goddess of countless peoples before Rome, whose power fades elsewhere but is strong here. The pool seems bottomless because of the regio; at its top level, with Faerie aura 10, lies the true bottom and a gateway into Arcadia. Vast Aquam vis could be taken here, at the near-certain cost of Danu's anger.

details.tethers: Danu, the river's spirit

levels.name: The true bottom
levels.notes: The top level of the regio, where the pool's real floor lies, and a gateway into Arcadia that feeds the river. The levels between are not given.

neighbours.name: The Swabian Jura
neighbours.summary: Harsh limestone hills between the valleys of the Danube and the Neckar, east of the Black Forest, whose defensible peaks the Hohenzollerns and other local lords have forted. They are riddled with stalactite grottos such as the Nebelhoehle, the Misty Cave. On the south side near Zweifalten monastery the Wimsener Hoehle swallows the river Ach, a Danube tributary, which runs underground for a couple of miles through a tunnel that can partly be navigated by boat. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Blautopf
neighbours.summary: A large round pool of startling deep blue at the southern edge of the Swabian Jura beside Kloster Blaubeuren, the source of the little river Blau, with a Faerie aura of 2. It is the home of the Schoene Lau (Faerie, Might not given), a beautiful, reclusive, long-haired water maiden with webbed feet, banished here by her husband, a faerie king of the Black Sea, because she cannot laugh: the future holds no surprise for her. Those who come for wisdom, Blaubeuren's monks among them, bring a modest gift and she foretells their future; her predictions always come true and seldom bring the happiness hoped for. Whoever makes her laugh breaks the curse and earns her eternal gratitude.

neighbours.name: The Limes
neighbours.summary: The Roman frontier fortifications of the first century, whose ramparts, forts and temples lie in ruins along their whole route past Gmuend and through the Odenwald, the Swabian Forest and the Swabian Jura. The Cult of Mercury guided the legions in building it and its magically linked roads, and its building first split the Black Forest and its spirit from the Hercynian Forest. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Kaiserberge
neighbours.summary: Three round wooded hills south of Gmuend in the Stauferland, each topped by a castle: the Hohenstaufen to the west, the lowest and grandest, ancestral seat of the imperial dynasty; the Hohenrechberg; and the Stuifen to the east, the highest. The Stauferland about them is the rolling country between the Swabian Forest and the Swabian Jura, named for the Hohenstaufens. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Terschelling
neighbours.summary: A deserted, weather-beaten island of the Frisian chain on the Wadden Sea, the shallow water the sandy islands enclose, shared by the pirate magi of Waddenzee and many thousands of seabirds whose noise in spring and summer has earned it a name for haunting, which the magi encourage; they have driven off every other settler. The Magic aura is 3 over the covenant building and a few hundred paces about it. A long, low Danish-style long-house sunk partly into the ground houses the covenfolk, four separate magus buildings join its walls by sunken covered walkways, and there is a harbour for the covenant's five ships.

neighbours.name: The Pirates' Graveyards
neighbours.summary:
Dozens of graves marked with standing stones and boulders on a low ridge some fifty feet above the swamp in Drenthe, a couple of dozen miles up the river Ems from its estuary; they are the only stones in Friesland. The pirates of Frisia, Waddenzee's among them, bury their dead here, and the place is haunted. Lucas von Beck of Waddenzee takes vis and corpses from it for his necromancy. The aura is not given and its realm is uncertain.

Secrets
The power here may be Infernal rather than Magic; Lucas has barely considered it.

neighbours.name: Haithabu
neighbours.summary: The old Viking trading city a few miles from the fishing town of Schleswig on the Schlei fjord, founded at the start of the ninth century where the land crossing between Baltic and North Sea is shortest. Only earth ramparts and burial mounds remain, and, the locals say, ghosts. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Ash of Nortorf
neighbours.summary: A small ash seedling in the churchyard of the little town of Nortorf in Holstein, where the roads to Schleswig, Lübeck and Hamburg meet. Every New Year's Night a white rider on a white horse cuts it down while a black rider on a black horse tries and fails to stop him. The prophecy says that one day the black rider will win, the shoot will grow into a tree, and once it is big enough to tether a horse under, a king will come with a great army; while his horse stands under the tree he cannot be beaten and gains fell powers. The tree's spirit (Infernal, Might 15, potentially 60; Ambitious +2) grants victory and the virtues of entrancement, inspiration and toughness; the white horseman is Divine and the black an Infernal agent. Agents of the black rider may tell magi of the ash as a future vis source and not of the prophecy, hoping they will guard it on New Year's Night: if the Divine rider is driven off or killed he never returns. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ash seedling itself

neighbours.name: The Giant's Grave
neighbours.summary: A rectangular bed of stones forty yards by ten in the Everstorf Forest north of Schwerin in Mecklenburg, near Naschendorf. The farmers of the village found a cattle-stealing, crop-trampling giant asleep, rolled him into a huge grave and buried him; his wife dragged stone blocks in her apron to cover it so he could not escape, and he suffocated while she was never seen again. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Teutoburger Forest
neighbours.summary: Forested hills in Westphalia where Hermann's Germans destroyed the Roman legions in the first century and Charlemagne fought in the late eighth, the beachhead of every conqueror and so a wilderness with strong guardians, one of the last on the northern lowlands. At its heart a great clearing is ringed by ancient trees of different kinds that together are the forest's spirit (Magic, Might 50; Patient +3, Unforgiving +1), which grants simple-mindedness and victory, shrouds, holds a regio and keeps the legionaries in stasis. The surviving Romans withdrew into the forest after the battle and vanished; they are trapped in the regio's top level and would make loyal, well-trained grogs for anyone who bargained their release with the trees, unless a renegade magus or hedge wizard hidden in the forest already uses them as his turb. The Externsteine stand on its south-eastern edge. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ring of ancient trees about the great clearing

levels.name: The legionaries' camp
levels.notes: The top level of the regio (its levels are not numbered and their auras not given): a fortified Roman camp in the clearing where the surviving legionaries of Hermann's battle still live, kept from aging and from leaving, free to hunt and forage, heavily Warped and reverent of the trees.

neighbours.name: The Externsteine
neighbours.summary: Thirteen jumbled sandstone rocks, some over a hundred feet tall, in a large clearing on the south-eastern edge of the Teutoburger Forest near Paderborn, with a Divine aura of 4. Once a pagan site, its caves were consecrated as a chapel in 1115; a carving of the Descent from the Cross stands at the foot of one rock, and inside another a bare upper chapel has a window that catches the sunrise of the summer solstice. It is enigmatically peaceful and home to a handful of ascetic hermits.

neighbours.name: The Teufelsmoor
neighbours.summary: A vast swampy waste of dark peat for miles north-east of Bremen, bare of grass and trees, always misted and foul-smelling; strange shapes and lights move in it at night. The locals think it cursed and keep away, though peasants cut peat at its edge for fuel. The book suggests it as an unpleasant but workable covenant site. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Lüneburg Heath
neighbours.summary: A sprawling open heath south of Lüneburg with small woods, a few villagers and shepherds tending Heidschnucken, the goat-like sheep descended from Corsican mouflon brought here about two hundred years ago. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Teufelsküche
neighbours.summary: A forgotten circle of round stones about an ancient altar deep in the Haldensleben Forest north-west of Magdeburg, where Woden was worshipped: tall red-bearded priests in long white cloaks came in the hour before dawn with men in skins and other dark shapes, slaughtered a sacrifice and burned its vitals to greet the day. The missionaries who purged the cult named it the Devil's Kitchen; whether any priest of Woden survives is the storyguide's choice. The Wild Hunt, the troupe of storm and winter faeries led by the Wild Huntsman (Faerie, Might 50) with its Horsemen (Faerie, Might 20 each) and Hounds (Faerie, Might 10 each), rises from here on stormy winter nights, so winter is a bad time to visit. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ancient altar of Woden at the circle's centre

neighbours.name: The northern swamps
neighbours.summary: The bogs and marshes of northern Germany generally, the haunt of the Boglin (Magic, Might 25; Greedy +5, Reclusive +2, Guileful +1): a carapaced sac of a body the size of three men with eight slimy dark-brown tentacles twelve feet long and a toothy maw, lying under murky water and betrayed only by a foul stench and a faint murmuring. It chokes prey with a cloud of stinking gas, paralyses it with venomous barbs, drags it to the maw in three rounds and regrows a lost tentacle each season it hibernates; it is blind, gluttonous and a cunning hunter. Its tentacles hold a pawn of Animal vis each and its brain six of Perdo. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Münsterland
neighbours.summary: The flat, highly fertile plain of Westphalia round Münster, the prosperous market city founded as a monastery in 805 to convert the Saxons. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Heorot on Zealand
neighbours.summary: The site of the hall of Hrothgar, the legendary king of the Danes, on the island of Zealand in the kingdom of Denmark, where Beowulf fought Grendel; Rügen lies not far across the water. Zealand is by tradition Novgorod Tribunal territory, but no covenant of the Order has lasted in Norse lands long enough to attend a Tribunal, so the claim is a grey area the new covenant of Heorot means to exploit. The kin of Grendel (trolls; realm and Might not given) still haunt the island's bogs and have killed fourteen of the covenant's grogs and taken its leader's left arm. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Fengheld House
neighbours.summary: Fengheld's most remote chapter house, a single fortified townhouse in the city of Cherbourg in Normandy, outside the Rhine Tribunal altogether, owned by Sir Jozef of Poznan, a crusader of Polish birth. It runs a small trading business with England and France. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Harz Mountains
neighbours.summary: Germany's northernmost range, fifty miles of high granite hills on the edge of Saxony, a desolate wilderness ringed by the civilised Saxon towns. Wind off the northern plain, rain and fog prevail, and low cloud hides the peaks and cuts them off from the lowlands; the lower slopes are gloomy forest with strange hidden rocks, whispering streams, lakes and caves. A small number of secretive dwarf-like folk live here: Gübich (Faerie, Might not given), morose, dwelling in mossy caves, who calls up rain and storms, leads travellers astray, claims to be king of the dwarves and may be the dwarf king of the Rumaquelle tale; and Kröpel (Faerie, Might not given), good-natured, who roams widely hidden under his hat of fog. The witches of the Harz gather on its peaks. The range has no aura as a whole; Fengheld lies in its eastern hills.

neighbours.name: The hill of Fengheld
neighbours.summary: A remote hilltop in the eastern Harz, on the border country of Saxony and Thuringia, with a Magic aura of 5 on the summit. Vineyards and orchards cover the south slope, grain and root crops the valley floor, and sheep and goats the rest of the hill, feeding well over two hundred people; an immense curtain wall rings a summit complex of about twenty buildings, a tower for each resident magus, an elaborate guest house, a huge meeting hall and quarters for covenfolk and grogs, with outlying hamlets below. Weather magic keeps the sun, the rain and a strategic fog over it, and the local nobility has somehow never noticed the scale of what grows here.

neighbours.name: The Rammelsberg silver mines
neighbours.summary: Germany's largest silver mines, by Goslar on the northern edge of the Harz and a prized imperial asset, which are slowly flooding and failing because spiteful gnomes (Faerie, Might not given) have diverted an underground river into them. Whoever drove off the gnomes and drained the mines would be richly rewarded by the emperor. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Rumaquelle
neighbours.summary: A hidden spring of distinctive green water on the forested southern slopes of the Harz near the Römerstein castle. Romer, a young giant of the Römerstein, secretly married Ruma, daughter of the dwarf king, his father's sworn enemy; when a son was born the king found them out, cursed them, killed the child and shut Ruma in a cave. Her mother having been a mermaid, she turned herself into a stream and searched the underground passages for years until she surfaced beyond the dwarves' realm, and the spring is her outlet. Romer (giant; realm and Might not given) and Ruma (water spirit; realm and Might not given) are said still to meet here, and the spring may be a door to the dwarf king's realm. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Brocken
neighbours.summary: The highest peak of the Harz at 3,750 feet and one of the most potent supernatural sites in Germany. Its bare summit is crowned by a heap of huge granite blocks, the Witches' Altar, with a Faerie aura of 4; the lower slopes have 2, and both double on Walpurgis Night. Every 30 April the goddess Walpurga (Faerie, Seelie, Might 50), lady of summer and growth and Queen of the Holzfrauen, wholly kind to mankind, summons the summer's spirits to overcome winter's, and the Wild Hunt loses its battle with her airy elementals about the Altar; witches from miles around climb the slopes that night trailed by dozens of villagers who keep the old ways, light fires and sing to forgotten gods, and only the strongest approach the Altar. For the nine days before, Walpurga wanders the Harz as the humble wood-wife Frau Holle on a rickety wagon, hunted by the Wild Hunt, asking villagers for help and checking their housekeeping, and rewards those who shelter her with gold; at the summit she sheds her rags and stands in a white cloak and crown, shoes of fire, with a spindle and a three-cornered mirror that shows the future. The Brocken is a witches' meeting place all year and magi know it as a good place to find an apprentice. The Magic Fountain nearby gives visions to those who drink, and the Sorcerer's Flower, a pale violet anemone of the slopes, is reputed vis.

details.tethers: The Witches' Altar and Walpurga's yearly rite

neighbours.name: The Hexentanzplatz
neighbours.summary: The Witches' Dancing Ground, a rocky crag in the north-eastern Harz a dozen miles east of the Brocken, climbed by a flight of ancient steps to a weathered summit with a Faerie aura of 2. The witches of the Harz meet here every April to hold their council before going on to the Brocken. The Rosstrappe faces it across a ravine.

neighbours.name: The Rosstrappe
neighbours.summary: A great rock on the lower slope directly across the ravine from the Hexentanzplatz, bearing a huge hoofprint. Princess Brunhilde, fleeing the lustful knight Bodo, spurred her horse across the chasm to the Hexentanzplatz; a witch nearby turned Bodo into a dog and he fell into the gorge. Some say a hound (realm and Might not given) still lives by the stream at the bottom, guarding Brunhilde's crown, which fell from her head in the leap. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Bears' Cave
neighbours.summary:
A hidden primeval cave on the slopes of the northern Harz with a Magic aura of 3, its floor strewn with the arranged bones, teeth and scraps of hide of bears far larger and fiercer than any known today, which can be harvested for Animal vis (amount not given).

Secrets
The cave is the secret retreat and private vis source of an ancient line of bear-heartbeast Bjornaer descending from the Founder herself, whose two living members are Archmage Urgen of Crintera and his filia Odorpes of Fengheld's Lusatia chapter. Each visits now and then and would be furious to find anyone else harvesting their vis.

neighbours.name: The Kyffhäuser Mountains
neighbours.summary: A double line of hills on Thuringia's northern border with Saxony, said in legend to hold the sleeping bodies of famous kings, above all Frederick Barbarossa. Fengheld's chapter Turris Acontiarum stands among them and the Apple of the Kyffhäuser at the foot of their tallest peak. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Apple of the Kyffhäuser
neighbours.summary: A withered apple tree at the foot of the tallest peak of the Kyffhäuser, guarded by men-at-arms. Whichever prince hangs his shield on it becomes lord of all the West; whoever fails must guard the tree for ever as one of its warriors. Three successful challengers, Clovis, Charlemagne and Barbarossa, each cut it down to stop imitators, but it always regrows in full leaf and then withers as their fortunes fade; it last bore fruit in Barbarossa's reign. When it next comes into leaf a terrible battle begins, and when it fruits the king hangs his shield, all men rally to it and the wicked are rooted out. The tree's spirit (Magic, Might 70; Regal +4, Peaceful -1) grants victory to whoever hangs a shield, keeps its men-at-arms unaging, heals wounds and possesses anyone who fails against the guards (their number and Might not given). The Mongol Khan may one day hear of it and come to hang his shield. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The withered apple tree

neighbours.name: Turris Acontiarum
neighbours.summary: Fengheld's chapter house in the Kyffhäuser Mountains on the border of Saxony and Thuringia: a solitary tower where one magus studies the stars with a single mute companion. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Wartburg
neighbours.summary: The ancestral castle of the landgraves of Thuringia near Eisenach, founded in 1067 by Count Louis I, whose walls have never been breached. Since Landgrave Hermann I it has been a famous court of literature and music in the French courtly fashion, holding lavish festivals that draw minnesänger and noble guests from afar; at the Sängerkrieg of 1204 Walther von der Vogelweide defeated Wolfram von Eschenbach, Henry von Ofterdingen and every other rival. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Rothaargebirge
neighbours.summary: The Red Hair Mountains, heavily wooded highlands of western Thuringia, named either for the autumn colour of their trees or for the strange and fierce folk who live there, whom the book does not describe. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Sauerland
neighbours.summary: Rugged, inhospitable uplands south of Paderborn bordering Thuringia. The Dragon of the Sauerland (realm and Might not given) lives here, and the second Quest of the Path of Energy is to conquer it and eat its heart. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Goldene Aue
neighbours.summary: The Golden Meadow, a fertile plain of eastern Thuringia north of the river Saale. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Riesenstein
neighbours.summary: The Giant's Stone, standing alone in a field near Züschen a little north of Fritzlar. The Devil, watching from the mountaintop as the pious villagers of Neueburg built a church and refused his temptations, hurled a great stone at them; it caught on his sleeve and fell short, and he wept tears of blood on it that left three red stains. Every All Hallows' Eve the tears run from the stains again, and they are Ignem vis (amount not given). The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Thuringian Forest
neighbours.summary: One of the largest forests left in Germany, nearly a hundred miles long along the border of Thuringia and Franconia and about thirty wide, over low mountains whose rounded summits form a continuous ridge. Pine and fir cover it, and its deep valleys hide lovely glens and clearings. It is the traditional divide between north and south Germany: dialect, custom and dress change sharply from one side to the other. Kleon of Criamon walked the Path of Warping here and is probably lost to Twilight. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Feengrotten
neighbours.summary: The Faerie Grottoes at the eastern edge of the Thuringian Forest, with a Magic aura of 1: hidden caves reached by slippery descents past underground streams and stalactite chambers, opening into central crystal caverns where coloured lights dance over the walls. The passages seem to shift, and scrambling through them coats the explorer in glittering dust. Whoever is genuinely lost for days finds on emerging that the dust is Imaginem vis, more for more days lost; whoever tries to get lost on purpose finds only dust.

neighbours.name: The Donar Oak
neighbours.summary: The remains of the great oak sacred to Thunor in a hidden glade at Geismar in the Thuringian wilderness near Fritzlar, once the focus of the pagan power of the whole Hercynian Forest. In the eighth century Boniface made a shallow cut in its trunk before scornful heathens; a great wind shattered it into four pieces, the heathens converted, he built an oratory to St Peter from the wood, and the old forest's power broke into the smaller forests of today. The stump bears a simple cross at its centre and has regrown in several offshoots, which stand for the Hercynian Forest's rebirth as many woods. The glade is utterly serene and every wild beast turns docile in it; some believe it a gate to Eden. Its spirit (Divine, Might 40; Peaceful +5, Wild -3) heals and rarely grants virtues. The acorns are Creo vis (amount not given): an animal that eats one may be tamed, and a forest in which one is planted and grown to maturity may be tamed. The glade's location is legendary and its aura not given.

details.tethers: The regrown stump of Thunor's oak with its cross

neighbours.name: The Taunus
neighbours.summary: A forested ridge north of Frankfurt between the Main and the Lahn; the book says nothing more of it. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Vogelsberg and the Rhön
neighbours.summary: The two ranges flanking Fulda's long valley: the Vogelsberg to the west, a bright and airy wooded region about the conical peak of the Taufstein, and the Rhön to the east, an impenetrable and secretive wilderness of which the book says nothing further. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Odenwald
neighbours.summary: A forest of Franconia on the right bank of the Rhine south of Frankfurt, fifty miles long, which blooms earliest and most spectacularly of all German forests: its carpet of lilies and the blossom of its many fruit trees announce spring to the whole land. The book proposes it as the seat of the Court of the Alder Prince, with the Willow Maiden's court in the Swabian Forest nearby. The old Roman military road, the Strata Montana, runs north to south through it and is now the busy Bergstrasse to Frankfurt; bandits lurk on the swampy, deserted east bank of the Rhine along the forest's western edge, and fortified way-stations are being built along the road against them. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Stromberg
neighbours.summary: Gentle fertile hills south of Wimpfen between the Odenwald and the Black Forest where grapes have been grown for centuries. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Linden of Neustadt
neighbours.summary:
The great lime tree of Neustadt an der grossen Linden in Franconia, whose spirit (Magic, Might 30; Protective +6), uniquely among forest spirits, has adopted the people of the town as the inhabitants of its realm; it grants victory, berserk fury and toughness to the town's defenders. Having a town for its heart has weakened the spirit, but the townsfolk have become very reluctant to clear or exploit the woods. During a siege the tree's wide branches were ruined and were afterwards propped on stone columns and monuments carved with the arms of the princes and nobles who fought there. The prophecy says that when the tree dies the town loses its freedom; though an important trading post, Neustadt has resisted growth and stays a quiet backwater. A magpie has nested in the Linden and is slowly killing it, and every attempt to drive it off has failed. The aura is not given.

Secrets
The magpie is a Bjornaer magus in heartbeast form. What has he foreseen that makes him destroy the tree?

details.tethers: The great lime tree in the town

neighbours.name: The Harberg and the Drudenbaum
neighbours.summary:
The Harberg mountain and its forest overlook Nuremberg, and legend puts on its top a tree called the Drudenbaum, so named because wizards meet beneath it. Its glossy leaves shed golden drops now and then, milk oozes from its roots, a dragon guards a treasure under it, and a great black bird perched in its crown claps its wings to raise a storm whenever someone tries to take the treasure; whoever drinks a cup of the golden liquid becomes a sorcerer. The golden drops are Creo vis and the milk Vim vis (amounts not given). The spirit (Magic, Might 30; Mysterious +3) grants magic sensitivity and second sight and possesses. Magi, hedge wizards and stranger beasts all hunt the tree. The aura is not given.

Secrets
The dragon and the treasure are myth; the rest is true. The Drudenbaum is no real species: when the spirit possesses any tree of its domain, that tree takes on the Drudenbaum's look and vis for a time, and the black bird settling in its topmost branches marks the possession, so the tree keeps moving about the Harberg Forest.

details.tethers: Whichever tree of the Harberg Forest the spirit possesses

neighbours.name: The Luisenburg and the Fichtelgebirge
neighbours.summary: East of Bamberg the Luisenburg is a region of countless huge, bizarrely weathered granite blocks scattered at random for miles; beyond it rise the Fichtelgebirge, the Spruce Mountains, a forbidding empty land of rock-strewn hills, moorland and forest. The wood-spirit Katzenveit (Faerie, Might not given) is named here. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Danube
neighbours.summary: Already a great river where it crosses Bavaria, two hundred miles from its source in the Black Forest. Only the smaller, thinly peopled part of Bavaria north of the river, never Roman, belongs to the Rhine Tribunal; the Danube cities, chiefly Regensburg, and all the land south of the river are claimed by the Greater Alps Tribunal. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Rügen
neighbours.summary: Germany's largest island, about twenty miles across in the Baltic: mostly low grassland and heath with long beaches and marshy inlets, the Jasmund and Mönchgut peninsulas hillier and partly wooded, Wittow to the north windswept. The Stubnitz Forest on Jasmund, the largest wood, ends at the chalk cliffs of the Stubbenkammer and hides Crintera. Hedinsey, a narrow ten-mile island to the west, is deserted heath named for a Norwegian king who fought a battle there for his bride. Bergen, founded by the Danes, is the only town; farmsteads lie in the west, fishing hamlets in the east, and there is no real port; monks have only just begun farming Mönchgut. The islanders are mostly Slavic, Christianity is new and brought by the Danish king, and the Danes have requisitioned every horse. In the wild places the Forest Brothers Rugevit, Porevit and Porenitz, gods of rowan, beech and larch (Faerie, Might not given), are still worshipped by their few remaining priests, the volkhvy, who are welcome in Stubnitz and bury their dead at the Ziegensteine. A church is planned at Sagard, five miles from Crintera. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Stubnitz regio
neighbours.summary:
Deep in the Stubnitz Forest on the Jasmund peninsula of Rügen, five miles from Sagard, a Magic regio of four levels with auras of 1, 3, 5 and 8 holds Crintera, the domus magna of House Bjornaer; the mundane level looks like virgin forest and its aura is not given. The forest is strongly aligned to the Animal Powers, the entities who ruled here before the Bjornaer came, and religion of any kind is banned inside the regio in their honour. One route, the Watching Path, leads through Stubnitz; its start is marked by two mossy, crumbling stones in a glade near the forest's edge, known to Redcaps and Bjornaer, and every visitor is watched by covenfolk and animal allies. Every visitor, magus or mundane, should be given a heartbeast that fits his character before he crosses the boundaries. Locals shun the forest with tales of animal attacks, shadow-monsters and witches, which the covenant encourages.

Secrets
The pristine look of Stubnitz is a deception; the forest is full of hidden covenfolk settlements.

details.tethers: The Animal Powers who ruled the forest before the Bjornaer came

levels.name: The first level
levels.enter: A Corpus effect at each boundary draws the crosser's heartbeast forward; here it gives a Personality Trait of the beast. Parma usually resists, but resisting is thought rude; Bjornaer shrug the change off with a Heartbeast roll
levels.notes: Six roundhouses, the homes of the six clans, and the covenfolk's magically hidden hut clusters, which spill onto the mundane forest too.

levels.name: The second level
levels.enter: The second boundary brings a minor physical change toward the beast
levels.notes: The clans' six barracks and the training ground.

levels.name: The third level
levels.enter: The third boundary brings another minor physical change
levels.notes: Six roundhouses; visiting Bjornaer build their temporary sancta here and may stay for years as guests.

levels.name: The fourth level
levels.enter: The fourth boundary brings the last change; one who has crossed all four is visibly a quarter to a third animal
levels.notes:
The sancta of the six Elders of House Bjornaer, in six roundhouses.

Secrets
The fetishes of the Animal Powers stand here: a wooden squirrel on a stump, a stone otter in cattails, a woven-rush snake in a hollow of a boulder, a clay wolf with teeth of shell, stone birds in willow saplings ringed with feathered thongs, every animal represented and only a few visible from any one point. They are truly ancient and said to hold primordial nature spirits; touching one's own gives a deep sense of connection, and those who resisted the regio's changes, or approach another's fetish, feel compelled not to touch. Covenfolk leave offerings at the fetish of their heartbeast.

neighbours.name: Arkona
neighbours.summary:
The ruined Slavic fortress-temple on the cliffs of Kap Arkona, the northernmost point of Rügen on the Wittow peninsula, once among the holiest pagan sites of the Baltic and dedicated to the four-faced sun and war god Svantovit (Faerie, Might not given), who opposes the Queen of Winter (realm and Might not given). Bishop Absolon of Roskilde destroyed it in 1169, and a Faerie aura of 2 remains of centuries of worship. Each early spring Falke, Prima of Bjornaer, and the magi of Crintera cast the ritual that thaws the Baltic here, Appease the Queen of Winter, with a bonus of 10 to the Casting Total from the god's presence; she learned it with help from the volkhvy of Arkona and a lab text at Crintera. Two priests of Svantovit remain, a very old man trying to pass on all he knows and his grandson, who has seen no power and follows only from family duty, scraping a living on Wittow. A white horse, of which the Danes have left none on the island, is needed for the Great Ritual to the god; whoever brought one might rekindle the old priest's link to Svantovit and make a zealous pagan messiah of the grandson.

Secrets
The two priests have laboriously moved the surviving upper half of Svantovit's statue from Arkona into a well-hidden shrine: four faces looking four ways, a bull's horn in its right hand and the god's huge sword laid before it; looters took the jewelled saddle and bridle.

details.tethers: Centuries of worship of Svantovit, now fading

neighbours.name: The Königstuhl
neighbours.summary: The King's Seat, a chalk cliff rising over 380 feet from the sea beside the Stubbenkammer cliffs on the north-east shore of Jasmund. Whoever climbs it from the sea becomes king of Rügen and sits on the stone throne at the top. In 1168 Valdemar I secretly made the climb before taking the island, was seen at the top by islanders and acknowledged as rightful ruler, which is said to be why the conquest went easily; whether Valdemar II has climbed it is not known, and islanders who want the Danes gone have tried and failed, as did the Horse Elder of Crintera before Istvan Padas, who fell to his death halfway up. Whether the seat confers a Divine right or a pagan or faerie power is the storyguide's choice; cheating with magic is certain to fail. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Hertha Lake
neighbours.summary: A small dark lake, partly covered in lilies, hidden in the Stubnitz Forest a short walk from Crintera. Every May Eve the goddess Hertha (Faerie, Might not given but powerful) bathes here and afterwards drowns one of the mortals gathered to watch; her priestess marks the victim, who alone of those present does not know his fate, and the ghosts of earlier victims (realm and Might not given) gather on the shore. In return she grants good harvests to farmers who sprinkle the corners of their fields with water taken from the lake after she has bathed. Zora, the darkly beautiful faerie-blooded priestess who leads her small priesthood, is the lover of Istvan Padas of Crintera and backs his Wilderist cause; Crintera protects the priestesses from discovery, and Zora gives the covenant Creo vis each year from the goddess's presence and never chooses her victim from its covenfolk. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The goddess Hertha's yearly bathing

neighbours.name: The Ziegensteine
neighbours.summary:
The Goats' Stones, a cluster of ancient graves and megaliths in the woodland near the Mönchgut peninsula, the most prominent a barrow of two great slabs on uprights beneath a giant oak. The volkhvy of the Forest Brothers bury devout believers here; the great barrow itself is empty. Only a volkhv can open the gate it holds, and they often let Bjornaer magi use it because of Crintera's friendship, which makes it useful for contact between the Rhine and Novgorod Tribunals. The aura is not given.

Secrets
The barrow is a pre-Hermetic supernatural gateway, one end of a faerie trod through a particularly dark and frightening region of Arcadia whose far end comes out near the covenant of Pripet Major in the Novgorod Tribunal. Nobody at the Russian end can open it, so it works one way only.

details.tethers: The great barrow under the oak

neighbours.name: The Buskam
neighbours.summary: The god's stone, the largest of Rügen's findlinge, the out-of-place boulders of foreign rock that dot the island: a huge ball of stone half-submerged in the sea just off the Mönchgut peninsula, which the Slavic islanders still worship now and then. The findlinge were left by giants, the only remains of an epic battle centuries ago in which the giants of Rügen were driven out to Pomerania. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Pomerania
neighbours.summary: A thinly peopled Slavic land between the Baltic and Poland, bordering the Novgorod Tribunal, whose towns cluster on the coast and the rivers away from the primal forests inland. It has been part of the Empire only since 1181, when Barbarossa made Bogislaw a duke; German settlers are increasing, and the Church is weak here, unlike the rest of Germany, though the Knights of the Sword are founding Christian towns and monasteries and hunting pagan remnants in the forests. The giants banished from Rügen came here, and the Pomeranian Forest is the reputed stronghold of witches and werewolves. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Romowe and the Holm Oak
neighbours.summary: A sacred grove in the northern Pomeranian Forest, a wood of pine, fir, holly and evergreen oak that spills into Poland and stays dark and green all year, where every local knows not to break a twig or kill a beast. At its centre a huge holm oak hangs with cloth ribbons and talismans, and a small band of foresters keeps a fire of fallen branches burning beneath it that must never go out. This is no pagan revival: the fire imprisons the malevolent spirit of Romowe (Magic, Might 45, now 30 while entrapped; Domineering +3, Cruel +1), which grants depression to anyone who breaks a branch or kills an animal and possesses anyone who takes a branch. The last time it was free it possessed a man who violated the grove and ruled the region as a tyrant until St Adalbert of Prague defeated it, forced it back into the oak and lit the fire. A magus who took a bough for a talisman would carry much of the spirit away with him. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The fire of fallen branches that must never go out

neighbours.name: Rethra
neighbours.summary: Once a great Slavic fortress-temple to rival Arkona: a triangular citadel about the great Oracle of the god Radegast, each wall painted with old gods and holding a gate, two onto the forest and one onto a holy lake. For centuries it was also a covenant of Slavic magus-priests, which sank into deep Winter for a century or more as the forest folk abandoned the old faith; about twenty years ago the Knights of the Sword desecrated and plundered the crumbling temple, and with no word from its magi for decades the Tribunal of 1207 declared the covenant abolished. The Faerie aura is 4. The nobles of Mecklenburg still come secretly to honour Radegast though his priests are dead and would resent plunderers. The ruin may be haunted by the ghosts of its magi or shelter an ancient one on the edge of Final Twilight, and the Oracle may yield Intellego vis.

details.tethers: The Oracle of Radegast

neighbours.name: The Margravate of Brandenburg
neighbours.summary: Low-lying land on the east bank of the Elbe, founded as a march in 1150 by Albert the Bear, a Saxon who took the title of margrave after his campaigns against the Wends, and ruled since by his Ascanian descendants. Its people are a thorough mixture of Germans and Wends; it is mostly forest, slowly being cleared for farms. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Margravate of Meissen
neighbours.summary: Moderately peopled rolling land bounded to the south by the Thuringian Forest and the Ore Mountains and to the north by the Elbe and the Saale, the most civilised part of the Marches and yet a political, commercial and ecclesiastical backwater, fully German and ruled by the Wettin dynasty since 1089. It has had no Hermetic covenant since Sirmium, which the invading Magyars destroyed in the tenth century; the magical sites and vis sources the Order knew here perished with it, and none are now known. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Bastei
neighbours.summary: Spectacular limestone cliffs and pinnacles, some a thousand feet high, above the Elbe upstream of Meissen near the Ore Mountains; the hilly country here and southern Lusatia to the east hold many such dramatic rock formations. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Ore Mountains
neighbours.summary: The Erzgebirge, a bleak unsettled range of evergreen forest between Meissen and Bohemia, adjoining the Spruce Mountains of Franconia; the Elbe cuts through its eastern end, the main link between Meissen and Bohemia. Silver and tin have lately been found, and mining towns have sprung up, the largest Freiberg, founded in 1186; a twelfth-century imperial decree lets anyone prospect here and keep the proceeds. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Margravate of Lusatia
neighbours.summary: Luzica, east of the Elbe bordering Silesia: mostly forest wilderness, sparsely settled and entirely by Sorbs, ruled for generations by the margraves of Meissen. Bautzen is the only place with real German influence, and the Knights of the Sword keep a large fortification there for the slaves they ship to the Prague market. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Lusatia chapter
