neighbours.summary: The pirates of the Frisian coast, Waddenzee's among them, who bury their dead at the Pirates' Graveyards in Drenthe, a low ridge of standing stones and boulders above the swamp a couple of dozen miles up the Ems, the only stones in Friesland. The local nobility cannot unite against them.

neighbours.name: House Tremere in the Rhine
neighbours.summary: The Tremere of the Tribunal fall under two men. Stentorius of Fengheld is exarch and holds about three-fifths of the Tremere sigils, his filius's and the two Tremere of Triamore's among them; Severicus of Roznov holds the other two-fifths, including his two filii's and Hygwald Veritas's of Waddenzee. Fengheld's Tremere, with the Transylvanian Tribunal, served Henry III's conquests of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary and seized many vis sites; blocked by the Tribunal from founding daughter covenants, they built chapter houses instead, the largest run by Clemens filius Stentorius, and have lately loosened their Transylvanian ties. Roznov Fort remains an arch-conservative stronghold in regular contact with Transylvania, suspected since 1074 of being a beach-head for that Tribunal, and its companion Ladislaus sends Gifted children from the Prague slave market to Coeris.

details.rules: Only Stentorius and Severicus hold their own sigils; the exarch holds about three-fifths of the rest, Severicus the remainder
details.wants: Order, hierarchy and a strong hand on the Tribunal's eastern frontier

neighbours.name: The bear lineage of House Bjornaer
neighbours.summary:
Bjornaer magi of bear heartbeast who look back to the Founder herself; the Senior Elder of the House always has a bear heartbeast in her memory.

Secrets
An ancient hidden line descending from Bjornaer, now only Archmage Urgen of Crintera and his filia Odorpes of Fengheld's Lusatia chapter. They keep the Bears' Cave in the northern Harz, floored with the bones of primeval bears, as a private source of Animal vis; each visits now and then and would be furious to find anyone else harvesting it.

neighbours.name: Harmonists of House Bjornaer
neighbours.summary: One of the two ancient factions of House Bjornaer, whose shared philosophy holds the Magic realm to be the pristine state of the world before the fae, who arise where wilderness mixes with human curiosity, and that wilderness must be guarded from mankind, the Church and the fae alike. Harmonists hold that human expansion cannot be stopped and Bjornaer are too few to defend everything, so mundanes who do not destroy the wild must be taught to live beside it. They dominate the council at Crintera: Jon Arnsson and Phyllia are committed, and Falke leans their way without declaring. Their counsel prevailed in 1168, when the House chose to wait out the Danes on Rügen.

details.rules: Dominant on the Bjornaer council; chose in 1168 to wait out the Danish occupation
details.wants: Mundanes persuaded to live respectfully alongside the wild

neighbours.name: Wilderists of House Bjornaer
neighbours.summary:
The more extreme faction of House Bjornaer. Wilderists would keep humanity behind city walls and the wild places feared, and their zealots work to turn farmland back to wilderness and drive settlers off. Urgen, Senior Elder, former Primus and leader of the Hawthorn Gild, is their most influential voice, arguing that the Order must hold back the growing mundane population and that Bjornaer should enter Hermetic politics to do it; Istvan Padas of the Horse seat belongs, and Zora, priestess of Hertha, backs them. They gain adherents as the occupation of Rügen drags on, and the Gathering of 1227 is expected to bring the dispute to a head.

Secrets
Urgen is widely suspected of driving mundanes from the wild with covert animal attacks, and is stepping up such campaigns now he is free of the Primacy.

details.rules: Zealots revert tamed land to wilderness and drive out settlers
details.wants: Humans confined to walled cities; forests, marshes and moors left to beasts and feared

neighbours.name: Volkhvy of the Forest Brothers
neighbours.summary:
The few remaining priests of Rugevit, Porevit and Porenitz, the gods of rowan, beech and larch still worshipped in Rügen's wild places. They are welcome in the Stubnitz Forest, bury devout believers among the graves and megaliths of the Ziegensteine near Mönchgut, and alone can open the great empty barrow there, which they often let Bjornaer magi use because of their friendship with Crintera; Janis, leader of Crintera's Swan clan, is one of them.

Secrets
The barrow is a pre-Hermetic gateway, one end of a faerie trod through a particularly dark region of Arcadia that comes out near the covenant of Pripet Major in the Novgorod Tribunal. Nobody at the Russian end can open it, so it works one way only.

details.rules: All male; nearly all have Ways of the Forest and a fierce devotion to family
details.offers: Burial at the Ziegensteine; the opening of its gate for Bjornaer magi

neighbours.name: Volkhvy of Svantovit
neighbours.summary:
Only two priests of the four-faced sun- and war-god Svantovit remain, a very old man and his grandson, scraping a living on the windswept Wittow peninsula below the ruined temple of Arkona that Bishop Absalon destroyed in 1169. The elder is trying to pass on all he knows; the grandson has seen no power and follows only out of family duty. No white horse remains on Rügen for the Great Ritual, since the Danes took them all; were one brought, the old man would have his grandson steal it, and the rite's display of power would make the doubter a zealous pagan messiah bent on returning Rügen to the god, which watching magi might take for diabolism.

Secrets
The two have laboriously moved the surviving upper half of Svantovit's statue from Arkona into a well-hidden shrine: four faces looking four ways, a bull's horn in its right hand, the god's huge sword laid before it. Looters took the jewelled saddle and bridle.

details.wants: A white horse for a Great Ritual to the four-faced god
details.offers: Knowledge of the rites of Arkona, which helped Falke learn to thaw the Baltic

neighbours.name: Priesthood of Hertha
neighbours.summary: A small priesthood of women led by Zora, darkly beautiful through her goddess's gifts and the lover of Istvan Padas of Crintera, whose Wilderist stance she strongly backs. Every Walpurgis Night Hertha bathes in the small dark lake in the Stubnitz Forest a short walk from Crintera and afterwards drowns one of the mortals gathered to watch, marked by the priestess and the only one present unaware of his fate; the ghosts of earlier victims gather on the shore. Crintera protects the priestesses from discovery, and in return Zora gives the covenant Creo vis each year and never chooses her victim from its covenfolk.

details.rules: Every May Eve the goddess bathes in Hertha Lake and one marked watcher is drowned
details.offers: Good harvests for farmers who sprinkle their field corners with the lake's water; Creo vis yearly to Crintera

neighbours.name: The Order of Odin
neighbours.summary:
The Norse wizards beyond the northern border, as the Order imagines them. The fear of them has stopped any Hermetic covenant lasting long enough in Norse lands to attend a Tribunal, which leaves Zealand a grey area between the Rhine and Novgorod. The Tribunal founded Oculus Septentrionalis in 1144 to learn about them and it never did; the new covenant of Heorot has taken up the task, and Pancrestis of Heorot longs to meet a Norse wizard. Most Lowland magi know of at least a few Scandinavian wizards.

Whether it exists at all the book leaves to the storyguide, who must answer two questions: are there Norse wonder-workers who can match a Hermetic magus, and is there any organisation among them, and how tight? The answer may run from a Norse mirror of the Order hurling runic spells down to scattered weak hedge wizards brewing love potions. Norse legend tells of magicians who change shape, foretell the future and see far places, and of some who use runes to raise the dead, rule the weather, aid in battle and curse their foes; no single one of them should do all of these.

Waddenzee hunts Norse wizards on the Ash Gild's behalf and has killed a handful; Heorot studies them; Oculus Septentrionalis wants the Baltic trade.

Secrets
Waddenzee has found no evidence of an organised Order of Odin and keeps the myth alive anyway. The bulk of any such order may be Gymir's wizard pawns, or renegade Hermetic magi.

details.wants: Undecided: a rival Order's dominion over the North, or nothing more than a hedge wizard's living
details.offers: Norse magics of shape-changing, prophecy, far-seeing and the runes

neighbours.name: The Knights of the Sword
neighbours.summary: A military order founded in 1202 by Albert von Buxhövden, bishop of Riga, to crusade against the pagans of Livonia, far east along the Baltic in the Novgorod Tribunal; they took Fellin in 1211, massacring captives and baptising by force, and it is now their base. They grow ever more lawless, in an uneasy alliance with the Danish king and with Bishop Albert, who cannot restrain them. In Pomerania their war is as good as won and knights have settled on seized estates, feared by all and most by the less pious; nearly twenty years ago they desecrated and looted the temple of Rethra. They control the slave trade, holding slaves, mostly Pomeranian, at their fortification in Bautzen before taking them to Prague, and the profits fund their expansion.
neighbours.ruler: Albert von Buxhövden, bishop of Riga, founder

details.rules: A rule modelled on the Templars; in practice murder, rape and robbery go unpunished
details.wants: The pagan Baltic conquered and baptised; estates and silver
details.offers: Christian towns and monasteries in Pomerania; slaves for the Prague market

neighbours.name: The Werewolves of Pomerania
neighbours.summary:
The fireside tales of witches and werewolves in the Eastern Marches are warnings, and villagers watch neighbours and strangers for odd features or accents, for animals' fear, for a prickling neck. Shapeshifting runs in distinct lineages that form one far-flung extended family, passed reliably from two werewolf parents and less so from one; some live apart from humanity, others prey on livestock and children. Their only organisation, contrary to what House Bjornaer believes, is the yearly meeting on 30 April where disputes are settled, territories agreed, kinships renewed and the young hear the legends of a glorious past united under a war-leader against the Romans. Children of werewolf families are Skinchangers; those born to human families usually have the Lycanthrope Flaw and cannot control the change. Small animals flee them, horses shy and dogs bark, unless they have Animal Ken. Some, especially women, become greatly respected witches with powers of entrancement or second sight. The storyguide may add bear or lynx clans.

Secrets
Their legends tell of the betrayal of Bjornaer, who carried their secrets to the Roman priests, which they blame for their fall from kings of men to fringe-dwellers; the Founder was a Pomeranian shapeshifter-witch of their kind.

details.rules: Once a year on Walpurgis Night the factions of a region meet round great bonfires under compacts that forbid fighting
details.wants: Territory, kinship renewed, and the old glory remembered

neighbours.name: The God of Truth
neighbours.summary:
A dualist faith that has arisen in the last decade in the villages near the Bohemian Forest. It teaches that a God of Truth made the cosmos, while a God of Law made and rules the material world without caring for its people, and that the Church errs by worshipping the stern God of Law. The God of Truth is immaterial and can be found only in the wild, where he has sent his angels, whom men call faeries, to guide humanity. With no clear leader or line of transmission, churchmen cannot stamp it out. Tales speak of the Prophet Iacob, always accompanied by an albino crow, who appears unpredictably and never preaches, yet the religion springs up wherever he has been seen.

Secrets
The Prophet is Iacob of Irencillia, whose caricature Nestor is the white crow, carrying out Primus Handri's plan to found a religion in the name of the fae. The Quaesitores would be appalled.

details.rules: No catechism beyond reverence for the wild and leaving the churches
details.wants: Mankind led into the wild by the angels men call faeries

neighbours.name: Waddenzee's piracy
neighbours.summary: Five magically enhanced ships and nearly two hundred pirates raid North Sea shipping from Terschelling, breaking mundane law daily and skirting the Code by leaving no witnesses. Oculus Septentrionalis has lost several ships and cargoes, the Nebelkönigin with its vis and books among them, and waits for one misstep; the Quaesitores have warned the pirates repeatedly that they will get no Tribunal support if the mundane authorities move against them. Only the nobles' failure to unite has saved the covenant so far.

stages.title: Ships lost
stages.clues: Merchants of Lübeck and the Frisian coast count their losses; a stolen flagship sails under a new master.
stages.ignored: The raids grow bolder and each pirate magus edges nearer a charge of High Crimes.
stages.stopped: A ship recovered or a witness left alive gives Oculus Septentrionalis its case at Tribunal.

stages.title: The nobles unite
stages.clues: Lords who could never agree begin to talk of the haunted island.
stages.ignored: A mundane army is raised against Terschelling, perhaps at Oculus Septentrionalis's secret prompting.
stages.turned: The Tribunal is asked whether Waddenzee's magi brought ruin on themselves.

stages.title: War on the pirates
stages.clues: Bigger ships sail in convoy; the merchant towns hire soldiers and court noble allies.
stages.ignored: With Oculus Septentrionalis at the head of the merchant league, a direct assault on Waddenzee follows; but this lies more than twenty years off.

neighbours.name: The Ash of Nortorf
neighbours.summary: A small ash seedling in Nortorf's churchyard, cut down every New Year's Night by a white rider on a white horse while a black rider on a black horse tries and fails to stop him. Prophecy says that one day the black rider wins, the shoot grows into a tree, and when a horse can be tied beneath it a king comes with a great army; while his horse stays under the tree he cannot be beaten and gains fell powers. The tree spirit is Infernal, of Might 15 now and potentially 60, ambitious, and able to grant victory and the gifts of entrancement, inspiration and toughness; the white rider is Divine, the black an agent of Hell.

details.antagonist: The black horseman and the spirit of the ash

stages.title: A tip about a vis source
stages.clues: Agents of the black rider tell the magi of a tree in a churchyard that will one day yield vis, but not of the prophecy.
stages.ignored: The characters are expected at Nortorf on New Year's Night to guard it.

stages.title: New Year's Night
stages.clues: A white rider comes to cut down a seedling; a black rider rides against him.
stages.ignored: If the Divine rider is driven off or killed he never returns, and evil gains a foothold.
stages.stopped: The white rider cuts the ash as every year, and the seedling stays small.

stages.title: The tree grows
stages.clues: The ash leafs and thickens year on year until a horse can be tied beneath it.
stages.ignored: A king comes with a great army and the tree's fell gifts.

neighbours.name: Boglins
neighbours.summary: Tentacled spirit-beasts of the northern bogs, Magic Might 25 of Aquam: eight slimy dark-brown tentacles twelve feet long round a carapaced sac of a body with a toothy maw, lying under murky water where a foul stench and faint murmuring betray their pools. Gluttonous, reclusive and cunning, a boglin ambushes anything that passes, chokes it with a cloud of stinking gas, paralyses it with venomous barbs and drags it to the maw within a few rounds to eat later. Each tentacle takes wounds separately and regrows over a season's hibernation; the carcass yields eight pawns of Animal vis, one per tentacle, and six of Perdo from the black nodule of its brain.

neighbours.name: The Holy Vehm's hangings
neighbours.summary:
The secret courts of the north hang suspected witches and heretics after trials no accused can win, and leave an SSGG knife by the corpse. Their informants are everywhere, their jurisdiction covers witchcraft and sacrilege, and their courts have lately begun to sit south of their old lands.

Secrets
Philippus Niger of Durenmar turns the Vehm on hedge wizards, has had at least one Marched magus hanged by it, and spreads it southward while telling House Guernicus it is no threat to the Order.

details.antagonist: The Holy Vehm, and Philippus Niger behind it

stages.title: Courts in the south
stages.clues: Hanged men with knives beside them appear where the Vehm never sat before; a hillock gathering by night.
stages.ignored: Cunning-folk and hedge wizards near the covenant vanish one by one.

stages.title: A hedge wizard hanged
stages.clues: A wise-woman the covenant dealt with is found hanging in the market place.
stages.ignored: Informants note the covenant's own dealings; a grog or companion is summoned to appear.
stages.stopped: A Freigraf's men are exposed, and someone asks who he answers to.

stages.title: A magus accused
stages.clues: Seven witnesses are ready to swear; the accused is not expected to appear.
stages.ignored: A sentence of hanging on a magus, and a quarrel at Tribunal over whether the Vehm is a mundane matter.
stages.turned: The trail leads to Durenmar's archmage and a scandal before the Quaesitores.

neighbours.name: Imanitos Mendax
neighbours.summary:
A master of House Jerbiton at Oculus Septentrionalis in Lübeck who poses as the owner of the upmarket Goldenes Kalb tavern, with a discreet brothel upstairs for rich clients, and whose third trade is the blackmail and extortion of citizens and magi. Tall, lean and handsome, a subtle Mentem specialist with competent Imaginem for disguises; his covenant-mates find him useful despite his morals.

Secrets
He feeds Eric Ribecus of Waddenzee advance word of the covenant's ship movements for a share of the plunder, perhaps by tiny Astasian messenger demons taken for airy spirits; discovery would mean expulsion and undying enmity. Optionally he is a diabolist of a hidden dark Jerbiton lineage serving the demon Radegast, corrupting Lübeck's notables through the Goldenes Kalb, posing as the prophet of Radegast to the Mecklenburgs, able to swap the covenant's three Verditius magestones for infernally tainted copies, and perhaps planting corruption at the heart of the coming merchant league.

stages.title: Word reaches the pirates
stages.clues: Waddenzee's ships always know where the richest Lübeck cargo sails; airy spirits are seen about the Goldenes Kalb.
stages.ignored: More ships are lost and Oculus Septentrionalis blames bad luck.

stages.title: The prophet of Radegast
stages.clues: The Mecklenburg princes grow bold; a stranger is honoured at their secret rites.
stages.ignored: A pagan house with unnatural powers gains a Hermetic adviser.
stages.stopped: The prophet unmasked, the Mecklenburgs turn on their god's false servant or on the Order.

stages.title: Tainted stones
stages.clues: Greed and quarrels grow in the covenant's laboratories.
stages.ignored: The three magestones are copies; the Hermetic books Waddenzee stole are tainted, and Lucas von Beck's necromancy draws on infernal lore unknowing.
stages.turned: His treachery proven, Imanitos is expelled and the richest covenant in the Rhine has a new enemy.

neighbours.name: The Wild Hunt
neighbours.summary: Folk memory confuses two hunts. Hellequin's Hunt is a host of the unfulfilled dead in a mobile regio centred on Hellequin, a cursed spirit whose task is to guide souls that cannot reach Heaven; its ghosts seek the grace of mortals to pass on. The Wild Hunt proper is a troupe of winter and storm faeries that rises from the Teufelsküche and sweeps Germany on stormy winter nights: the Huntsman, a grim figure on an immense black horse in a storm-grey robe with a gleaming helm and a spear, perhaps a fragment of Woden, with ten to fifteen ghostly Horsemen of Might 20 who merge with their mounts and command fear, wind and cold, and twenty-five to thirty immense grey Hounds of Might 10 whose howls are the arctic wind. It hunts the Holzfrauen, holding that if every vegetation faerie is caught spring cannot come, and sometimes mortals; being spirits of wind and night it can only terrify, buffet and chill, unless the Huntsman talks a mortal into riding with it. Then every huntsman strikes with lethal force, and the rider is found at dawn exhausted and frozen, Enfeebled for good.

details.antagonist: The Wild Huntsman, Unseelie lord of Might 50

stages.title: Frau Holle's flight
stages.clues: For nine days before Walpurgis Night a humble wood-wife in a rickety wagon begs villagers for help and shelter and checks their housekeeping, the Hunt at her heels.
stages.ignored: A village that turns her away hears the Hunt pass over; one that shelters her draws its attention.
stages.turned: A peasant who carves her a new linchpin finds the shavings turned to gold; a farmer who hides her in his barn finds gold in his rye.

stages.title: Walpurgis Night
stages.clues: The Harz witches climb the Brocken, fires are lit on the slopes and the auras double.
stages.ignored: The Hunt fights the airy spirits of summer round the Witches' Altar and loses, and at dawn Walpurga drives her wagon off across the clouds.

stages.title: Stormy winter nights
stages.clues: Howling like the arctic wind over the peasants' roofs; a grim rider who asks a traveller to mount up.
stages.ignored: A mortal who rides is found at dawn, never to recover.
stages.stopped: A Holzfrau sheltered or a rider refused, and winter loosens its grip a little.

neighbours.name: Bandits of the Bergstrasse
neighbours.summary: Bandits hide in the swampy, deserted east bank of the Rhine along the western edge of the Odenwald and prey on the merchants who use the old Roman road, now the busy Bergstrasse, north to Frankfurt. Fortified way-stations are being built along the road against them.

neighbours.name: Fengheld's hidden ambition
neighbours.summary:
Fengheld commands more than forty Tribunal votes, nearly a quarter of the whole, though they are seldom all cast together, and presents itself as the Tribunal's neutral peacemaker and arbiter of disputes. The more paranoid magi already suspect a hidden agenda behind the neutrality.

Secrets
Fengheld's real policy is to keep every other covenant so tangled in politics that nobody notices its own growing power, and it has worked so far.

neighbours.name: Balastor's liberation
neighbours.summary: A young journeyman of Fengheld, born feral, who believes enlightenment means casting off humanity and means to return himself and others, consenting or not, to a primal state. His magic releases suppressed emotion and behaviour, his face takes a savage cast when he casts, and he delights in humbling self-important mundanes.

neighbours.name: The Great Khan
neighbours.summary: At the foot of the tallest peak of the Kyffhäuser stands a withered apple tree of Might 70, guarded by the unaging men-at-arms who failed to hang their shields on it. Whichever prince hangs his shield there rules all the West; Clovis, Charlemagne and Barbarossa each did and cut it down, and it regrows and withers with their fortunes. When it next leafs a terrible fight begins; when it fruits the king hangs his shield and the wicked are rooted out. The Mongol Khan may hear of it and come to hang his shield, and the fate of the West will turn on who stops him.

stages.title: The tree leafs
stages.clues: Travellers in the Kyffhäuser report the dead apple tree in full leaf.
stages.ignored: A terrible fight begins, as the legend says.

stages.title: The Khan rides west
stages.clues: Word from the east of a lord of horsemen who asks after a tree where kings hang their shields.
stages.ignored: The Khan's host reaches the hills and the men-at-arms meet it.
stages.stopped: Whoever defeats the guards and fails to hang his shield is possessed and joins them.

stages.title: The tree fruits
stages.clues: Fruit on the branches for the first time since Barbarossa.
stages.ignored: A king hangs his shield, all men rally to it, and the wicked are rooted out, whoever he is.

neighbours.name: Grendel's kin
neighbours.summary: Trolls still haunt the bogs of Zealand round the site of Hrothgar's hall, where the new covenant of Heorot has settled. They have killed fourteen of its grogs and taken the left arm of its leader Signum Irruptus, who believes them the degenerate descendants of gods and pursues his study of them regardless.

neighbours.name: The Danish occupation of Rügen
neighbours.summary: Since Valdemar I and Bishop Absalon took the island in 1168, Rügen has had Danish rulers, the Danish-founded town of Bergen, new churches at Bergen and Altenkirchen, a Cistercian monastery whose monks now farm Mönchgut, and a church planned at Sagard, five miles from Crintera. The domus magna of House Bjornaer has been in Winter for fifty years because of it: recruiting a turb from an increasingly Christian island is hard, its magical resources were damaged, and the Dominion creeps toward the Stubnitz Forest. The Tribunal of 1186 split on whether the Guardians of the Forests ruling allowed a reprisal, and in 1194 Quaesitor Caecilius ruled that no wilderness had been invaded while Crintera's forest stood; the grievance drives the House toward the Wilderists.

details.antagonist: Valdemar II of Denmark and the Church on Rügen

stages.title: The church at Sagard
stages.clues: Masons and a priest arrive at Sagard; the monks' fields spread over Mönchgut.
stages.ignored: A Divine aura grows five miles from Crintera's regio and the covenfolk's children are baptised.
stages.stopped: Animal attacks and tales of witches drive the builders off, and Bjornaer magi face prosecution as after 1186.

stages.title: Crintera's turb dwindles
stages.clues: Empty roundhouses on the first level; the Horse clan's herd thinned by Danish requisitions.
stages.ignored: The Wilderists gain the council, and Urgen's covert campaigns grow open.
stages.turned: A Harmonist settlement with the Danes, if the Quaesitores and the king can both be satisfied.

stages.title: The Gathering of 1227
stages.clues: Fifty to a hundred Bjornaer converge on Rügen for the Teufelsjahr.
stages.ignored: The dispute between Harmonists and Wilderists comes to a head before the whole House.

neighbours.name: The slave trade of Prague
neighbours.summary:
Prague holds a large slave market, and the word for a slave is the word for a Slav; the Church forbids only the enslavement of Christians. The Knights of the Sword control the trade, which pays for their corrupt expansion in Pomerania and beyond: they bring slaves to Prague and sell them to Jewish merchants who resell them in Muslim lands. An ordinary slave costs a few shillings, less than a good horse; the exceptional ten times that, and the young, healthy and strong fetch more. Owning slaves is legal in Germany and frowned on by the Church.

Secrets
Ladislaus, a shady-looking man at the market, is a trusted companion of Roznov with Magic Sensitivity; he picks out Gifted children among the slaves, who are delivered to Coeris, the domus magna of House Tremere in Transylvania. The other slaves he buys are traded or used by Roznov, and some become the victims of its summer-solstice sacrifices.

details.antagonist: The Knights of the Sword and the slave merchants of Prague

neighbours.name: Giants of the Bohemian Forest
neighbours.summary: Giants haunt the Bohemian Forest, nearly as large as the Black Forest and kept free of men by its climate and its peat bogs, swamps and marshes. They gathered the great broken rocks of Obri Hrad, the Giants' Castle, on its hilltop above the Losenice at the forest's southern edge, and may still visit it, though its Magic aura of 3 makes it a possible covenant site. Rügen's giants were long ago driven out to Pomerania after an epic battle, leaving only the out-of-place boulders of that island.

neighbours.name: The Rhine Gorge
neighbours.summary:
Below Mainz the valley closes in under forested hills. A poor road follows the banks at least as far as Bingen and Rüdesheim, but nearly everything travels by water, and in the middle, at the Loreley, the banks rise into cliffs. Between Bingen and Koblenz more than a dozen castles stand, with more a-building, because the narrow river lets a castle force a toll on the heavy traffic; the map is a chessboard on which nobles trade and conquer castles for their toll positions, and the worst of the minor lords levying 'unjust' tolls are plain robber-barons.

Only the greatest nobles, the archbishops among them, hold imperial leave to take a 'just' toll; the imperial rates are a penny for a small rowing boat of five or fewer, two for a large rowing boat or fishing vessel, four for a small ship of ten tons or less, eight for a single-masted ship and twelve for a ship of two masts or more. Two dozen vessels or more pass a station each day, so a station brings in ten shillings a day or better, enough to feed a couple of hundred peasants or keep a castle; but a toll needs real force behind it, and captains pass word of weak stations and run those that ask too much.

The river's two great hazards are the Bingen Hole and the Loreley rapids; nearly half the merchants carry their goods overland from Rüdesheim to Lorch to avoid the Hole, and some now as far as Kaub, where the count of Katzenelnbogen taxes them. Here the lands of the archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier meet, and two ancient faerie courts face each other across the water; Trier's Roman remains lie up the Mosel and the Westerwald, where Siegfried slew Fafnir, to the east. Four covenants have stood here and all four have fallen, the last two so badly that the Tribunal of 1200 banned magic in the Gorge for twenty years. That ban has now run out.

Secrets
Students of the Tribunal's records notice that each lost covenant fell within exactly eleven Tribunals, seventy-seven years, of its founding: the root of the tale that the Gorge is cursed, officially idle speculation. By the middle of the century a dozen toll stations stand between Mainz and Cologne, and in the Interregnum of the 1250s they double in four years.

neighbours.name: Rüdesheim and the Brömserburg
neighbours.summary:
The site of Rudiaria, the first covenant of the Gorge, on the right bank opposite Bingen some twenty miles below Mainz. Rudiaria was founded in 892 with the First Tribunal's sponsorship and the grant of every magical site on the Rhine between Mainz and Cologne, a Flambeau-leaning house dogged by reports of malefic doings; a charge of diabolism against its magus Eginolf went unproven in 962, and in 969 the place burned in what looked like a magical catastrophe, every magus dead or missing, while a crippling famine gripped the region. Its lesson to later founders: do not deal with demons.

Nothing could be salvaged, and Archbishop Rudbrecht of Mainz claimed and sanctified the land. The magi's keep was rebuilt as the squat square Brömserburg, long held by a minor family of Mainz's vassals, and a sizeable village grew round it; the town's name probably comes from the covenant or the archbishop. Redcap Crumena's note of 1032 AA spoke of a fortress partly visible from Bingen with covenant boatmen at its dock; only the fortress is still true, hardly a trace of magic remains, and of the four sites this is the least promising.

The Brömsers have their own sorrow: Hans Brömser, taken on the Second Crusade, vowed his only daughter to the Church for his freedom; Mechthild, who loved a young knight of Bolanden, could not face the convent and drowned herself in the Rhine, and he built a chapel on the hill in her memory. Her restless ghost still troubles the family, and Thibaud the Fat, the present baron, quietly asks learned strangers for help.

Secrets
Mechthild's ghost has no realm or Might given. The old dungeons of Rudiaria beneath the castle were merely bricked up and forgotten, and may hold Hermetic treasures and traces of its black past; were the baron to open them he might loose a captive demon on the district. In the Infernal reading of the curse Rudiaria sold its souls for seventy years of power, held Hatto II in thrall, tried to cheat and burned, and the famine and Hatto's madness both trace back to it.

neighbours.name: Rupertsberg
neighbours.summary: The hill above Bingen on which Hildegard founded her monastery in the middle of the twelfth century; it looks down on the town and on the Nahe's meeting with the Rhine.

neighbours.name: The Mäuseturm
neighbours.summary:
A slender half-ruined tower on a small island at the mouth of the Bingen Hole, built in the tenth century by the grasping Archbishop Hatto II of Mainz to squeeze tolls from the river. The tale runs that in a famine the starving begged him for his hoarded corn; he shut them in an empty barn and burned it, laughing that the mice were squeaking in his corn, whereupon thousands of mice poured out, chased his boat to the tower and ate him alive. Nobody lives there, sailors cross themselves as they pass, and none has landed in decades.

Hatto's shade still holds the tower: an Infernal spirit of Might 30 (Mentem), a ragged man-shaped shard of darkness with a twisted mitred face, wholly insubstantial and beyond any weapon, kept in being by hate (Hateful +6, Merciless +4, Brave +3, Int +1). It lurks unseen in the shadows (Perception and Awareness against 12, or 9 by day), fills up to ten people with a dread of the island that with repetition drives them mad or kills them with fright, the fate of anyone who spends a night there, and its chill touch (Initiative +3, Attack +6, dodged only with Brawl) takes a Fatigue level and gives it back five Might. Some ten swarms of demonic mice serve it, each of Might 10 (Animal), about a thousand mice to a swarm, fiery-toothed and proof against fire, and they grow back from the aura until it is cleansed. A swarm takes on about three people; an unprotected victim takes a stress die +6 each round, falling with better clothing and armour to -9 in full armour with helm and gauntlets (armour does not add its Soak), and kills ten mice for every five points of Brawl attack total; a swarm flees at half its number. Group or Room spells hit a swarm and its victims together; an Animal effect at Voice, Concentration and Group takes one swarm, and one more magnitude clears the island for a while. Hatto's crosier holds 6 pawns of Perdo vis, found only once he is destroyed.

Secrets
Hatto's corruption and the famine may both be linked to Rudiaria's misdeeds: in the Infernal reading of the curse the covenant held him in its sway.

neighbours.name: The Bingen Hole
neighbours.summary: The stretch just below Bingen, one of the river's two deadliest: rocks, a sudden quickening of the current and treacherous eddies. Only skilled, seasoned or foolhardy boatmen attempt it, though there are enough of those; many merchants portage round it.

neighbours.name: The Stone of Bacchus
neighbours.summary:
A small wooded island opposite Baccharach's quay where the wildest part of the town's autumn-equinox wine festival takes place; a few yards off its far side a weathered finger of rock rises fifteen feet from the water, the Stone of Bacchus, touched by the locals for luck with the harvest. Far too small for a covenant.

Wine drunk on the island during the festival grants +6 to resist its ill effects, but brings on mounting hallucinations and visions and debauched behaviour that each reveller perceives differently (personality traits may shift by up to 3 for the night), and at dawn the drinker is at -6 for a day. The dregs left over are Muto vis, usually about 6 pawns and up to 12: the more riotous the revelry, the more vis, however much wine is left, and hoarding the wine does not help.

neighbours.name: Pfalz Island
neighbours.summary:
The site of Rheinstein, mid-river a couple of hundred yards above Kaub (not the haunted island by Bingen). Rheinstein was founded in 1123 by Schwall of Bjornaer and Fulmonious of Tytalus with the First Tribunal's sponsorship, promising every other covenant three pawns of vis a Tribunal for five Tribunals; its magi also seemed to hold Burg Rheinstein near Bingen, though they were seldom there, as Redcap Ioanna noted in 1265 AA. In 1200 an army of angry mundanes under the archbishop of Trier destroyed it, and the magi's fate is unknown; Horst of Mercere's report laid much of the blame on their own conduct, and the Tribunal banned magic in the Gorge for twenty years. Its lesson: be subtle enough and strong enough.

The island is about a hundred yards long and under half as wide. Its upstream half carries the castle, still unrepaired since the attack, with a tiny courtyard and the rocky stump of a central tower, and a small pier on half-sunk rocks facing the left bank where the traffic runs; the downstream half is a copse of a dozen trees, with a fresh corpse on a makeshift gallows. A longer, thinner, more wooded crescent of an island lies a couple of hundred yards upstream, joined by a spine of rock that shows only at the lowest water; at high water everything but the castle and the trees floods. It looks like a stone ship riding the river. Rebuilt, it would make a cramped but serviceable covenant and a uniquely good toll station, a bowshot covering the whole river.

Lord Robert Schönburg, the baron's bastard, holds it with about a dozen ruffians taking tolls that amount to piracy; Wolkan, a branded thief, is among them. Baron Jürgen Schönburg owns the island and must be dealt with. Dripstones (chalcedonius) grow on the rock spine, one a season, brownish and waxy to the touch; pierced and worn at the neck one lets its wearer see through magical or faerie illusions (Perception against 3 plus the illusion's magnitude) and tell truth from lies (Perception against 6), and each is worth a pawn of Imaginem; a passing captain may ask for the Loreley charm the old inhabitants sold. A young vine in the copse yields a little Intellego vis from its sap with great care.

Secrets
The vine was cut in secret from Durenmar's famous vine; Durenmar does not know and may be displeased. The old magi sold dripstone charms against the Loreley to ship captains. Two ancient burial mounds hide among the upstream island's trees; Robert robbed them (paltry treasure, perhaps vis) and woke their guardians, two powerful undead corpses of unstated realm and Might with powers of stealth and destruction, who wait for a midsummer night when the river is low enough to cross the spine and fall on the castle.

neighbours.name: Loreley
neighbours.summary:
The narrowest and most treacherous point of the Gorge: the river squeezes into a canyon 150 yards wide roaring over hidden rocks between rocky slopes, and a cliff four hundred feet high, all but unclimbable from above or below, rises over it. Even with no siren singing (she may go unseen at night, in rain or in fog) the passage needs Profession: Boating against 9 from anyone who has not learned the rocks. Vis might be gathered here at great hazard.

The Loreley herself is a faerie of Might 30 (Aquam), an exceedingly beautiful maiden clothed only in the long golden hair she combs for ever with a jewelled comb (Pre +5, Com +5, Dex +2, Str -2, Sta -1; Hateful to Men +3, Jealous of Women +3). Daughter of the Rhine Spirit of the Rhinefalls, she resents mankind's taming of her father and wrecks its shipping, and envies women who win men's hearts: she lures mariners toward the cliff, climbs down, bends them to her will and drowns them. She has a faerie's nature (no fatigue, disease or ageing, speech with anyone, Second Sight) and a faerie's bane in iron, which wounds her at a touch. Her song (4 points, Imaginem) makes up to ten people a round long to reach her, an Intelligence stress roll against 9, with +3 for women and for wax-stopped ears, and a dripstone's wearer shrugs it off on Perception against 6; her gaze (8 points, Mentem) binds one man at a time who fails Intelligence against 12 to obey her utterly, even to death; she works any Creo or Rego Aquam effect up to level 30 for a point a magnitude; and for 10 points she melts into the Rhine, regaining 5 Might an hour and healing in minutes, hours and days, so that she is all but unkillable. Her blood holds 6 pawns of Aquam and her comb 4 of Imaginem.

neighbours.name: Kloster Maria Laach
neighbours.summary: A Benedictine abbey of 1093 in lonely meadows beside Laach Lake, the foremost monastery of the middle Rhine. Its church is a Romanesque masterpiece, the first columned basilica built with arches, and the garden court before it, full of statues and fountains, is a divinely inspired image of Eden; the aura of 4 is the garden's.

neighbours.name: The Teufelsloch
neighbours.summary: The Devil's Hole, in the hills west of Laach Lake: a huge eroded pit with steep crumbling edges, black within and of unknown depth, reeking of the livestock that have fallen in and rotted.

neighbours.name: Rolandseck and Nonnenwerth
neighbours.summary: On the left bank north of the Gorge the ruined castle of Rolandseck looks down on the quiet island of Nonnenwerth and its convent. Legend says Roland, count of Angers, Charlemagne's nephew and his greatest knight, loved Hildegunde, daughter of the local count Heribert, and began a castle and watchtower for them; called to fight the infidel in Iberia he was reported dead, she took the veil on the island, and when he came home too late the two could only greet each other across the water for the rest of their lives.

neighbours.name: Drachenfels
neighbours.summary:
The lowest of the Seven Hills and the nearest the Rhine, a thousand feet high. Under it runs the cave where Siegfried slew the dragon Fafnir and bathed in its blood to make himself invulnerable, as the Nibelungenlied tells; the catacombs are extensive and the aura of 3 runs throughout. It would suit a covenant were it not for Schloss Drachenfels, the archbishop of Cologne's great castle built directly above. Who or what lives in the caves is not said; perhaps Fafnir's brood endures, or that of his brother Regin who plotted the slaying with Siegfried.

The hills themselves have their legend: the wild Rhine once pooled into a lake here and spilled ruinously northward, until seven giants dug a gap with great spades to drain it, were paid in mined treasure, and left their spoil heaps as the Seven Hills.

neighbours.name: The Westerwald
neighbours.summary:
East of the right bank north of Koblenz, running more than fifty miles eastward with the Lahn valley for its southern edge: an almost unbroken rumpled blanket of birch, beech and oak with fir and pine on the heights, home to many wolf packs and, in its heart, to the faerie Court of Bright Winter. The count of Nassau, whose lands lie just to the south, is pushing into the forest and sending bands of foresters to kill its wolves.

The Court asks that the wolves be protected and intruders driven out, and would give leave to hunt and gather vis in return; the Rhine's ruling that magi may actively defend a wilderness applies. Red-Hame, a large faerie wolf of Might 12 with a ruddy ruff and back, carries the Court's wishes to the hedge wizards of Waldheim through his companion Torven. No aura is given for the forest as a whole; the glade at Waldheim is Magic 2.

neighbours.name: Waldheim
neighbours.summary:
The site of Oakdell, a dozen miles into the Westerwald. Oakdell was founded in 934 by magi of House Diedne with the First Tribunal's sponsorship and a ban on trespassing on Rudiaria's territory; unwelcoming and secretive, it brought spurious charges of spying against Durenmar in 997, saw Wizard War declared on its Caithlinn by Severus Maximus of Flambeau and on its Pietro by Cirion of Tremere in 1004, and was razed in the Schism War in 1016 with every magus slain. Its lesson: do not make powerful Hermetic enemies. Redcap Harundo's directions of 1075 AA still serve: by boat from Koblenz up the Lahn to Ems, north on the forest track for several miles to a weathered standing stone on the left, then a barely used path north-west for a couple of hours and over a small stream into a glade round an ancient oak.

The glade now holds a tiny hamlet of rude buildings and little more than a dozen people: the large hut of the elder Ludold, the smaller one of his son Torven, two more family huts and a barn. The crumbled foundations of Oakdell's two stone buildings hold a neat vegetable plot and an open pen of wild-looking pigs that obediently leave the vegetables alone. The villagers trade pigs for grain and see almost nobody else; visitors are met politely but warily. The path beyond leads toward the Court of Bright Winter, whom the villagers serve for protection while calling themselves the count of Nassau's loyal subjects and refusing to speak of the court.

Ludold, gaunt and white-haired with a necklace of bones, is a cunning man of minor potions and charms whose shelves hold bones, herbs, mushrooms and preserved organs, some perhaps vis, which he gathers round the glade; he will trade them for a wife found for Torven, there being nobody of marriageable age in the hamlet. A covenant could settle here by ousting the villagers, angering forest and court alike, or by living beside them, who resist any major building; the place is isolated and has nothing beyond the basics.

neighbours.name: The Courts of Dark Summer and Bright Winter
neighbours.summary:
Two rival faerie courts facing each other across the Gorge, their details left to the storyguide. Bright Winter, Seelie, belongs to light, snow, cold and the hunt, keeps court in the highest snowy hills of the central Westerwald east of the river, and is found at midwinter by day; Dark Summer, Unseelie, belongs to dark, fire, warmth and the fields, keeps court in the lowest swampy ground of the Hunsrück forest west of the Gorge, and is found at midsummer by night. Dark Summer rules Bright Winter from Walpurgis Night to All Hallows' Eve, and Bright Winter rules Dark Summer the rest of the year. With diplomacy either court might become a contested source of vis. Red-Hame the wolf serves Bright Winter; the Schönburg family carries Dark Summer's blood.

The storyguide may instead use the Courts of the Seasons of the forests chapter: King Holly of Winter in the Westerwald, the Alder Prince of Spring in the Odenwald, King Oak of Summer in the Palatinate Forest and the Willow Maiden of Autumn in the Hunsrück.

Secrets
In the Faerie reading of the curse the two courts play a game of seventy-seven years with the Gorge's nobles as pawns and clear the board at the end of every round. The fae of Dark Summer know a cure for Karlotte Schönburg and will sell it.

neighbours.name: The Schönburg
neighbours.summary: The large castle of Baron Jürgen Schönburg on the riverside hill just south of Oberwesel, on the left bank. The family descends at a distance from the fae of the Court of Dark Summer and keeps a little faerie blood, and a faint trace of Faerie hangs about the place at certain times of year. The red crocuses that bloom outside its walls in early summer are a source of Ignem vis. Here live the baron, his heir Karlotte, and, when he is not on Pfalz Island, his bastard son Robert.

neighbours.name: The Seven Maidens
neighbours.summary: Seven pointed rocks just breaking the water below Oberwesel, held up as a warning to Rhineland girls. Seven cold-hearted virgin sisters of the Schönburg, raised by a meek aunt after their father died of grief for want of a son, spent their days feasting, riding and hawking and toyed with and cruelly refused every suitor; pressed at last to choose, they left by boat, the eldest mocking the crowd on the shore, and a storm wave drowned them all at this spot.

neighbours.name: The Mosel Valley
neighbours.summary: The Mosel comes from the Vosges through Upper Lorraine, and its lower course between Trier and Koblenz winds between the Eifel and the Hunsrück past castles and south-facing vineyards. Smaller and quieter than the Rhine, it still carries fair traffic upstream from Koblenz to Trier or Metz.

neighbours.name: Treverorum
neighbours.summary:
The lost covenant beneath Trier, between the Fleischstrasse that leads to the main market and the poorer Niederstrasse behind it. First proposed in 1088 by Xantippes and Julia of Jerbiton and Selena Tibicena of Bonisagus to recover Rome's secrets, and refused for want of sponsors from Irencillia, Crintera and Dankmar, it was approved in 1095 when Arliandus of Tremere joined them. Mundane meddling ruined it: Redcap Ioanna was murdered in the city in 1151, Xantippes was convicted in 1158 of years of self-devised Mentem magic on Trier's people for gain, the covenant was fined fifty pawns in 1165 for harming the Order's standing with town and Church, and in 1172 Scholastus of Jerbiton declared himself its last survivor, called Trier unsafe for magi because of its churchmen, and left for the Greater Alps with part of the fine unpaid. Its lesson: do not meddle drastically with mundanes and the Church. Its symbol, the Porta Nigra, is carved on the smashed council table.

Redcap Ioanna's directions of 1236 AA named a merchant's shop on the Fleischstrasse and the password 'Pax Hermae'. The shop now sells wine under Isaac for his uncle David ben David, neither of whom knows of magi; the Blaue Keiler inn stands to its left and a narrow alley to a back street and a butcher's to its right. Two underground levels lie behind the shop under the alley, with five ways in: a bricked-off passage in the wine cellar that the last owner called haunted; the wooden ceiling shutters of two upper sancta under the rubbish-strewn old garden yard; a raised stone 'grave' of Selena Tibicena in the neglected graveyard across the alley, marked with a sanctum sign instead of a cross, hiding stairs to her sanctum (she is not buried there); a disused stair in a burnt-out house next to a brothel on the Niederstrasse, where vagabonds sleep; and, least likely, the Roman culvert from outside the walls, which runs a few hundred yards to the maze beneath the ruined Barbarathermen and the other way under the Frankenturm, a fortified merchant tower in the city.

Of the four sites this is the most intact and the most readily claimed, but it lies underground in a city: settling it without the merchant above knowing is nearly impossible, and privacy hard to come by. Its remaining vis is a few pawns of Mentem in old Roman coins in Arliandus's sanctum, and the ghosts of the amphitheatre outside the walls. Divine at street level, Magic 1 on the upper level and Magic 2 on the lower, as are many of Trier's other Roman cellars Magic 1.

Secrets
The ghosts of the covenant's magi rest in the burial alcoves by the underground stream; disturbing one may bring pestering, or lost secrets at a price.

levels.name: Upper level
levels.notes: Three sancta, decayed and mostly empty but for rubbish and rats; Selena's, under the graveyard, holds assorted skeletons. A wide circular light shaft at the centre, its path now overgrown and impassable, and an old ladder up.

levels.name: Lower level
levels.notes: The council chamber with its smashed oak table; a solid metal sanctum-marked door that reads as magical; the library of waterlogged, moss-covered books and parchment and the empty stores; double doors to an overgrown pond at the foot of the shaft and to the old sewer stream with the magi's burial alcoves. Behind the door Arliandus's sanctum stands intact: a well-equipped Mentem laboratory with modest treasures and Mentem vis in Roman coins. The Door of Deimos, iron embossed with faces and skulls inlaid in lead and silver, is unlocked but latched through a leering mouth: it compares whoever touches it with an arcane connection to the long-dead Arliandus (InCo 5, level 8, 6 a day, Touch, Momentary) and on a mismatch or a resisted check fills the intruder with terror (CrMe 15, level 43, Touch, Sun, 6 a day, Penetration 22, Intelligence against 12 or flee), gloves notwithstanding. The Crystal of a Hundred Candles in the ceiling lights the room when the door opens (CrIg 10, level 23, 24 a day). The Mirror of Dreams, gold-framed with smaller fragments, shows a willing gazer his thoughts as images and gives +3 to Mentem laboratory totals at a Warping Point a season (InCrMeIm 35, level 45, Eye, Concentration, unlimited). The Trumpet of Ghostly Summoning, a small silver trumpet, calls nearby ghosts and spirits and makes them visible (MuMeIm 40, level 41, Touch, Sun, Room, 2 a day). The storyguide may add books and laboratory texts here.

neighbours.name: The Amphitheatre of Trier
neighbours.summary:
A deserted oval Roman amphitheatre a few hundred yards east of Trier's walls along the Hermesstrasse, at the foot of the Martinsberg. Overgrown passages lead from the sandy arena into small empty chambers in the hillside once used by gladiators, where spells or Second Sight find faint ghosts; the arena is Magic 1 and the chambers Magic 2.

Three ghostly gladiators of Might 20 (Magic) linger: Marcus the Valiant, their leader, a stocky hoplomachus with round shield, arm-guard, greave, gladius and brimmed bronze helm (Str +2, Sta +3, Dex +3; Attack +14, Defence +13, Damage +7, Soak +7; Brave +3, Duty-Bound +3, Honourable +1); Cyrillus of Argentoratum, a wiry retiarius with trident, net, shoulder-guard and copper Poseidon mask (Qik +4; Initiative +7, Attack +12, Defence +14, Damage +7, the net a scuffling attack, Soak +4; Crafty +1); and Caudelix the Gaul, a burly giant of Size +1 with a great axe, iron skull-cap with a spectacled mask and leather breeches (Str +5, Sta +4; Attack +16, Defence +9, Damage +15, Soak +8; Violent +1). Blown here at night, the Trumpet of Ghostly Summoning raises the three, who arm themselves and challenge whoever is present to a duel to the death, each wagering a trinket of jewellery or Roman coin against a stake of like worth. The fight looks real but is not deadly: a killing blow knocks out, wounds are tracked as non-lethal and the players learn their true wounds only after treatment. A gladiator who wins takes his prize, later found buried in the chambers and ruined by age, and fades; one who loses fades leaving his trinket, worth 2 pawns of Mentem vis. Each fights once a year.

Secrets
The record of 1248 AA, Valdus of Tytalus fined a pawn for twice harvesting vis from Treverorum's site outside the walls, is the clue that leads to a vis source near Trier, and so to the amphitheatre, its ghosts and the trumpet.

levels.name: The gladiators' chambers
levels.notes: Small empty rooms in the hillside off the arena's passages.

neighbours.name: Fenistal
neighbours.summary:
A regio deep in the southern Bohemian Forest, dangerously close to Irencillia, of which the Order knows nothing.

Secrets
The original temple of Diana, where Merinita served as the goddess's last disciple in Germania, long thought destroyed but held ever since by the surviving renegades of early House Merinita, the exsules, as their 'covenant'. The regio has a single level, the top, at Magic 8, with no intermediate levels, so that entering it is very hard; the strongest magic of its masters goes to keeping it hidden. Fewer than a dozen exsules live there with the barest staff of servants, all once animals given human form, and two of them always stand guard. From here come raids on weak covenants, the recruiting of failed apprentices, fae set against the Order, the Huntress in the Wood as an unwitting arm, and a long-planned revenge on the Tribunal.

levels.name: The temple of Diana
levels.enter: The only level; with no intermediate levels, very hard to enter.
levels.notes: The exsules' hidden covenant.

neighbours.name: Louis I Wittelsbach, Count Palatine of the Rhine
neighbours.summary: Duke of Bavaria and Count Palatine of the Rhine. He holds Baccharach with Burg Stahleck, where his tolls are just, and Burg Thurant, and is overlord of Eberhard von Eppstein. A legitimate toll-gatherer, and, if the book's future holds, a member of the Rhine League.

neighbours.name: Werner IV, Count of Bolanden
neighbours.summary: A vassal of Mainz and a fervent builder of castles, with lands south-west of Mainz and Burg Ehrenfels, Burg Sterrenberg, whose tolls are unjust, and Burg Liebenstein. Elder brother of Philip I of Falkenstein. A knight of Bolanden was the lover of Mechthild Brömser.

neighbours.name: Dieter II, Count von Katzenelnbogen
neighbours.summary:
A fervent castle-builder holding a large, thinly peopled territory between the Taunus and the Lahn east of the Gorge: Kaub, whose tolls are unjust, Burg Hohenstein, Burg Kaub, still a-building, and Burg Katzenelnbogen, whose tolls are also unjust. His family rose fast from humble east-bank origins in two generations, and its castles and intrusion into the Gorge alarm the archbishops.

Tall, proud and not very pious, fond of tournaments and war, he loves nothing so much as ruthlessly gathering land and castles. Easy to make an enemy of, but treated with care and respect a possible ally: he has no qualms about dealing with useful wizards.

neighbours.name: Henry II the Rich, Count of Nassau
neighbours.summary: Holds land along the Lahn and round the Westerwald: Burg Nassau, the town of Nassau and Limburg, taking unjust tolls at both. He is pushing hard into the Westerwald to bring it under his hand and sends foresters to kill its wolves, the grievance of the Court of Bright Winter. Torven of Waldheim's uncle was one of his foresters.

neighbours.name: Gerlach IV, Count of Veldenz
neighbours.summary: A vassal of Trier whose lands lie south-west of Koblenz and along the Mosel.

neighbours.name: Eberhard II, Count of Aremberg
neighbours.summary: Holds lands on the edge of the Eifel west of Koblenz: Altenahr, Burg Are and Burg Aremberg.

neighbours.name: Philip I, Baron Falkenstein
neighbours.summary: Younger brother and vassal of the count of Bolanden, holding some of the Bolanden lands and Burg Reichenstein.

neighbours.name: Jürgen, Baron Schönburg
neighbours.summary:
Holds Oberwesel, the Schönburg and Burg Pfalz, where the tolls are unjust. Of distant faerie descent from the Court of Dark Summer. Father of Karlotte, his lawful heir, and of the bastard Robert, whom he put in charge of the Pfalz tolls; he is ashamed of Robert and suspects him of unjust tolls, but divided loyalties leave him paralysed and blind to the worst of it.

He owns Pfalz Island. Magi who cure Karlotte and prove Robert's guilt win his gratitude; he may then lease them the island, perhaps sharing the toll profits if they rebuild Burg Pfalz and run the station, though Robert's band must still be put out by force. Driving Robert out first makes an enemy of the baron.

neighbours.name: Eberhard von Eppstein, Baron of Braubach
neighbours.summary: A vassal of the Count Palatine holding Braubach and the Marksburg, where his tolls are unjust.

neighbours.name: Thibaud the Fat, Baron of Rüdesheim
neighbours.summary: A minor vassal of Mainz holding Rüdesheim and the Brömserburg, the old keep of Rudiaria. Haunted by the ghost of his ancestress Mechthild, he discreetly asks knowledgeable strangers for help.

neighbours.name: Arnold, Baron von Eltz
neighbours.summary: A minor noble holding Karden and Burg Eltz, where his tolls are unjust.

neighbours.name: Hermann von Wien, Baron of Sooneck
neighbours.summary: A minor noble holding Burg Sooneck, where his tolls are unjust.

neighbours.name: Bingen
neighbours.summary: At the southern end of the Gorge, where the Nahe meets the Rhine under a Roman bridge: an old walled town guarded by Burg Klopp, where tolls are taken for Mainz. The Bingen Hole lies just downstream, and Hildegard's monastery of Rupertsberg looks down on the town.

neighbours.name: Rüdesheim
neighbours.summary: A sizeable village on the right bank opposite Bingen, grown up round the Brömserburg and held by Thibaud the Fat, a minor vassal of Mainz. The overland portage to Lorch, and now to Kaub, starts here.

neighbours.name: Baccharach
neighbours.summary: A left-bank town amid wide vineyards making a potent and locally prized wine, with a modest quay. Its autumn-equinox wine festival draws townsfolk and peasants from miles about, the wildest of it on the island of the Stone of Bacchus opposite. Held by Louis I, the Count Palatine, from Burg Stahleck, whose tolls are just.

neighbours.name: Kaub
neighbours.summary: A walled town, little more than a prosperous village, on the right bank a couple of hundred yards below Pfalz Island. Count Dieter II von Katzenelnbogen took it lately, is building Burg Kaub on the hillside above, and has begun taking unjust tolls from the merchants who portage overland from Rüdesheim.

neighbours.name: Oberwesel
neighbours.summary: A prosperous left-bank town two miles below Kaub, held by Baron Jürgen Schönburg from his castle just to the south; the rocks of the Seven Maidens lie just downstream.

neighbours.name: Koblenz
neighbours.summary: A fair-sized city where the Mosel meets the Rhine, named from the Latin for the confluence. The Roman fort is long gone but the old walls stand; the chief church, the collegiate foundation of St Kastor of 830, has lately grown to four towers, and there are several more churches, a courthouse and many merchants grown rich on Mosel wine. Emperor Henry II gave it its charter in 1018 and the archbishops of Trier have held it since, taking just tolls. The Teutonic Knights have lately founded a chapter house at its north end.

neighbours.name: Limburg
neighbours.summary: A fortified town on the Lahn some two dozen miles above the Rhine, guarding a large wooden bridge of the twelfth century (not the duchy of the same name). Held by Henry II of Nassau, whose tolls here are unjust.
neighbours.ruler: Henry II the Rich, Count of Nassau

neighbours.name: The Teutonic Knights of Koblenz
neighbours.summary: A chapter house of the Teutonic Knights, newly founded at the north end of Koblenz.

neighbours.name: Kloster Maria Laach
neighbours.summary: The Benedictine abbey beside Laach Lake, founded in 1093 and the foremost monastery of the region, with its arched columned basilica and its garden court made in the image of Eden, where the Divine aura reaches 4.

neighbours.name: Rupertsberg monastery
neighbours.summary:
The Benedictine house Hildegard of Bingen founded on the hill above Bingen in the middle of the twelfth century. Hildegard, schooled at a monastery from the age of eight, was theologian, physician, mystic, diplomat, poet and politician, and most famous for music that seemed close to miraculous; she never quite mastered Latin and wrote through a scribe to emperors, popes and archbishops, and to several magi. It is said, though never confirmed, that House Jerbiton took her in around 1158 as a Larta, an unGifted maga under its protection and teaching; she never came to Tribunal and met few magi. She had Communication +4 and was a Good Teacher.

Her works in the original are all of Quality 13 (copies may be poorer): Scivias, a tractatus on Theology; Liber Vitae Meritorum, a tractatus on moral Philosophiae and Theology; Liber Divinorum Operum, a summa on metaphysical Philosophiae at level 2 and Theology at level 5; Physica, a tractatus on natural Philosophiae and Medicine; Causae et Curae, a summa on natural Philosophiae at level 2 and Medicine at level 3; Ordo Virtutum, a tractatus on the music of Artes Liberales, moral Philosophiae and Theology; and Symphonia Armoniae Celestium Revelationum, a tractatus on the astronomy and music of Artes Liberales.

Secrets
In the Divine reading of the curse Hildegard is the pattern of the humble, pious wizard whom God lets prosper where the Order fails; seeking out her writings may show the way.

neighbours.name: The Curse of the Rhine Gorge
neighbours.summary:
After Treverorum and Rheinstein fell, the Tribunal of 1200 forbade all magic in the Gorge for twenty years. The ban has now lapsed, and Durenmar's leaders want a new covenant on the middle Rhine to put life back into a Tribunal where no covenant has been founded in decades, Fengheld's chapter houses multiply and magi drift away to other Tribunals. Newly Gauntleted magi, some who finished their apprenticeships at Durenmar and some invited from elsewhere, are to survey the four lost sites, choose one and found a covenant under Durenmar's sponsorship, subject to the other covenants' approval. Murion, Prima of Bonisagus and Praeco, lays out the grand but detail-light plan at the Forum straight after their initiation; Occultes of Durenmar may offer encouragement; Xavier of Mercere, the Tribunal's archivist, supplies the old Redcap directions, and a season in the Great Library yields the records of the four covenants.

The four teach the Lessons of Failure: Rudiaria, do not deal with demons; Oakdell, do not make powerful Hermetic enemies; Treverorum, do not meddle drastically with mundanes and Church; Rheinstein, be subtle and well defended. The storyguide may run it gently, with years of support from a parent covenant such as Fengheld or Durenmar and exploratory forays first, or throw the magi in at the deep end, with Durenmar disorganised and resources scant. The party should mix Rhine and non-Rhine magi: Rhine-trained ones may take the Gild Trained Virtue and a parens from the book's masters and archmagi; one or two from rich covenants start with a shield grog and money, and several, but fewer than half, should come from Fengheld with favoured resources for the sake of the politics. Grogs come from local recruits or sponsors' gifts, and a shield grog is played by someone other than its magus's player.

Secrets
Each lost covenant fell within exactly seventy-seven years of its founding, and the saga can climax about seven decades in, when the curse's forces gather and the covenant meets its predecessors' fate unless it breaks the curse and founds a lasting Hermetic power. The storyguide chooses one cause, or none but self-inflicted misfortune:

Magic, the revenge of the Nibelungs: Siegfried cheated the dwarves and giants who first tamed the Rhine, dooming his line and every kingdom or wise man who follows him to fall within seven decades, as the Burgundians fell to Attila, the Merovingians, and Charlemagne's empire to the Norse. Breaking it may uncover the lost Rhinegold and may require the untaming of the river's elemental spirit; it ties to Schwall of Bjornaer's schemes and the Path of the Heartbeast.

Faerie, the rivalry of the Courts: Dark Summer and Bright Winter play a game more than a thousand years old with the Gorge's nobles as pawns, and its rules clear the board every seventy-seven years, sweeping away nobles, covenants and kingdoms alike; the Romans were Dark Summer's pieces and the barbarians Bright Winter's, then Burgundians against Huns as the Nibelungenlied records.

Infernal, the pact of Rudiaria: the first covenant sold its souls to a powerful devil for gifts falling due after seventy years, grew mighty, held Archbishop Hatto II in thrall, and when payment came tried to cheat and was destroyed battling Hell in a great fire; the devil has since lured each later covenant to the same fall on the same schedule. This ties to the Gymir and Radegast arc.

Divine, the corruption of the Merovingians: the Christian wizard-kings, Merovech descended from David and keeper of the Grail, rose by God's plan and fell within seven decades to corruption and infighting; God blessed the Carolingians and cursed every wizard's work in the region to fail in the same span, the Order's included, and only humble pious wizards such as Hildegard prosper. Her writings and the counsel of Albertus Magnus may show the path. If history holds, the Rhine League of the 1250s is a further threat to any covenant taking tolls.

details.antagonist: The curse of the Gorge, whichever realm the storyguide gives it

stages.title: The Praeco's commission
stages.clues: Durenmar's unease is talked of: no new covenant in decades, Fengheld's chapters spreading, magi leaving. Right after the initiation at the Forum Murion names the Gorge, now free of its ban, and offers Durenmar's sponsorship. A season's work in the Great Library (a fitting Mercere Gauntlet) turns up the Tribunal records, and Xavier the archivist the Redcap directions of Crumena, Harundo and Ioanna. A side road: a panicked, injured young magus reports his reckless Jerbiton friend and their grogs dragged off by shadowy figures in the Black Forest, and Durenmar's own magi will not stir; the rescue may serve as a Flambeau, Tytalus or Merinita Gauntlet, may be a true accident or a parens's test, and the rescued magus may promise to sponsor the covenant.
stages.ignored: The magi scatter to other covenants or Tribunals and the Gorge stays empty; Fengheld may plant a chapter there instead.
stages.stopped: Murion is refused; Durenmar looks weaker still, and remembers.
stages.turned: The magi take the commission on their own terms, bargaining for gentle support or accepting the deep end.

stages.title: The road north
stages.clues: Nearly a hundred miles and about a week from Durenmar: the north-east edge of the Black Forest, Wimpfen, the Odenwald, where bandits waylay badly guarded travellers, Frankfurt's great market fair, and Mainz, whose archbishop rules the southern Gorge.
stages.ignored: A careless party loses goods or grogs to the Odenwald's bandits.
stages.stopped: The bandits are beaten off or bought; the magi reach Mainz intact.
stages.turned: A first acquaintance in Mainz or Frankfurt, a merchant or a cleric, becomes a contact for the years ahead.

stages.title: The four sites
stages.clues: At Rüdesheim only a fortress and a haunted baron; at Pfalz Island Robert Schönburg's ruffians, a corpse on the gallows and a cramped ruin that commands the river; at Waldheim a wary hamlet, tame pigs and a path toward the faerie court; under Trier a wine merchant's cellar, a false grave and a sealed Tremere door. Round them wait the Mouse Tower, the Loreley, the Stone of Bacchus and the amphitheatre's ghosts.
stages.ignored: Hatto's dread, the Loreley's song or Robert's gang take their toll of the unwary; a night on the Mäuseturm island kills.
stages.stopped: Each hazard faced yields something: Perdo vis from Hatto's crosier, dripstones against the Loreley, Mentem trinkets from the gladiators.
stages.turned: Thibaud, Ludold, David ben David or Baron Schönburg become friends rather than obstacles, each with a price.

stages.title: Forest or city, covenant or chapter
stages.clues: The choice mirrors the Tribunal's own divide: the forest covenants Crintera, Irencillia and Dankmar against the city covenants Oculus Septentrionalis, Triamore and Waddenzee. Durenmar wants a neutral traditionalist covenant to pull the Tribunal together; Fengheld wants a chapter house that would make it the Tribunal's giant, and makes generous offers at the cost of independence, which Fengheld-trained magi may favour.
stages.ignored: Drift leaves the magi with no site and no patron as Tribunal approaches.
stages.stopped: Fengheld's offer refused, Durenmar's sponsorship stands, and Fengheld becomes a rival, not an enemy.
stages.turned: A Fengheld chapter: funded and protected, bound by Fengheld's charter, needing no Tribunal vote, and Durenmar disappointed.

stages.title: Sponsors at Tribunal
stages.clues: A new covenant needs one sponsoring magus from every other covenant; one suffices against his fellows' views, and refusing reflects badly on a covenant, so modest terms usually serve unless the proposal looks like a direct threat. The deals are best struck in the days before Tribunal opens at Durenmar, and each sponsor brings a founding gift in the measure of its regard: books, items, valuables, grogs, some only promised. One gift may be an enigmatic item with only hints to its use; another's lavish gifts turn mundane and insulting when the Moon-duration Imaginem spells on them lapse, showing what the giver really thinks.
stages.ignored: Without a sponsor from every covenant the foundation is not recognised.
stages.stopped: A covenant that sees the Gorge foundation as a threat withholds its sponsor; the magi must find what it fears and buy it off.
stages.turned: The covenant is recognised, its sponsors' favours owed and their gifts in hand.

stages.title: Settling in
stages.clues: Mundane entanglement is certain: at the island, toll-gathering among archbishops, the Count Palatine, Katzenelnbogen and the robber-barons, with Robert's band to evict and Karlotte to cure; in the forest, survival, Nassau's foresters and the Court of Bright Winter's demands; under Trier, a hostile archbishop and a merchant overhead. Gild membership and the Durenmar-Fengheld rivalry pull at the magi from inside the Order.
stages.ignored: Unjust tolls, a slighted baron or a provoked court bring the fate of Rheinstein closer.
stages.stopped: The covenant holds its ground, pays or collects its tolls lawfully and keeps the Church at arm's length.
stages.turned: Katzenelnbogen or Schönburg becomes an ally; the Court sells leave to harvest vis; the covenant is a power on the river.

stages.title: The Lotharingian question
stages.clues: The north-western covenants, the Lotharingians, talk of seceding from the Rhine to deal more freely with mundanes. A Gorge covenant sits on the border and must choose between loyalty to Durenmar's traditions and a freer hand in a smaller Tribunal.
stages.ignored: Both sides count the covenant among the uncommitted and court or threaten it.
stages.stopped: The covenant stands with Durenmar and the motion fails or passes without it.
stages.turned: The covenant goes with the Lotharingians, and Durenmar's sponsorship sours.

stages.title: The seventy-seventh year
stages.clues: As the covenant nears its eleventh Tribunal the signs of its predecessors' falls return: malefic rumours and famine as at Rudiaria, powerful Hermetic enemies as at Oakdell, trouble with town and Church as at Treverorum, an army at the gates as at Rheinstein; the Rhine League, if history holds, is tearing down robber castles. The chosen cause shows its hand: the river spirit stirring, the Courts clearing their board, the devil of Rudiaria calling in its debt, or the Order's works withering where Hildegard's prospered.
stages.ignored: The covenant falls within seventy-seven years, like the four before it.
stages.stopped: The curse is broken at its root: the Rhinegold found and the river untamed, the game of the Courts ended, the devil defeated, or grace won through humility and the counsel of Albertus Magnus; the covenant endures as a lasting power.
stages.turned: The covenant survives by a bargain with the curse's source, and inherits its debt.

neighbours.name: Gymir
neighbours.summary:
A name from the North that the Order does not know in 1220.

Secrets
A demon prince whose earthly fief is Scandinavia, at war with Radegast and with the Dominion; Might not given. It strikes at the Church, works through catastrophe and weather and through the Norse, commands an aggressive faction of wizards, profits from Waddenzee's piracy, and is worming into the Holy Vehm, whose leader, the archbishop of Cologne, it has murdered in 1225 if the book's future holds, meaning to turn the Vehm on Radegast's pagans in northern Germany.

details.wants: (secret) the Church undone and the Holy Vehm turned on Radegast's followers
details.offers: (secret) storms, catastrophe and infernal power to its wizard pawns

neighbours.name: Radegast
neighbours.summary:
A god of the Old Ways to the Slavs of the Baltic shore, as far as the Order knows.

Secrets
A demon prince whose fief is the Slavic lands, its heartland the eastern Baltic shore; Might not given. It wants the Germans deflected north and the Hanseatic towns rotted by greed, poses as the pagan gods, and can dress Infernal power as Magic or Faerie: the auras of Rethra and Mount Radhost are really Infernal. Its pawns are Imanitos Mendax, willingly; Roznov, unwittingly; a cult among the townsfolk of Holstein and the Slavic princes of Mecklenburg; and an Ash Gild-led war on the Norse it is planning.

details.wants: (secret) Germans turned north against the Norse, the Hansa corrupted by greed
details.offers: (secret) the powers of a 'god' to those who worship it

neighbours.name: The cult of Radegast
neighbours.summary:
Worshippers of the Old Ways among the townsfolk of Holstein and the Slavic princes of Mecklenburg.

Secrets
Nobles and priests of the Holstein cities and the Mecklenburg princes who worship the demon Radegast believing it a god and receive diabolic powers; Imanitos Mendax poses as their high priest and gathers power among them.

details.wants: (secret) the favour of their 'god' and power over their neighbours
details.offers: (secret) diabolic powers to its members

neighbours.name: The exsules of Fenistal
neighbours.summary:
Nothing of them is known to the Order in 1220.

Secrets
Fewer than a dozen self-styled exiles (exsules; one exsul) living at Fenistal in the Bohemian Forest: descendants of the losing faction of early House Merinita who rejected the Order after Myanar's death and keep a Hermetic-like tradition cut off from modern Magic Theory. All have Weird Magic; all know Parma Magica but imperfectly (Flawed Parma Magica); most have studied from vis all their lives, so Poor Reader is common; the line bears Faerie Enmity from Quendalon's curse; many have Mythic Blood from Merinita or from powerful magical spirits, and Ways of the Forest, Free Study and Study Bonus are common. Heirs of Merinita's nature magic, many have walked the Paths through the Forest and may have overcome one or more Lesser Limits, and they may have taken in Diedne fleeing the Schism War, in which case they excel at spontaneous magic. With little access to Hermetic grimoires their spells rouse nature's fury rather than strike directly, and should feel alien and frightening to a Hermetic magus.

They mean to survive hidden, keep up with Hermetic advances by theft and spying, shelter failed apprentices, set the fae against the Order, and in the end take revenge on the Tribunal; they count Irencillia their greatest enemy, though Irencillia knows nothing of them. They keep no warriors and the barest servants, all former animals given human shape, which makes infiltration all but impossible; two members are always on guard. The Huntress in the Wood is their unwitting instrument.

details.rules: (secret) two members always on guard; no outsider enters
details.wants: (secret) to stay hidden, steal the Order's advances and avenge themselves on the Tribunal
details.offers: (secret) shelter to failed apprentices; the old nature magic of Merinita

neighbours.name: The Huntress in the Wood
neighbours.summary:
A secret society within the Order, mostly of House Bjornaer's followers, devoted to preserving primal, nature-bound magic. Its members meet in secret wearing animal masks.

Secrets
It is unknowingly a pawn of the exsules of Fenistal, who have steered it since its founding; with every face hidden, its members do not know that not all of them are magi of the Order. The agenda instilled in it is to take over the Elder Gild and with it Irencillia.

details.rules: Members meet masked as animals and keep one another's names secret
details.wants: Primal nature magic preserved; (secret) the Elder Gild and Irencillia in its hands
details.offers: Fellowship among the Order's wild-hearted magi
