neighbours.name: The Pomeranian shapeshifters
neighbours.summary:
A close-knit but far from united community of mostly unGifted shapeshifters in Pomerania, long at feud with House Bjornaer, which no longer remembers why. They have factions and feuds of their own, and the most peaceable among them may treat with Prima Falke.

Secrets
In the Crintera Schism arc they are admitted to House Bjornaer in 1227 and 1228 and mostly lean Wilderist, tipping the House's balance.

details.wants: Their old feud with Bjornaer settled on their own terms
details.offers: The shapeshifter's art, outside Hermetic tradition

neighbours.name: The Rhine League
neighbours.summary:
No such league exists in 1220.

Secrets
If history holds: as toll stations grow to a dozen by mid-century and double in four years in the Interregnum of the 1250s, merchants and lawful toll-takers suffer, and Mainz and Worms found the Rhine League to protect their merchants; many cities, the princely nobles (the three archbishops and the Count Palatine) and lesser nobles join. It puts down unjust tolls by trade sanctions and by destroying robber-barons' castles, besieging or razing nearly a dozen and unseating several barons, and disbands after three years with its aims met. A formidable foe for any covenant that acts as or allies with a robber-baron: vast resources, a large army and God on its side.

details.wants: (secret) unjust tolls ended and the robber castles razed
details.offers: (secret) protection for merchants and lawful toll-takers

neighbours.name: Lord Robert Schönburg's band
neighbours.summary:
About a dozen malcontents and ruffians living in the ruins on Pfalz Island under Lord Robert Schönburg, taking river tolls that amount to piracy; Wolkan the branded thief is one of them.

Secrets
Robert is a diabolist.

details.wants: Tolls, by extortion if need be
details.offers: A living on the river for men nobody else will have

characters.name: Murion

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Archmage, Prima of House Bonisagus, leader of Durenmar, leader of the Oak Gild and, as holder of Bonisagus's sigil, Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal: the most politically powerful maga in the Tribunal. Haughty and overbearing, she wants Durenmar and the Rhine restored to the first place in the Order, and so quietly favours the Ash Gild's war on the Norse wizards, which would draw mighty magi and loot to the Rhine. Brilliant in every Art, above all Rego and Imaginem; she wears a great cloak of white feathers enchanted with illusions, and there are theories about whom she has impersonated in it. Her familiar is the raven Kolkrabus.

Secrets
She sends Kolkrabus to spy on Dankmar and on others she takes for enemies, in breach of the Code.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, Colens Arcanorum and librarian of the Great Library, Murion's first filius, about forty years past his Gauntlet. Thin and balding with a perceptive, commanding stare, he decides who may use the library and which gifts it accepts, so he is unwise to annoy. His duties keep him at the covenant and away from his own research. Many see him as Murion's puppet; rumour says he is preparing to challenge for Archmage within ten years.

characters.name: Tandaline

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, of the Trianoma lineage, Murion's closest confidante and her appointed Tenens Occultorum. Pale and slender, with eyes that shift colour hypnotically; a master of Muto and Auram for decades, she studies the air by turning herself into vapour. Politically Murion's ally, yet respected as a free thinker in her own right; she writes to many Bonisagus magi and uses those connections to punish anyone reported to have abused one of the House. Her apprentice is Petrus Virilis's Gifted son.

characters.name: Caecilius

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Archmage of House Bonisagus, the most venerable magus of Durenmar, senior Quaesitor of the Rhine Tribunal and the greatest living exponent of Intellego. Appointed Quaesitor long ago, it is said unwillingly and out of duty when the Tribunal's Quaesitorial presence was thin; his research extends the investigative rituals of House Guernicus. Reluctant and slow to act, with ever more frequent Twilight episodes, he is nonetheless a brilliant investigator with a spotless record who has solved many Hermetic crimes, and he adjudicates at Tribunal. His familiar is a silver-coated wolf.

characters.name: Occultes

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Master of House Bonisagus, leader of the Linden Gild and figurehead of Durenmar's outward-looking faction, which would admit exotic magic; a sizeable minority of the House would rather have him as Primus. A colourful man who researches manuscripts and items of every kind, has made a small golem that serves in his lab, enchanted many texts and quills, and collects news of artifacts and strange practices from far away. He was librarian until the former Primus Avarret removed him. Murion tolerates and watches him, judging his ambitions modest and fearing a schism in the House if she moved against him.

Secrets
He knows the restricted texts and has quietly copied or moved the most interesting into his own sanctum, passing them to close allies whose research they suit.

characters.name: Ricardus Caespuus

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, a recluse whose sanctum on the covenant's southern edge is a great building walled almost entirely in glass, thousands of lead-framed panes on timber beams, unlike anything else in the century. Inside is a Herbam laboratory full of exotic plants from which he cultivates several kinds of vis, much as others extract it. Earnest and friendly but understood by nobody; Murion's circle rate him little better than a hedge wizard and bear with him for his harvests and his steady gifts to the stores.

characters.name: Petrus Virilis

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Journeyman of House Bonisagus, an otherwise mediocre magus whose seed is Vim vis, whether by faerie gift or through the obsessive research into fertility and the Gift of his liberal-minded mater Susanna, now in Final Twilight. Tandaline talked him into an experiment that fathered a Gifted son on a serving maid, now her apprentice, and on Murion's orders he has fathered four more, all Gifted, and all sons when born at Durenmar because of Philippus Niger's Twilight scar. Averse to sex and ill at ease with women, he would keep his vis to himself, but the covenant deems his talent too valuable; interested young magae write to him.

Secrets
He plans to invent a longevity ritual that would probably leave him infertile; Murion would be furious. A maga wanting a Gifted child must offer more than seduction; he might instead fall for a peasant girl and plan a wedding in a nearby town.

characters.name: Winfrida

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Guernicus and Quaesitor, young, inexperienced and timid, admitted some years ago because a Guernicus must always be at Durenmar; she passed her Gauntlet in the Greater Alps. She would secretly rather live the research life of a Bonisagus. She and Tabanus may be the only two Guernicus in the Rhine; Murion is grooming and indoctrinating her, confusing her loyalties, and Tabanus thinks her weak.

characters.name: Philippus Niger

description.biography: Equipment: clothes, a dagger and a long sword; Encumbrance 3 (3). Talisman: the Knife of Human Bone; he also owns the Wizard's Bridle and the Subtle Chain. Familiar: Sordus, a basilisk. Twilight Scars: he seems to swell when angry, his shadow sometimes moves of itself, he knows true gold from false, only boys are born where he has lived a year, he sours wine, loud noise pains him, black animals gather round him outdoors, and flames dim when he comes in. His focus and his Ambitious Flaw come with his Mythic Blood, whose feat lets him smell magic. Chaos of the Angry Waves came from a Twilight. He knows Demon's Eternal Oblivion and Wind of Mundane Silence at levels 25 and 50, and Dreadful Bane of the Fae, Sap the Griffon's Strength and Shattering the Malicious Rune at 30 and 50. From forty years past his Gauntlet he learned his spells as laboratory projects.

characters.summary: Archmage of House Flambeau, of the Apromor lineage, leading figure of the Ash Gild and Protector of Durenmar, chosen by Murion, whose political ally he is. Called the Black: a smallish, well-built, cool and reserved man who looks ninety, somewhat deaf, bowed and creaky, in a black hooded cloak over darkest grey with a serrated dagger of human bone, his talisman, always at his belt. He has spent his life defending the Order against non-Hermetic wizards and is the Order's foremost master of Perdo; now, with Final Twilight near, he turns to politics, driving the Ash Gild's push for war on the Norse wizards beyond the Baltic and pressing Oculus Septentrionalis to investigate harder and to open a Mercere Portal to Durenmar, which would wound Fengheld. Most of Fengheld and its allies oppose him and several hedge wizards want him dead; he lives in the Watchtower on the cliffs, built apart so that his familiar Sordus, a basilisk whose gaze kills and whose presence withers plants and fouls water, should not blight the valley. His Twilight scars are many: he seems to grow when angry, his shadow moves on its own, flames dim when he enters, wine sours near him, black animals follow him, and only sons are born where he has lived a year. He has trained four apprentices and made the Wizard's Bridle, which binds a magus's words and gestures, and the Subtle Chain, a silver loop that lays six wards at once.

characters.name: Gudrun Tigurina

characters.summary: Master of House Verditius and Artificer of Durenmar, the honorary post that crafts items for the covenant's glory. She lives in Verditius' Forge, the half-buried laboratory the Founder built when he came to study with Bonisagus.

characters.summary: Master of House Mercere, the only Gifted Mercere in the Rhine and the Tribunal's archivist. He oversees the Mercer House in the basement of the Tower of Trianoma, which serves the southern Tribunal, and is content that Horst of Fengheld leads the Rhine's Redcaps from the other Mercer House.

characters.name: Sula
characters.summary: Autocrat of Durenmar: a wrinkled, gentle woman past ninety and still hale, who arranges lodging for guests and places visitors with uncanny ease.

characters.name: Schadrit

characters.summary: Master of House Ex Miscellanea, co-founder and iron-handed ruler of Dankmar. Trained as a Bonisagus apprentice at Durenmar under Aschlaranda, expelled with her mistress a year before her Gauntlet and finished outside the House. A withered hag in a voluminous hooded black robe, her face a mass of wrinkles about a long mole-covered nose; her longevity ritual kept her alive but not her looks. An expert in Faerie Magic, taught by Orphedra, and perhaps its only practitioner outside House Merinita; malicious to the point of evil.

characters.name: Orphedra

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Merinita and the covenant's link to the forest fae. Apprenticed at Irencillia a hundred and twenty years ago, she found it stifling and sought the primeval dark instead. Stick-thin, hair in a tight bun, angular, with unnaturally smooth skin and an air that makes the covenfolk's skin crawl. She revels in Faerie Magic, which she taught Schadrit, leans to the dark fae, works in illusion, cold, darkness and fear, cast the covenant's Shrouded Glen, and has a deal with the local bockmen to patrol its surroundings.

characters.name: Jiphella

characters.summary: Master of House Ex Miscellanea and master of Mentem, Schadrit's own daughter, conceived under a dark faerie charm long after her mother's longevity ritual, trained by her and wholly cowed by her. Immense and bloated, with lank greasy grey hair and a sickly orange left eye with a blood-red iris that bewitches with a glance; most of the covenfolk are under her spell and worship her. She was Dankmar's only delegate at the Tribunal of 1214, where she denied any part in St Georgen's fall.

characters.name: Larinda

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Ex Miscellanea, Jiphella's daughter and filia, conceived under the same charm. Pretty and sunny despite a cruel mother and a domineering grandmother, whom she obeys out of family duty. Her affinities are for the natural world, Animal, Herbam, Aquam and Auram, and she is becoming an expert brewer of potions. The rest of her traits are lost in the source.

characters.summary: Master of House Jerbiton, a friendly, effusive polymath: scholar, fighter, hunter, musician and poet, mostly without recourse to magic, though he knows many useful spells.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Tremere and devious co-founder of Waddenzee, an Englishman trained at Blackthorn in Stonehenge. Scrupulously honest with Quaesitores, whom he secretly longs to join, and arrogant to everyone else, he lies, cheats and steals whenever it serves. Well groomed, looking in his late thirties, dressed to show his wealth; a Mentem specialist, above all Rego Mentem, who leans heavily on Aura of Rightful Authority.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Tytalus, co-founder of Waddenzee and its most committed pirate: a black-haired Dane from Ribe, dashing, charming and extroverted, with a swollen opinion of himself, who looks far younger than he is thanks to illusions and a good longevity ritual. A generalist favouring Aquam and Auram, he fights beside his men with a magical sword; his familiar is Aegir, a long-tailed skua. His younger cousin Estrid Danesson of Oculus Septentrionalis is his bitter enemy.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Flambeau, son of a German altgraf whose family believes him dead; he keeps a nobleman's habits. Very tall and stocky, always in black, and since a Twilight his clothes fall to pieces when he casts too much. A short-tempered expert in Perdo who kills troublesome mundanes with Perdo Corpus; he has lately taken up necromancy, using the pirates' victims and the Pirates' Graveyards.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Criamon, a quiet, naive Muslim, filius of Hassan El-Megrayhi of Fengheld, who fell in with the pirates by chance. His astrology helps plan their raids. He dresses in stolen cream and blue silks and walks with a limp.

characters.name: Aethelbald
characters.summary: A deputy of the magi who claims to be the Saxon heir to the English crown.

characters.name: Bjorn Ironside
characters.summary: Ship's master of the Nebelkönigin, Waddenzee's stolen flagship.

characters.name: Calum

characters.name: Aelfhere
characters.summary:
A Frisian shipwright of near-magical skill who keeps the covenant's five ships at sea.

Secrets
He secretly corresponds with Marcus Navicularius of Oculus Septentrionalis.

characters.summary: Master of House Jerbiton, of the Apple Gild, and disceptator of Oculus Septentrionalis as its oldest remaining member. Corpulent, sociable and splendidly dressed, probably Lübeck's richest merchant and among the richest commoners in Germany, a respected administrator and diplomat who was apprenticed in Normandy and joined soon after the founding; he means his family to become a dynasty leading the covenant. A Mentem master who uses high-magnitude Mentem for subtlety, never force. His townhouse on the Holstenstrasse has shop and offices below, library and scriptorium above, then meeting rooms, dining hall and guest chambers, then the family's quarters, with three labs at the top for himself, Brunhilda and Gunhilda.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Ex Miscellanea and of the Apple Gild, a recent recruit and the second Scandinavian wizard the covenant has taken in. A man of Ribe who joined the Order late as a hedge wizard of sailing and weather, a flamboyant rogue whose sanctum and lab are aboard his ship; he gathers the covenant's vis around the Baltic and is married to Gunhilda. He is the younger cousin and bitter enemy of Eric Ribecus of Waddenzee; they have fought at sea, though no Wizard's War has been declared.

characters.name: Marcus Navicularius

characters.summary:
Master of House Verditius and of the Apple Gild, Lübeck's foremost shipwright: large and stern, with iron-grey hair and beard, owner of a shipyard that is also his workshop and lab, staffed by skilled craftsmen. A Terram master whose enchanting suits very large things such as ships and cannot work on anything smaller than a sword; he sells magical ships to covenants for vis and lost the Nebelkönigin to Waddenzee. He is designing the Baltic cog the Hanse will adopt.

Secrets
He secretly corresponds with Aelfhere, Waddenzee's shipwright.

characters.name: Imanitos Mendax

description.biography: Equipment: fashionable fine clothes and costly jewellery; Encumbrance 0 (0). Twilight Scars: a forked tongue he keeps hidden, a voice people want to hear, and a faint smell of funeral incense. His Affinity with Finesse came from a Twilight, and his Compulsion is lying. He means to make his serpent-and-ruby ring his talisman. His longevity ritual gives only +2, but his apparent age rises only on an aging roll of 7 or more.

characters.summary:
Master of House Jerbiton, lately so by the approval of three Fengheld magi, Apple Gild trained, Gauntleted at twenty-two after an apprenticeship at Doissetep in Provence. Tall, lean and handsome, black-haired and blue-eyed, in fashionable blue or black, with a serpent-and-ruby ring he means for his talisman; a vanity longevity ritual keeps him looking thirty-nine. He poses as owner of the upmarket tavern Goldenes Kalb, above which a discreet brothel for rich clients is helped along by wine that heightens lust, and his third trade is the blackmail and extortion of citizens and magi. His focus is Mentem, with competent Imaginem for disguises; his Twilight has left him a hidden forked tongue, a compelling voice and a faint smell of funerary incense. His covenant-mates find him useful despite his morals; his sanctum on the top floors of his townhouse is secret and magically guarded.

Secrets
He sells Oculus Septentrionalis's ship movements to Eric Ribecus of Waddenzee for a share of the plunder. Optionally a diabolist of a hidden dark Jerbiton lineage, servant of the demon Radegast, corrupting Lübeck's notables through the Goldenes Kalb and posing as Radegast's prophet to the Mecklenburgs; he might swap the covenant's magestones for tainted copies.

characters.name: Carolus

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Jerbiton and of the Apple Gild, well meaning and scatterbrained, who poses as an eccentric scholar tutoring the citizens. A naive visit to Crintera to mend relations went wrong when Caprea of Bjornaer, a guest there, blinded his raven familiar as a spy; the real spy was Kolkrabus, Murion's familiar.

characters.name: Boris of Novgorod

characters.summary: Journeyman Redcap of House Mercere, not of the Apple Gild, a well-travelled, shrew-like Russian posing as an itinerant merchant who serves the northern Rhine and Novgorod. He owns the new Novgorod Inn at the north end of town, popular with Redcaps and Russian merchants, and hopes for Master rank within a couple of years so that it may become a Mercer House. He sells trinkets, trades books, items and vis, and gets Novgorod vis cheaply.

characters.name: Brunhilda
characters.summary: Henri's Swedish wife of more than thirty years, a seeress in the Norse manner who sends her spirit out in animal form while in trance. Not Gifted enough for the Order but treated as an equal by the magi; she runs the covenant's daily affairs more than Henri does, and her divination guides his luck in trade.

characters.name: Matilda
characters.summary: Gunhilda's elder, un-Gifted sister, autocrat of the covenant and Henri's housekeeper.

characters.name: Stentorius

characters.summary: Archmage of House Tremere, leader of the Oak Gild, authoritarian princeps of Fengheld and Tremere exarch of the Rhine, holding about three-fifths of the Tribunal's Tremere sigils, his filius's and the two Tremere of Triamore among them, while Severicus of Roznov holds the rest. Large and ageing well nearly a century past his Gauntlet, with a bushy iron-grey beard to his chest and a craggy nose; a famed master of Rego, able with most Forms, in showy deep-crimson robes covered in the symbols of Rego, the Forms and his House. His familiar of more than fifty years is Oswald, a hugely arrogant large grey cat in a jewelled gold pendant holding several uses of Aura of Rightful Authority among other effects, who believes he rules Fengheld if not the Tribunal; Murion's raven Kolkrabus taunts him at Durenmar for usurping her place at the head of the Oak Gild.

characters.name: Horst

characters.summary: Master of House Mercere, an un-Gifted Redcap, senior Redcap of the Rhine Tribunal and master of Fengheld's Mercer House, where many Redcaps rest between journeys. A famous and prolific author of high-quality books on a huge range of mundane subjects and on Magic Theory, the backbone of most Rhine apprenticeships; corpulent, with a near-encyclopaedic memory consulted at Tribunal on obscure points of Hermetic law. Wholly apolitical, so his knowledge of the Order's business is of no political use to Fengheld. He wrote the visitor's account of Durenmar.

characters.name: Eule

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer with the honorary rank of Quaesitor from House Guernicus, retired from official duty; for many years she was the Rhine's only senior Quaesitor. Owl heartbeast, and with Caecilius of Durenmar and Schadrit of Dankmar one of the oldest magi in the Tribunal. Magi still come to her for her celebrated advice.

Secrets
Only her filius Günther Lupus suspects that she has passed into Final Twilight: she has not taken human shape for years and has not spoken for longer. Her wisdom is a fraud. An item hidden in the floor of her audience room casts a low-level, very high Penetration Perdo Mentem effect that calms the mind and strips emotion, Günther translates her hoots with a few leading prompts, and the calmed petitioners find their own answers and thank Eule.

characters.name: Peter von Würzburg

characters.summary: Master of House Verditius, a celebrated vintner and grape-grower within the Order and among the nobles of southern Saxony and Thuringia. Minor enchanted items let the vines on Fengheld's south slope thrive this far north, and he turns special varieties into wines that are Charged Items; his squirrel familiar is as industrious as he is, and the two are seen tying vines, testing the sweetness and fertilising. Usually the first magus a visitor meets, out among the grapes; he oversees the head vintner, the orchard keeper and the farm foreman.

characters.name: Dorana

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, the leading maga in the Rhine of the lineage of Irmele filia Trianoma. Decades as a peregrinator before she settled at Fengheld taught her nearly every covenant and many magi of the Tribunal in detail; she argues for reason and peace in Fengheld's dealings and usually wins. She detests her Prima, Murion, pressing Stentorius to contest the Oak Gild and her close ally Occultes of Durenmar to contest the Primacy. A weather specialist, she manages the sun, rain and visitor-deterring fog that Fengheld's farms and privacy depend on; her latest apprentice Felecia has just passed her Gauntlet and gone travelling.

Magus of House Bjornaer (rank not given), Eule's filius, wolf heartbeast. He hunts oath-breakers with Indulius and attends his ancient parens.

Secrets
He is the author of the Eule fraud, keeping up the myth of her wisdom with a hidden Perdo Mentem item and his own translation of her hoots.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Criamon whose philosophy matches the Hawthorn Gild. Born feral, he had a powerful vital spirit his master saw fade as he learned speech and human ways, and he now means to return himself, and others whether they consent or not, to that primal state, holding that enlightenment demands casting off the mundane. His magic releases suppressed emotion and behaviour, and a Warped Magic flaw gives his face a savage cast when he casts; a puckish troublemaker who loves humbling self-important mundanes.

Raised by a dryad, he understands faeries far better than people; his skin is faintly green and his bronze hair stirs in a wind nobody else feels.

characters.summary:
Maga of House Bjornaer (rank not given), filia of Urgen, Archmage of Crintera, and sole inhabitant of the Lusatia chapter, an idyllic house on a bend of the Spree in the March of Lusatia only ten miles from the agreed Novgorod border, whose founding caused the latest boundary dispute between the two Tribunals. Bear heartbeast, in which she spends most of her time, hibernating all winter; a poor member, accused by Fengheld at Tribunal more than once of neglecting her duties, but never punished hard for fear of her aggressive, powerful parens.

Secrets
She and Urgen are the two living magi of a hidden lineage of bear-heartbeast Bjornaer descending from the Founder herself; they harvest the Bears' Cave in the northern Harz.

Master of House Criamon and leader of Heorot, whose magi serve the Ash Gild's chief interest.

He is consumed by the trolls of Zealand, which he holds to be the degenerate descendants of old gods, and his study of them has cost the covenant fourteen grogs and him his left arm. He carries on regardless.

characters.summary:
Journeyman of House Jerbiton, formerly of Oculus Septentrionalis, and Heorot's historian.

A necromancer by method, he raises the ghosts of the dead and questions them about the past. It frustrates him that he has not yet found the remains of Hrothgar or of Beowulf, on whose ground the covenant is said to stand.

characters.summary:
Journeyman of House Bonisagus at Heorot, who means to meet a Norse wizard and learn that magic for the Order.

His parens Occultes is famous and his mentor, the Archmage Philippus Niger of Durenmar, has impressed on him how urgently the Order needs those secrets revealed. Yet a deep dread of the wilderness has so far kept him from setting foot in pagan Scandinavia.

characters.name: Urgen

characters.summary:
Archmagus of House Bjornaer, Senior Elder in the Seat of the Bear, leader of the Hawthorn Gild and Primus of the House from 1165 to 1203, through the Danish invasion. His heartbeast is a bear.

He is the most influential of the Wilderists, holding that the Order must check the swelling mundane population and that Bjornaer must enter Hermetic politics to do so. Twice in fifty years he has torn a powerful magus apart in Wizard War, and his age and his victories earn him respect; support for him grows the longer the occupation of Rügen lasts.

characters.name: Falke

description.biography: Prima of House Bjornaer, Famous since she took the post; her heartbeast is a silver-grey falcon. Equipment: her talisman, a silver anklet set with crystal and amber (attuned +5 to water effects, +3 Corpus), which turns into a leg-band when she changes shape and can read a person's motives; Encumbrance 0 (0). Twilight Scar: her feet are always wet and leave puddles.

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer, Linden Gild trained, and its Prima in the Seat of the Wolf since 1203. Her heartbeast is a silver-grey falcon with white-banded wings; she looks about 45 and passed her Gauntlet at 23.

Raised at Fengheld, she rose to prominence with an impassioned plea at the Tribunal of 1194 to let Crintera resist the Danes. She leans Harmonist without declaring it and governs by patience and seclusion, working to win back the trust of the Quaesitors and the Order. She has just become a Master and taken her first apprentice, and each spring casts the ritual at Arkona that thaws the Baltic.

Her magic centres on bodies of water, Aquam above all, and a Twilight scar keeps her feet always wet, leaving a puddle wherever she stands still. She is small and lithe, plain but commanding, with silky uniform grey hair, simply dressed and always barefoot to show her talisman, a silver anklet patterned in watery crystal and amber. Not suited to play as a player character.

characters.name: Jon Arnsson

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer and protector of Crintera in the Seat of the Stag since the Gathering of 1167, a year before the invasion. His heartbeast is a lion.

A devout Christian who regards Valdemar's Church-backed conquest as righteous, yet fiercely loyal to Crintera, he is a man of divided and conflicted loyalties whose theology any other Christian would call heresy. Gentle and hating violence, he accepts its necessity and, as protector, joins Wizard's Marches against Bjornaer when he can. The second eldest after Urgen, he is a fervent Harmonist.

characters.name: Phyllia

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer in the Seat of the Eagle, who keeps the council informed about the Order. Her heartbeast is a polecat.

She travels widely and has contacts across the Tribunal and beyond, but is a notorious gossip, quite unable to keep a secret. A Harmonist.

characters.name: Ardea

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer and leader of its rituals in the Seat of the Swan. Her heartbeast is a heron.

Quiet and contemplative, a famous seer and diviner with a hunger for magical knowledge worthy of a Bonisagus, she keeps her political opinions to herself because her word carries such weight, and sides with neither faction. She stages the re-enactments of old legends at the Gathering.

characters.name: Istvan Padas

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Master of House Bjornaer in the Seat of the Horse, which keeps track of Crintera's magi and of every Bjornaer. His heartbeast is a magnificent stallion.

The youngest and most wilful Elder, a man of action, he descends from a line of horse-shaped Bjornaer taken into the House from the invading Magyars in the Order's early days. A Wilderist, strongly backed by his lover Zora, priestess of Hertha. His predecessor in the Seat died trying to climb the Königstuhl.

characters.name: Caprea

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.
